## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-26 — Web sessions use short-lived tokens that renew in the background (AUTH-G011, AUTH-G015)

- **Decision (user):** keep bearer tokens, make them short-lived and renew them silently. Total session length is unchanged: 24 h, or 30 days with a trusted device.
- **Server.**
  - Web and workspace tokens last 15 min and carry `sat`/`sma` (session start and maximum age).
  - `POST /api/auth/web/renew` (`renewWebSession.ts`, `tokenRotation.ts`) accepts any validly signed web token within `sat + sma` and rotates it to a new `jti`. The successor is written first, then a compare-and-set supersedes the old token and drops the cached verdicts.
  - Presenting a superseded token within 60 s returns the same successor. Presenting it later revokes the whole session (`session_revoked`). Non-web tokens are refused.
  - Migration 1369 adds `auth_tokens.superseded_by`. Migration 1370 extends rows already issued, so the expired-credential sweep can't remove a sleeping device's current token.
- **Clients.**
  - The website (`frontend/src/lib/auth/tokenRenewal.ts`) renews at 75 % of a token's life and again on focus. One tab renews at a time and the others adopt the new token.
  - A 401 triggers one renewal and one retry; a brain-stream 401 renews in the background.
  - The agent-runtime CLI renews its stored web token, and qa-e2e signs in once per worker.
- **Checks.** Three Opus reviews ran. Fixed findings:
  - the 1 h grace window that signed out sleeping laptops;
  - workspace tokens could be renewed into web tokens;
  - pre-deploy rows could be swept;
  - the tab-lock race;
  - an embed loop;
  - swallowed errors.
  - The api, frontend, agent-runtime and qa-e2e typechecks are clean, and the targeted tests pass (renewal 15/15). The migration guards pass. Row growth is tracked as `AUTH-G021`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-26 — The Visualizer no longer crashes VS Code on large repos and opens on the last review (AE-G063, AE-G062; VSIX 2026.11.225)

- **Crash (AE-G063).** On hired.video (6315 files) a finished load sent 123,843 edges and 24,674 per-edge `partition-violation` findings from the worker to the host, into `lastSeen` and on to the webview. The host stalled for up to 10 s, then crashed.
  - `clients/vscode/src/knowledge/graphBudget.ts` now bounds graphs that are drawn: the view load, live pushes and pack roots, each marked `view: true`.
    - Only edges between kept nodes survive. Parallel edges merge into one weighted edge, capped at 12,000, structural kinds first.
    - Violations are grouped per area pair, keeping up to 3 real findings each with true counts.
    - A count-based payload budget applies.
  - Whole-graph consumers keep every edge: domain proposals, pack cards, pack indexing and pack merge.
  - True totals stay in `stats`. Bound reasons appear in the trace and in Copy diagnostics.
- **First load (AE-G062).**
  - A run-gated host waits up to 5 s for `lastSeen`, then chooses the root in this order: selected, painted, newest.
  - On a miss it paints the stored review read-only, and Run still starts live updates. "Ready to run" shows only when nothing is stored. A late `lastSeen` never overrides a root the user picked.
  - `lastSeen` is written in slices that yield the thread, with its size and any oversize skip logged.
- **Diagnostics and logging.**
  - A Copy diagnostics button shows in every state. The Panels button hides when there is no graph.
  - Every load step goes to the Output channel and to a rolling log capped at 256 KB (`knowledge-log/` in global storage). Previously silent catches now report.
- **Checks.**
  - Opus review: two high findings fixed (whole-graph consumers had been bounded; grouped findings broke `[from, to]` consumers).
  - 96 targeted tests pass, and the VS Code typecheck is clean.
  - VSIX 2026.11.225 is installed, with the bounding, logging, wait and diagnostics code confirmed in the bundle.
  - Seven older failing view tests are tracked separately as `AE-G064`.

<details><summary>Spec as built</summary>

### Part C — Code and picture, one location (redesign, 2026-11-25)

The design is the working prototype `.builderforce/design/code-visualizer.html` (source `code-visualizer.src.html`; inventory `.builderforce/design/code-visualizer-v2/FEATURE-INVENTORY.md`). The rule it adds: **one location** (system › component › class › method › line), **code on the left, the picture on the right**, and moving in either pane moves both. Everything below plugs into seams that exist; nothing is a second copy of a built feature. Reviewed by Opus 2026-11-25 against the code; the corrections are folded in. Paths are relative to `packages/knowledge-graph-view/src/`.

**C1. The code pane is docked, always.** `stage/overlay/CodeDock.tsx` is docked on the LEFT at every band when the host has `readSource` and the box is at least `SPLIT_MIN_PX` wide. "Docked" and "reading" are two states: today `showCode = codeOpen || !!zoom.code` (`stage/overlay/useStageWiring.tsx`) also turns on `needRecords` (the records walk, a fixed perf regression), `CallBadges`, the hover tint, the fade, the reading ring and the `StatusStrip`. Those stay gated on *reading* (a file or the code band). Above the code band the docked pane shows an **outline of the current level built from the graph's own nodes** (members with their shape glyph, test and anti-pattern marks; no records walk); a click there moves the picture. Below `SPLIT_MIN_PX` the floating pane (`!code.split`, `stage/host/StageHost.tsx`) becomes a Code | Picture switch of the same location. A host without `readSource` (the web) shows the outline only. Hide state: `usePanelVisibility` gains a `code` slot (per viewer, localStorage, like `left|bottom|right`), threaded from `KnowledgeGraphView.tsx` to `StageHost`. The dock wiring moves out of `useStageWiring.tsx` (379 lines) into `stage/overlay/useCodeDock.ts`; no touched file ends over ~400 lines.

**C2. Code lens and gutter.** `stage/drill/CodeLayer.tsx` / `codeText.ts`: lenses sit on class and method lines (`Lens.kind`). `LensAction` gains `out` (on the symbol whose level you are inside), `simulate` (shown as "No test · Simulate" when its file/station has no test reaching it; opens the path simulator, `simulateMode`, on the path through it), `restructure` (with the anti-pattern's name, when a finding of a kind in `PROPOSERS` sits on its file). Lens actions are ROWS of a table (`stage/drill/lensActions.ts`), not branches in `LensLine`. The gutter shows the symbol's shape glyph (`ShapeGlyph`, `surface/LegendGlyph.tsx`; registry `shapes.ts`) on its first line, a warning glyph instead when it carries an anti-pattern. Facts are computed once, not passed as booleans: `surface/symbolFacts.ts` → `symbolFacts(graph, stations) → { antiPatternOf(ref): { kind, findingId } | null; untested(ref): boolean }` (untested = its file's station has no test reach — coverage is per station).

**C3. The selection card.** `surface/transit/cardModel.ts` / `StationCard.tsx` / `stage/overlay/StageCard.tsx` / `SymbolCard.tsx`: facts show risk, test reach and the anti-pattern name; actions are Go inside, Callers and Simulate, with Restructure in place of Simulate when the selection carries a restructurable anti-pattern. Actions are icon + short label from ONE glyph module: `cameraGlyph` (private in `surface/CameraBar.tsx`) moves to `surface/ui/glyphs.tsx` with the action glyphs beside it, and CameraBar imports it. A card action whose callback is absent is not shown.

**C4. One 3D / Flat switch.** One switch beside the view switcher (`surface/CameraBar.tsx`) for every stage camera (ids: `transit`, `system`, `graph`, `map`, `3d`, `heat`, `style`, `features`, `sequence`). Flat = tilt 0 on ground placements, the `3d` orbit pitched straight down; 3D = the placement's resting tilt. Tilt today is local state in `stage/Stage.tsx` (`setDepth`) driven by `stage/rig/DepthControl.tsx` (its only caller, `Stage.tsx:277`), whose `onTilt` also runs `setTowers(d>0)` — on `transit` "3D" means towers + role paint (`showsTowers`). The switch owns that: the tilt is lifted to the host, the switch sets `surface.towers` on `transit`, the Map-only `Segmented [{3d},{2d}]` in `StageHost.tsx` and `DepthControl.tsx` are deleted, and `depthLabel` (the canvas label fallback) is kept. Flat on a ground placement keeps drag = pan; the `3d` orbit in Flat rotates yaw only. Remembered per viewer.

**C5. Compare.** A comparison is one of three sources, held by ONE state (`useCompare` + `surface/CompareBar.tsx`; the existing `revision` toggles — `FixBeforeAfter`, `ServerTab`, `ResolvePanel`, evidence `side` — drive it; `useSurface` keeps the baseline for its delta):
- **baseline / snapshot** (`source.baseline()` async, `source.snapshot`): two graphs; the bar honours `KnowledgeBaseline.comparable === false` (shows its `reasons`, offers no Before).
- **restructure**: two graphs, today and `proposeRestructure` (C6).
- **commit** (a picked commit, `surface/TimeSlider.tsx`): NOT a second graph — no host can build the graph at a commit (`Commit` has `refs` only). It is a changed set over today's graph; history play steps the changed set commit by commit.

For the two-graph sources, `compute/compare/unionGraph.ts` builds ONE union graph (before ∪ after, keyed by ref) and ONE MarkSet over it (slots stay put, so the existing placement tween moves marks between sides). Before and After are two placements of the union: a slot absent on a side has scale 0, anchored at its `bornFrom` mark (the way B1a rule 4 grows hidden slots out of their parent, `stage/marks/MarkLayer.ts:186`), so a new mark grows out of its origin and a removed one merges back. `compute/compare/diffGraphs.ts` → `{ added, removed, changed: ref[]; edgesAdded, edgesRemoved }` (changed = a node in both whose badges, sourceHash or edge set differ). Diff and changed are **paint**, not MarkSet inputs (the commit's refs never rebuild the MarkSet — that broke B1a rule 1): `paintMarks` overrides `tone` with a diff tone (added / changed / removed); no new instanced attribute (the 4-slot budget, `stage/marks/shader.ts:41`). Tokens: `--kg-diff-added`, `--kg-diff-removed` in `tokens.css` (both themes) AND `scene/themeTokens.ts` `KG_TOKENS` (`TONE_ORDER` derives from it); "changed" reuses `--kg-changed`. `StageHost.tsx`'s `changed: NO_CHANGES` goes. The compare bar holds the source, Before | After, play, and close. The code pane marks added / removed lines of the selected file on the chosen side (C8).

**C6. Restructure proposals.** `compute/compare/restructure.ts` (worker-safe, no labels): `PROPOSERS: Record<kind, Proposer>`, `Proposer = (graph, finding, symbols: SymbolRecord[]) → { after: KnowledgeGraph; bornFrom: Map<ref, ref> } | null`; a kind has a Restructure action iff it is in `PROPOSERS` (and, for kinds that need them, once its file's symbols are loaded via `symbolsOf` — disabled until then).
- `partition-violation`: the edge that climbs a layer is removed and routed through the layer between, or dropped when there is none.
- `god-module`: the finding names the FILE; its members and their internal `calls`/`uses` edges come from `SymbolRecord.relations`. Members are split into cohesive groups (connected components of internal edges; a group of one joins its strongest neighbour); each group becomes a new module node `bornFrom` the file, edges re-pointed. It agrees with the codemod row (`surface/codemods.ts`, `god-module → splitByCommand`) on what moves.
Restructure is the picture of the Patterns drawer's anti-pattern card (`AntiPatternPreview`): "See it restructured" opens the compare; it is not a second preview. Proposals are never written; Apply goes to the existing fix flow.

**C7. Flow and Sequence at every level.** Flow becomes a stage placement (`compute/tasks/placement/flow.ts`) at system, component and class depth: the level's shapes on rising decks along the main path, which is `sequenceFlow.ts`'s entry walk (reused, not a second walker), with branch ends. Sequence joins the view switcher (`surface/cameras.tsx`, no `switcher: false`) where `hasLines`; it draws the selected line, or the first line when none is selected; PathStrip's Enlarge selects it. At code depth the view switcher replaces the code band's Flow/Sequence segmented control (`StageHost.tsx`, `codeLayout` in `useStageWiring.tsx`): Flow keeps the call arcs, Sequence draws the method's calls as raised bars on the stage — `PlacementRequest` gains `method?: ref` — and `stage/overlay/CodeSequence.tsx` is deleted with its test.

**C8. Source at a revision.** `KnowledgeGraphSource.readSourceAt?(rootId, path, rev, range): Promise<SourceText | null>`, `rev` a commit sha; `KnowledgeBaseline` / `KnowledgeSnapshot` gain `rev?: string` (the sha they were taken at) so Before can read its side. VS Code implements it with `git show <rev>:<path>` inside the root, validated like `readSource`: `clients/vscode/src/knowledge/knowledgeProtocol.ts`, `knowledgeBridge.ts`, `sourcePort.ts`, and the webview `hostKnowledgeGraphSource.ts`. Cross-package contract ⇒ Opus review. Absent ⇒ the pane shows today's file and says the old one is not available.

**C9. Strings.** Every new string is a `labels/` default and a `knowledgeGraph.*` key in all five `frontend/src/i18n/messages/*.json` catalogs with real translations.

**Done checks.**
- The harness (`npm run harness`) shows: the code pane docked left at system, class and method band; lenses on class and method lines with the C2 actions; Flat and 3D on `transit`, `graph`, `3d`, Flow and `sequence`; the god-module restructure Before → After with marks moving and new modules growing out of the file; a picked commit tinting the changed marks without a MarkSet rebuild; both themes; 360 px wide.
- Unit tests: `diffGraphs`, `unionGraph`, both proposers, `symbolFacts`, the lens actions per symbol, the card actions per selection, the paint diff override, the Flow placement at three depths.
- `rg "NO_CHANGES|DepthControl|CodeSequence" src` → 0; no touched file over ~400 lines.

</details>

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-25 — VSIX "Bad Image" on Windows; Knowledge Visualizer drill reset and flash (VSIX 2026.11.219)

- **Native addon per platform.** The CI universal VSIX (built on ubuntu) shipped the Linux `bfi_node` addon as `out/bfi_node.node`, which Windows refused to load with a "Bad Image 0xc000012f" dialog. Every vendored addon now ships under its own tag (`bfi_node.<platform>-<arch>.node`). The host loads only the file for its own platform, through `addonFileName` from `@seanhogg/bfi-node`; a platform with no addon runs the wasm. `scripts/lib/nativeAddonFormat.mjs` checks each addon's binary format and CPU architecture (PE, ELF, Mach-O, fat) at build and vendor time, and is registered as `check:native-addon-format`. `vsce-platform.mjs` passes `BFI_NATIVE_TARGET`, so a single-platform package ships only its own addon.
- **Visualizer: Classes no longer resets to Systems.**
  - **One rebuild at a time.** The overlapping 30-second whole-graph re-reads now share one settle-based throttle that never overlaps itself: `@builderforce/knowledge-client/settledThrottle`, with `onError` and `SKIPPED`. The view's growth re-read (`useGrowthReread`) and the host's live refresh both use it. They are coordinated through `rootLoads.ts`, so only one build per root runs. A refresh skipped during a view load re-runs when that load ends.
  - **The drill follows its files.** A drilled level whose community station was renumbered moves to the station that now holds most of its files (`reanchorDrill`). Symbol loads track file refs, and the nest entries at every level are rebuilt from layout data of a single generation (`deriveNestEntries`, `useNestEntries`, `useNestBasis`).
  - **No flash.** `useHeldFrame` keeps the last ready frame on screen during a same-view rebuild, keyed by `useDrillIdentity`, and the stage stays mounted.
- Covered by: nativeAddonFormat 5 tests, the vendor check, the source-package-graph guard; settledThrottle 10; knowledge-graph-view 49 files / 310 tests; vscode knowledgeLive, graphWorker, hostBfi and vsce-platform (77 tests); clean typecheck for vscode (including webview, harness and test-integration), knowledge-client and knowledge-graph-view.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-25 — Studio media isolation and recovery, and the project link on offline creation (WC-G008 in part, WC-G010)

- **Media is scoped to the workspace.** `mediaUploadQueue` takes `activeTenantId` and only uploads media whose destination is that workspace. It re-checks before the request and before it writes the result, and `uploadCanvasFile(file, { tenantId })` throws `tenant_switched` when the stored tenant differs. The blob store counts usage per workspace partition (`put(id, blob, { partition })`; rows from before partitions count against every partition).
- **One size rule.** `ASSET_MAX_BYTES` (10 MiB) and `ASSET_MAX_VIDEO_BYTES` (100 MiB) are exported from brain-embedded and are the blob store's caps. The API's `tenantAssetStore.ts` keeps its own copy of the two numbers (api does not depend on brain-embedded); a comment names the pair.
- **Failures are visible and recoverable.** A failed upload waits `30 s × 2^(n-1)` up to 30 min (`nextAttemptAt`, never synced). After five attempts it is `failed`; `BoardMediaIssues` lists failed and backing-off items with a Retry, and drop/paste intake tells the person when a file is too large or the device is full (`studio.media.*`, five locales).
- **Dropped and pasted media goes through the blob store.** `importCanvasFile` takes `{ mediaSink }`; images, meshes and DXF files carry `media:<id>`, never a data URL. DOCX figures now upload in parallel.
- **Project link survives offline creation.** `createLocalCreationSession('', undefined, project)` seeds a project card (`projectCardObject`, `project:<id>`) that syncs as an ordinary object; the API already checks it (`validateResourceAccess`: tenant, segment). The server-first branch and the `projectTieDropped` message are gone from `SessionList.tsx`, and the device list matches boards to the project from their cards (`projectTiesByBoard`, one scan).
- **Pull reads respect board membership.** `SyncPullStore` takes the reader; Canvas rows come back only for boards the caller may read (`readableBoardIdsSql`).
- Covered by: frontend `localFirst` and canvas suites (428 tests), `SessionList` 5, `ImportCanvasFile` 28 with the project card tests; API `SyncRepository` and `handleSyncPull` 34 (plus 1 new handler test). Typechecks: api clean; frontend and brain-embedded show only errors in `codeScanner.ts` and `code-shield/signatures.ts`, which this change does not touch.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-25: A sub-agent's unchecked "could not / does not exist" claims now reach the owner flagged

- **The gap.** A child reported that `agent-runtime/` "has no run-policy, so the verify phase could not be added". That was half wrong: `agent-loop.ts` holds a live `RunPolicyState`, so only the memory write was out of reach. The owner relayed the claim as fact.
- **Fix.** `parseSubagentReport` (`packages/agent-loop/src/subagent.ts`) returns `unverifiedClaims`. These are named-negative or impossibility sentences, found by the data-driven `NEGATIVE_CLAIMS` patterns.
  - **What it skips:** code fences, Verified/Changed/Checked result lines, fixed-bug descriptions, compiler or runtime error text, and sentences already listed as open issues.
  - **Limits:** the scan is linear and bounded at 8,000 chars, with lines over 1,000 chars skipped. It keeps 5 claims, then adds "…and N more".
  - **Rendering:** the shared `ownerSections()` in `packages/agent-tools/src/live-subagent-tools.ts` renders open issues and claims. It adds the line "Unverified claims — check each with one search before relaying or acting on it".
  - **Surfaces:** VS Code (`childRunSpawner.ts`), cloud (`cloudChildRuns.ts`) and on-prem (`agent-runtime/src/agents/subagent-announce.ts` `ownerSectionsOf`).
  - **Budget:** each surface counts the sections inside one report budget (`ownerSectionsChars`).
- **The other half of that report** was already fixed: `changedFiles` is derived from the write tool calls in the trace, not from what the child says it changed.
- Covered by `regression:` tests in `packages/agent-loop/src/subagent.test.ts` and `packages/agent-run/test/subagents/subagent.test.ts`, plus `childReportPacket.test.ts` and `subagent-announce.owner-sections.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-24: PRD 50: finished sections archived on consolidation

**PRD 50 — one pipeline above the kernel**

### Initial implementation review (2026-11-23)

The [pipeline map](./docs/specs/make.md#design--agent-pipeline-map) now describes the inspected checkout. Sections 0–7 below retain the original slice contract and historical rationale; they must not be read as current-state findings. This review supersedes stale file names and implementation assumptions in those sections.

| Contract | Inspected status | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required entryPoint (§2.1) | Required on Brain request; runPrepared has no default; openRun rejects a missing policy label | RunEntryPoint aliases shared EntryPoint; Brain conformance execution fails on the existing tool-dispatch path (see validation) |
| Participant through panel host (§2.2) | Implemented by participantRun.ts runViaHost → host.start; host labels vscode | Host gate tests pass; participant/host integration needs the built Brain package |
| Factories own policy (§2.3) | openRun composes surface ports for every inspected adapter | Recorded preflight facts and native history ports enter shared factories; no compaction.hook escape hatch remains |
| Shared spawnChild (§2.4) | Implemented by policy/subagents/child.ts; VSIX, durable cloud, in-process on-prem and all four legacy callers reach it | Authenticated host starts and native admission/completion semantics stay surface-owned |
| Sub-agent execution parity | The shared driver routes child tasks through the same stages and enforces root-only spawning. VSIX passes its routing settings to children, and the in-process relay carries its verification policy. | Validate against installed hosts |
| Children pass editor gate | Implemented through startThrough → gated.start | Does not imply a common start lifecycle across all surfaces |
| Kernel unchanged by this review | Entry, spawning, preflight and compaction changes stay above the kernel | Preserve runAgent → runAgentLoop |

Adjacent work has also advanced beyond the baseline: shared routeRun now owns full/quick scoring, Brain openingSections owns editor opening assembly, and deterministic close-out runs through openRun instead of a duplicate direct call from startRun. These do not complete routing configuration parity, cross-surface opening, or continuation consolidation.

#### Implemented child-start contract (§2.4)

The generic contract in §2.4 is now implemented. prepareChildStart validates registered entryPoint, nonempty owner/task/parent identity and integer child depth before host effects. spawnChild<Result> calls the scoped host start without interpreting its native result. The implementation preserves these requirements:

- Carry the parent's EntryPoint explicitly; openRun requires it.
- Define depth as the child depth. New admission requires depth 1. Preparing already admitted payloads accepts historical depth through `MAX_SUBAGENT_DEPTH`.
- Carry the owner's display identity and optional persona/base prompt, so shared subagentSystemPrompt preserves existing child instructions and inherited context.
- Separate background admission from eventual completion. VSIX spawn controls return a handle while observing the host completion promise separately; cloud admission returns a durable handle; on-prem childRunner returns a completed report. The generic start-result port preserves those behaviors. Do not await cloud completion inside a durable start request.
- Keep authorization in each authenticated start port. Shared lineage/depth validation does not replace tenant scoping, session agent allow-lists, or host tool approvals.
- Preserve all legacy callers. spawnSubagentDirect has FOUR production call sites: sessions-spawn-tool.ts, commands-subagents.ts, infra/local-agent-transport.ts and transport/local-adapter.ts. All four now reach shared spawnChild through that compatibility adapter; keep the adapter for gateway/session delivery and agent allow-list authorization. Shared admission enforces root-only spawning.
- The old buildSubagentSystemPrompt name is absent. `buildSubagentSessionPrompt` uses the shared `subagentSystemPrompt` and adds session context.
- openRun is the shared runtime entry; identity, editor journal/delta capture and durable execution creation still belong to host lifecycle ports. Passing openRun alone is not proof that a child passed the same host start as a user.

#### Policy and enforcement corrections

The production composition owner is packages/agent-run/src/openRun.ts. Adapters supply surface ports instead of modules. SurfacePorts.preflight now accepts RecordedModelPreflight data, not a hook. The shared policy/model createModelHook factory constructs the event and verdict, preserving the host plan model and suppressing a second check or repeated notices. Brain preflightRecorded.ts only snapshots cell facts. SurfacePorts.compaction now accepts only CompactionHookOptions. Its history strategy lives in policy/compaction/history.ts: memo reuse, immutable source rows, summary deadline and fallback, one timeout attempt per run, row comparison and saved-token accounting. Brain brainFold.ts supplies storage, native-row conversion, summary transport, activity/diagnostic sinks and recordFold for durable markers; it defines no hook body. The existing compactionSavedTokens API re-exports the shared implementation.

check-one-execution.mjs enforces imports, not the ownership of supplied hook bodies. The inaccurate enforcement comment was removed. The preflight data contract, shared-factory regressions and production-door single-check/no-duplicate-notice regression replace its callback exception. The compaction callback exception is also removed from the type contract; runPrepared.door.test.ts checks history ports and absence of the hook field. The import guard is not claimed to inspect arbitrary callback semantics.

#### Validation and upkeep

Coverage to retain: agent-run test/entry/openRun.test.ts and test/conformance/, Brain crossAdapterConformance.test.ts and runStore/openingSections.test.ts, VSIX participantRun.test.ts, brainRunHost.entryPoint.test.ts and hostStartGate.test.ts, and runtime conformance/crossAdapter.test.ts and onPremSubagents.openRun.test.ts. Existing assertions remain acceptance requirements; this source review is not a test pass.

The initial diff was verified before edits, including runStore/runTypes.ts; none of the prior reports were assumed applied. Added shared spawn coverage (18 cases), shared history strategy coverage (3 cases), durable prompt round-trip coverage, and an on-prem standing-instruction assertion. Existing preflight regressions remain. Repaired malformed newline literals in the participant regression fixture and runSetup turn-context join; typed existing test mocks/callback parameters so agent-run can typecheck.

### 1. What "above the kernel" means

A surface is above the kernel when it does any of these **before** `runAgent`:

1. Creates the chat id or the run id.
2. Runs a start gate (change set, run journal, delta capture).
3. Chooses or labels `entryPoint`.
4. Assembles a system prompt or a transcript.
5. Binds policy modules (`modules:`).
6. Starts a sub-agent by a path that is not the same start as a user chat.

`runAgent` and everything it calls (`composePolicyHooks` as used inside the driver, `openingRows` when the surface did not pass a transcript, `runAgentLoop`, settle) is the kernel. This slice does not edit those bodies except to stop accepting a module override from a surface (section 3).

### 2. Contracts for this slice

#### 2.1 `entryPoint` is required on the Brain request

`BrainRunRequest.entryPoint` becomes required. The wire values stay the existing `EntryPoint` union from `@builderforce/learned-routing` (the same union `RunPolicy.entryPoint` already requires). No new value in this slice.

```ts
/** Telemetry label. Required. Never branched on for behaviour. */
entryPoint: EntryPoint;
```

`runPrepared` assigns `req.entryPoint` with no default:

```ts
entryPoint: req.entryPoint, // was: req.entryPoint ?? 'web'
```

Callers that omit it fail the typecheck. The participant does not become a new caller of `runPrepared`; it stops calling `runBrainLoop` (section 2.2).

Known callers and the label they already pass, or must pass:

| Caller | Label |
|---|---|
| VSIX panel host | `'vscode'` (already) |
| VSIX participant, after 2.2 | `'vscode'` via the panel host |
| Web chat reply / web panel | `'web'` (already, `useBrainPanelController.ts:205`) |
| Canvas | `'canvas'` |
| Cloud tick | `'cloud'` |
| On-prem / channels | `'on-prem'` |

A test that passed `entryPoint: 'web'` to prove the old default is rewritten to pass the label explicitly. No assertion is loosened.

#### 2.2 Participant enters through the panel host start

`runNativeBrain` (`clients/vscode/src/nativeBrainRun.ts`) stops owning a run. It calls the same host start the panel uses (`brainRunHost` / the function that today handles `run.start`), with:

- `entryPoint: 'vscode'`
- the participant's chat id, user turn, model, and stream events as **ports**
- no second journal, no second system-prompt builder, no second tool-confirm wiring

Deleted from the participant path once the host start is the only caller:

| Owned today | Owner after |
|---|---|
| `runId = native:${chatId}:…` and `recovery.recordStarted/Checkpoint/Finished` (`nativeBrainRun.ts:144`, `:255`) | the host's `gateStarts` journal |
| `withRunPreamble` + `buildSystemMessages` (`prompt.ts:16`) | the host preamble (still duplicated with the webview until `buildOpening`; not deleted in this slice) |
| `createNativeRunTool` / `needsConfirm` / `subscribeRun` confirm modal wiring that parallels the host | the host tool port; the participant modal is a `HumanChannel` the host already accepts |

`nativeBrainRun.ts` may remain as a thin adapter (events in, host start out) under ~150 lines. It must not call `runBrainLoop` or `runAgent`.

#### 2.3 Surfaces pass ports, not modules

`RunAgentInput.modules` stays for tests and for the one place that binds engine ports. Production adapters stop passing a replacement hook.

The allowed production shape is a ports object the **existing** factory already accepts:

| Surface | Today | After this slice |
|---|---|---|
| VSIX `runPrepared.ts:90` | replaces `compaction`, `model`, `finish` | calls `createCompactionHook`, `createFinishHook` (and the recorded-model wrapper) **as the module's own factory**, fed Brain ports. The `modules:` key may remain only as `{ compaction: createCompactionHook(brainPorts), finish: createFinishHook(brainPorts), model: recordedModelHook(...) }` — those factories live in `packages/agent-run/src/policy/*`, not in `brain-embedded`. `brainFold.ts` / `brainFinish.ts` become port builders or are deleted if the factory already covers them. |
| Cloud `cloudPolicyModules` | replaces `compaction`, `guards`, `finish` | same factories, cloud ports (`cloudFinishPorts`, `GuardPorts`, gateway summarizer). `withShipGate` stays a port in front of `createGuardsHook`, not a second guards module. |
| Web `agentReplyRun.ts:206` | replaces `compaction` only | `createCompactionHook({ summarize })` from `policy/compaction`. Finish and guards stay the defaults, which already read ports. |
| Canvas, on-prem `onPremAdapter` | no `modules` | unchanged. They already finish through the default hook. |

`composePolicyHooks` keeps the override parameter so a test can still drive one module. A comment at the call states that a production adapter must not pass a hook defined outside `policy/*`.

This slice does **not** move `openLinkedWorkHold` or `specTicketCoverageGate` into the shared finish module. Those are the VSIX-only work-ledger (map section 3, item on work items). They stay bound as finish **ports** the VSIX supplies, so the surface no longer replaces the finish module's logic — it supplies the two predicates the shared finish hook already knows how to call. If the shared finish hook has no such port yet, add a `FinishPorts` field; do not copy the gate bodies.

#### 2.4 `spawnChild` re-enters the same start

One function, in `packages/agent-run/src/policy/subagents/child.ts` (the file that already owns `childPolicy`, `childProvider`, `childResult`):

```ts
export interface SpawnChildRequest {
  parentRunId: string;
  entryPoint: EntryPoint;
  /** Child depth. New admission requires 1. */
  depth: number;
  owner: string;
  task: string;
  role?: string;
  persona?: SubagentPersona;
  basePrompt?: string;
  workItemIds?: readonly string[];
}

export interface ChildStartRequest {
  prompt: string;
  systemPrompt: string;
  entryPoint: EntryPoint;
  lineage: { parentRunId: string; depth: number };
  workItemIds: readonly string[];
}

export interface SpawnChildPorts<Result> {
  /** Authenticated/scoped user-start port; returns its native admission handle OR completed result. */
  openRun(request: ChildStartRequest): Promise<Result>;
}

/** Validate before invoking the port; build standing instructions with subagentSystemPrompt only. */
export function spawnChild<Result>(request: SpawnChildRequest, ports: SpawnChildPorts<Result>): Promise<Result>;
```

Each surface's spawn tool calls `spawnChild` and supplies `openRun` as the start it already uses for a user message:

| Surface | `openRun` port | Deleted spawn path |
|---|---|---|
| VSIX | childRunHost calls spawnChild then the already-gated host start | Separate standing-prompt assembly; existing asynchronous completion observation stays |
| Cloud | spawnChild prepares standing instructions, persisted in CloudChildSpec before durable admission; childBrief appends the tick base prompt | Separate child-prompt policy; durable records and tenant scoping stay |
| On-prem | spawnChild then openRun, childPolicy/childProvider, parent lineage and inherited persona | Missing shared standing instructions; completed childResult stays |
| Legacy sessions | spawnSubagentDirect authorizes then calls spawnChild; gateway agent start reaches the existing session/channel runtime entry | Compatibility adapter retained for all four callers; session prompt adds session-specific context to prepared standing instructions |

The generic result preserves background admission (VSIX/cloud) and completed reports (in-process on-prem). A durable start must persist the shared prompt inputs or prepared opening for its later tick; it must not wait for child completion or discard the shared opening. Keep session-specific delivery and authorization until every legacy caller is migrated. Validate depth and lineage before any start side effects.

Editor children get a change set, a journal start, and delta capture through the gated host port. Other surfaces keep their own authenticated lifecycle ports. `entryPoint` is the parent's, not `'web'`.

### 5. Tests (existing assertions stay)

| Defect | Test |
|---|---|
| Missing `entryPoint` does not become `'web'` | Typecheck, plus a brain-embedded test that constructs a request without the field and expects a compile error (or, if the request is a runtime object, a thrown error — not a silent `'web'`). |
| Participant label | A test that the host start invoked by the participant records `entryPoint: 'vscode'`. |

Run the existing suites unchanged: `packages/agent-run/test/conformance/`, `brain-embedded` cross-adapter conformance, `agent-runtime/src/conformance/crossAdapter.test.ts`, and the files touched. Do not rewrite an assertion to go green.

### 6. Decisions

1. **Stop at `runAgent`.** The user asked to consolidate duplication above `runAgent => runAgentLoop` and then stop. `routeRun`, `planWork`, `evaluateRun`, stall/continuation, and the second on-prem adapter are specified so they are not forgotten, and not implemented in this slice.
2. **`RunPolicy.entryPoint` was already required.** The bug is the Brain request default, not the policy type.
3. **`modules` stays for tests and for factory binding.** Deleting the field would break the conformance suites. The rule is: a hook body lives in `policy/*`; a surface passes ports into that factory.
4. **Work-item gates stay VSIX ports** until `planWork`. Moving their bodies now would start the next slice.
5. **Cloud keeps a durable execution as a port**, not as a policy. `spawnChild` does not know about Durable Objects.

### 7. Acceptance criteria for this slice (not a completion report)

- This file is the slice contract. The pipeline map is the current-state diagram; the Gap Register links both. Keep their implementation status synchronized.
- `entryPoint` has no `'web'` default.
- The participant starts through the panel host.
- Spawn on every surface that has a spawn tool goes through `spawnChild` → the user start.
- Production finish/guards/compaction hook **bodies** are not defined outside `policy/*`.
- No edits under `runAgentLoop`. No deletion of `channelAdapter`, `progressGuard`, `continueChat`, or `useChatSystemPrompt` in this slice.
  *Later slices (re-validated 2026-11-24):* `useChatSystemPrompt.ts` was deleted in `c56ce694e` once shared opening assembly replaced it. `agent-runtime/src/run/channelAdapter.ts` was renamed to `channelRunPorts.ts`; its test file keeps the old name. `progressGuard` and `continueChat` remain. The other five criteria above hold in the current code. The open host failures are tracked in [make.md § PRD 50](./docs/specs/make.md#prd-50--one-pipeline-validation-and-diagnostic-gaps).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-24: PRD 50 executable evidence and diagnostic accuracy

- **MK-50-SELFVAL:** PRD 50 declares runnable acceptance commands with working directories. The shared runtime records completed exits from authorized calls and carries background jobs across ticks. It holds finish while required evidence is missing and records an unverified or failed result at settlement when appropriate.
- **MK-50-DIAG:** Stored diagnostic reads distinguish unavailable captures from observed results and expose snapshot timing and context pressure. Brain diagnostics use observed account provenance, report local work and verified delivery separately, and show when ticket link receipts or trace events are absent from separately loaded history.
- The shared suite passed 871 tests. Focused checks passed in Brain (219), VSIX (41), on-prem (9) and API (15). See [make.md](./docs/specs/make.md#prd-50--one-pipeline-validation-and-diagnostic-gaps) for the detailed verification and the remaining installed-host evidence.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-24: PRD 50 host failures, git_diff scoping, and the participant's lost messages

- **`git_diff` and `git_history` scoping.** These tools now accept workspace-relative paths when a repo is named. Before, a path like `Builderforce.ai/docs/x.md` with `repo: "Builderforce.ai"` matched nothing, and the agent saw an empty diff of its own edit (chat #300, step 4). Every path candidate (`commitPathCandidates`) is passed as a pathspec, so a repo that really contains `app/` keeps `app/page.tsx`. `git_diff` now shows staged and unstaged changes (`diff HEAD`). On a repo with no commits, `runGitTool` falls back to `--cached` plus the plain diff; the fallback requires exit 128 and an anchored `fatal:` line. Each command is one plain git call with no `||`, so on-prem Windows without bash still runs it. See `packages/agent-tools/src/git-tools.ts` and `git-repo-scope.ts`.
- **MK-50-PERSIST: participant messages were never saved.** Turns sent to `@builderforce` in VS Code's native chat lost the person's message from chat history after the participant moved onto `host.start`. The panel saves the user row in its send path, and the participant path had no equivalent. Now `runViaHost` saves the person's words, never the `#file` context, through `ParticipantRunOptions.saveUserTurn` (one `saveUserRow` helper) and passes `userTurnMessageId`. A Stop pressed during the save prevents the start. A failed save is logged and the turn still runs. The `participantRun.test.ts` oracle passes unchanged, and the VSIX typecheck errors in that file are fixed.
- **MK-50-TRACE: openRun conformance goldens.** `openRun` emits one `run.routed` after `run.started`. Adapters that enter through it now compare against the derived `CONFORMANCE_ENTRY_TRACE` (`packages/agent-run/src/conformanceTask.ts`): on-prem tickets and channels, Brain, canvas, web reply and cloud. `CONFORMANCE_TRACE` stays the kernel golden. `cloudAdapter.sharedTask.test.ts` had seen an empty trace since cloud moved onto `openRun`, because it wrapped the exported `runAgent`. It now tees `openRun`.
- **Validation.** agent-tools 93/93, api 27/27, VSIX 41/41, on-prem 12/12, agent-run 58/58, Brain 6/6, canvas 1/1. agent-tools and agent-run typecheck clean. `check-one-execution --enforce` and the source-package graph check pass. Two Opus review passes were run; the second found no blocking issues. MK-50-DIAG and MK-50-SELFVAL were implemented in the follow-up above.

## RESOLVED 2026-11-23: Question-run diagnosis, routing, budget, narration folding, and preflight

- Diagnostics v2 prioritizes the latest run's stopped and unanswered-question outcomes. It counts gateway failover attempts from the completion trace and surfaces run findings in the verdict.
- Explicit questions use the quick route unless the ask explicitly requests the full pipeline. Pasted context does not affect intent. Brain leaves question-run work uncommitted.
- The shared runtime offers a final answer after six question tool rounds, including on resumed ticks. Memory bookkeeping does not reset the read-only streak.
- Builderforce pins the published Memory 2026.10.84 build for chat #168571 (W5). The shared transcript fold drops repeated lead findings and keeps new sentences. Brain diagnostics use the same fold. The integrity-verified npm artifact passed 859 shared runtime tests and 109 focused Brain tests. [Memory release workflow](https://github.com/SeanHogg/builderforce-memory/actions/runs/45289192450).
- Read-only preflight probes share a 2.5-second allowance and report a `run.preflight` step. Scoped ripgrep is already wired. Symbol queries can use an identified stale snapshot during refresh, and registry metadata determines which reads can batch.
- Validation passed for 858 shared runtime tests, 147 focused Brain tests, 60 routing and tool tests, and 22 editor search tests. Shared runtime typechecking and the execution and source-package graph checks passed. The wider Brain run passed 593 tests and reproduced the existing late-backstop failure. [Pipeline map](./docs/specs/make.md#design--agent-pipeline-map) and [PRD 50](./docs/specs/make.md#prd-50--one-pipeline-validation-and-diagnostic-gaps).

## RESOLVED 2026-11-23: One pipeline for every modality

- Editor, on-prem, and cloud run through shared entry, routing, child admission, work evidence, and settlement policy. The on-prem session port binds native tools and streaming to the same entry as tickets and children.
- Closed native catalogs supply the actual tools they can execute. Shared settlement records the editor verifier's verdict and the on-prem host's completed package checks, with the latter invalidated by subsequent workspace changes. Durable cloud cancellation skips post-Stop verification.
- Runtime validation passed for 857 shared tests, 68 focused Brain tests, 30 editor host and steering tests, 23 on-prem tests, and 39 focused cloud tests. The cloud harness injects its database and gateway boundaries. The editor harness resolves Brain to current workspace source. [Pipeline map](./docs/specs/make.md#design--agent-pipeline-map) and [PRD 50](./docs/specs/make.md#prd-50--one-pipeline-validation-and-diagnostic-gaps).

## RESOLVED 2026-11-23: Ticket admission, durable child evidence, and finish verification

- Self-hosted change tickets and authenticated cloud assignments enter the shared ledger at opening. The shared finish and settlement policy lets the host produce PR evidence after the model finishes. Missing evidence stays open in the scorecard.
- Completed durable children record evidence before their execution lands. Owners gather it in one tenant-, parent-, and ticket-scoped query. The owner's PR supplies its own review evidence.
- The shared catalog excludes unavailable registry tools from closed surfaces. Prose and tool finishes use the same configured verification, and cloud branch CI and Brain's native checks reach the shared tally. Skipped checks stay unverified.
- Editor settlement wakes its inbox once and requeues directions when startup fails before admission, unless stopped. Brain continues explicit directions received during close-out. Cloud and relay share durable late-steer admission, and the scheduled sweep retries explicitly requeued directions from terminal executions.
- Validation passed for 856 shared tests, 66 focused Brain tests, 44 focused API tests, 19 on-prem child and outbox tests, and 15 VSIX child and start-gate tests. See the [pipeline map](./docs/specs/make.md#design--agent-pipeline-map) for the outstanding integration checks.

## RESOLVED 2026-11-23: Work evidence and the shared finish and on-prem entry paths

- Brain records linked-ticket and spec coverage evidence from its existing scoped reads. Cloud records review evidence from the PR the execution opened. The self-hosted relay records review evidence after the PR API confirms it. Completed invocations with open or blocked work stay out of routing feedback.
- In-process children inherit only an exact ticket that the parent host assigned, with a restricted evidence reader. VSIX children read only their delegated ticket from their scoped chat listing. Brain owner continuations and editor wakes recheck the reference from child handoffs against that listing. Cloud children carry an explicit ticket reference limited to the parent's task.
- Brain supplies the shared gate snapshot. The native editor still checks the actual tool and path after rewrite. Pending follow-ups and attachments enter the conversation after finish-tool results through the shared steering path. Brain no longer makes a second closing model call when the shared driver already attempted synthesis.
- Tickets, sessions, and in-process children use one on-prem execution entry. Session-specific model streaming and reporting are bound as ports.
- The full shared suite passed 851 tests. Focused Brain, VSIX, cloud serialization and scorer, and on-prem child and outbox suites passed. Shared typechecking and repository execution and source-package checks passed. The full channel suite needs `@sinclair/typebox`. Cloud tail integration needs `@neondatabase/serverless`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-23: Shared run entry, child admission, and explicit work tracking

- **Run setup.** Production adapters enter through `openRun`. The shared opening renderer puts governance and persona instructions before prepared history. The runtime defaults to full routing, supports explicit automatic routing, and preserves the chosen route across resumed ticks.
- **Child admission.** VSIX, cloud, in-process on-prem, and legacy session starts use shared child validation and prompt preparation. VSIX validates before recording a child. Cloud attaches the child handle to the admitted payload, preserving the tenant's current policy gates. Background starts return handles while in-process starts return completed reports.
- **Brain policy and close-out.** Shared factories own the recorded preflight and history compaction policies. Brain uses the shared progress and provider recovery logic, sizes tool results against the serving model, and records when the failure breaker requests a closing turn. Prose finishes now run the same ticket close-out as finish-tool calls.
- **Explicit assignments.** The runtime keeps assigned IDs and acceptance criteria in run state, checks host-supplied evidence in one batch at finish, and includes deterministic work counts in terminal diagnostics. Brain and in-process on-prem expose host bindings for explicit assignments.
- **Verification.** The agent-run suite passed 848 tests, and the focused Brain suites passed 145. Cloud child serialization passed 6 tests, VSIX child and host gates passed 14, and on-prem child tests passed 6. Agent-run typechecking and the execution and package graph checks passed. Broader Brain typechecking and cloud integration checks remain dependency-blocked. [Implementation details](./docs/specs/make.md#design--agent-pipeline-map)

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-22: Project memory lost across restarts and read-only runs — chat #173444 (`remember_fact` / `recall_facts`)

User report: the agent said it saved a fact, yet a restarted run did not recall it; and after reading files the run kept re-deriving the same conclusions (chat #173444: 40 reads, 0 facts written, the same hypothesis restated five times).
- **Resume carries what the run learned (brain-embedded `runResumeState.ts`, vscode `interruptedResumeTurn.ts`).** The journaled resume state now holds the facts the run saved (`remember_fact`/`builtin_remember_fact`, successful calls only, newest 12, 600 chars) and the files it read (`fileToolKind`+`toolCallPaths`, 40). The continuation turn lists both as recorded data, one line each; `parseResumeState` re-caps untrusted journal input. New `ir.continueFacts`/`ir.continueRead` labels in all 5 VS Code l10n bundles.
- **Turn-start recall keeps remembered facts (vscode `contextPack/requestAreas.ts`, `renderContextPack.ts`).** The pack's one recall used to keep only `codemap:` area facts and discard every `remember_fact`/`learned:*` fact; it now also renders up to 5 non-codemap facts (not `workspace:` digests), stale-marked, labelled as data. The staleness check shares the pack deadline and can never cost the code-map facts.
- **Read-only investigations learn (agent-run `learnedFacts.ts`, `runKnowledgeCommit.ts`).** Run-end extraction ran only when files changed; a completed run with ≥3 distinct reads and a final answer now extracts `learned:` facts from its conclusion (tail kept). Only COMPLETED runs learn; the answer comes from this run's own rows (`hostRunLifecycle.settledAnswerOf`, shared by panel and native paths) — never a previous run's row (process-unique transient ids), a child report, a budget-stop or a forced failure-close reply (`forcedFinish` marker). Skipped when the run already saved facts itself.
- **`remember_fact` honours the chat (vscode `cognition.ts`, `bfApi/projectMemory.ts`).** Writes carry the server chat id on both editor paths (the chat's Memory switch applies); refusals return a `{ok:false}` envelope so a refused fact is never listed as saved. `rememberProjectFact` returns `{ok, reason}`.
- **The per-turn brief lists facts saved this run (agent-tools `run-knowledge.ts`),** so trimmed tool results no longer erase the run's own conclusions; bounded (24 kept, 8 shown).
- **One rule each:** `REMEMBER_FACT_TOOLS`, `savedFactOf` and `isFailedToolResult` now live in `@builderforce/agent-tools` (brain-embedded re-exports); `read_compressed` classifies as a read. Kernel `finalAnswerOf` reads only the transcript tail.
- Tests: `runResumeState.test.ts`, `interruptedResumeTurn.test.ts`, `requestAreas.test.ts`, `contextPack.test.ts`, `cognition.test.ts`, `learnedFacts.test.ts`, `memoryHookRunEnd.test.ts`, `run-knowledge.test.ts`, `hostRunLifecycle.test.ts`, `nativeBrainRun*.test.ts`, `brainRunHost.test.ts`, `editorRunEnd.test.ts`. Parity snapshots unchanged. Opus reviews over four rounds; blockers fixed.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21: Chat #165961 regressions — interrupted rows lost their actions, chat tickets not shown, the agent quit a change with no edits, duplicate server chats

User report with chat #165961's diagnostics: History's interrupted rows showed only an 8-character id and Dismiss; the chat header read "No tickets linked yet" though the run filed a ticket; the run handed off and ended without changing any code while diagnostics said "healthy".
- **Interrupted rows (vscode `runRecovery.ts`).** Restart recovery marked EVERY running `execution` record interrupted — including cloud durable executions the chat rail ingests (`chatClientId`, no `chatId`), which then listed with no chat and no Resume. ONE predicate `isHostJournaledRun` (own device, not server-observed) gates recovery and the list; queued bogus `execution:interrupted:*` events for foreign rows are dropped so the rail restores their real status.
- **Chat tickets (local-first).** A sync pull overwrote the device's `chat-ticket-link` (`chatClientId`/`ticketClientId`) with the server's form (`chatId`/`ticketId`), so the rail selected nothing — 34 of 386 links on the reporting device (since 3a2c752db). Pulled links are kept in device form under the derived id only (`pulledChatTicketLink.ts`), misfiled links from older builds are retired once per destination (`linkFormRepair:v1`), a pulled `{removed:true}` tombstone removes every copy of the pair, 'created' never downgrades, one dead-letter-aware pending check. Runs send the CURRENT server chat id for chat-scoped tools (`platformTools.ts` `serverChatIdNow`, fallback reported).
- **Duplicate server chats (local-first `chatBindLease.ts`, brain-embedded `chatIdentity.ts`).** The bind POST raced the chat's own sync import (materialized before the bind mapping existed), so the server minted 282 beside the bound 281. A holder-tokened bind lease holds the chat's import while `bindOnce`, `adopt` and `createChat({ bindPending })` bind it; another window waits for the binding; 120 s expiry.
- **Agent quit a change with no edits (brain-embedded).** An INLINE `hand_off` counted as progress, switching off the change budget and the one-time forced change turn, so the inline coder's first stall finished the run. `progressed()` now ignores inline hand-offs. Ticket/task bookkeeping (`isWorkItemWrite`, incl. device `ticket-*` and chat linking) no longer counts as a change request's effect: diagnostics say "change requested, no code changed" and run totals list ticket writes apart. The deliberate final no-tool turn is no longer flagged as "offered NONE". The chat #128305 finishing protection is unchanged.
- Regression tests in `runRecovery.test.ts`, `pulledChatTicketLink.test.ts`, `chatRail.test.ts`, `platformTools.test.ts`, `chatBindLease.test.ts`, `chatBindRace.test.ts`, `runProgress.bookkeeping.test.ts`, `progressGuard.inlineHandOff.test.ts`. Opus reviews over three rounds; findings fixed.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21: Finish turn re-prompted with no tools → xAI doom loop — chat #128305 review (agent-run 2026.10.89, run-policy 2026.10.22, brain-embedded 2026.10.95, VSIX 2026.10.203)

Run #40 tripped the progress guard (`read_only_streak` → finish). Its final no-tools turn wrote a good report, then the `brain.ship` delivery gate sent that report back with "verify, self-review, git_commit" on a turn that still offered zero tools. Grok (xai-oauth) looped, xAI's `tail_repetition:64@response` check cut the stream, the policy did not fail over, and the run settled as an ERROR. Triage blamed "TOOL NOT ADVERTISED". Root cause: a surface's forced final menu had no way to be marked final, so the kernel ran the stall/delivery ladder on it.
- **Kernel contract (agent-run).** `TurnMenu.final` + `TurnSelection.finalBy` (`'guards' | 'surface'`, one predicate `finalSource` in `kernelHooks.ts`). A final turn advertises `[]`, is never judged as a stall or sent back by a rung, and only the guards' own A3 finish spends `finalTurnDone` / keeps the run's role. New `DeliveryLedger.finalAccepted` hook fires when a final turn is accepted.
- **Brain finishing (brain-embedded).** One `finishTurn` builds every finish turn; `RunProgressGuard.finishing` is sticky per run. The last finish turn is marked `final`; `brainDelivery.rungs()` returns no stop hook / gates while finishing; `loop.finish_skips_delivery_gates` (gates that would have applied, incl. `brain.stop_hook`, + files) is traced once per run (`run.finishSkipNoted`) from `finalAccepted` or a record turn.
- **Run policy.** `transportFailed`: an interrupted model that is not the user's standing non-releasable pin (verify review model, failover pick, escalation, releasable pin) is added to `broken` and the turn retries once; a run-chosen model returns to the user's pin (with its strictness) unless the pin broke; `strictPin` is always reset. `escalated` ignores a broken target; `nextTurn` never asks for a broken review model.
- **Answer kept.** A delivery-gate-sent-back answer survives a provider failure on its re-prompt: `brainSettle` settles quietly with `loop.reprompt_failed_answer_kept` (still `emit` + `onActivity`; no duplicate message, no Evermind learn). A later kept turn clears it; Stop and non-provider errors behave as before.
- **Triage.** `LikelyCause` `'provider-failure'` (`providerFailureCause.ts`), ranked right after memory-answered: names model, message, failover tried, a gate re-prompt of a no-tool turn, and an answer kept. VS Code harness treats it as bad.
- Regression tests: `finalTurnKernel.test.ts`, `policy.test.ts`, `brainDelivery.finishing.test.ts`, `brainTurnMenu.finishing.test.ts`, `brainSettle.test.ts`, `brainTriage.test.ts`, `run/parity/repromptFailure.test.ts` (replays the incident through `startRun`). No existing assertion or parity snapshot changed. Opus review: no blockers; its 5 should-fix + 7 nits fixed.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21: Composer typeahead, /starter-kit, /launch and launch failure (webcontainers 2026.11.8, VSIX 2026.10.201)

User report with screenshots: `/` showed commands only after Enter; `/starter-kit` called a folder holding only `.builderforce/` non-empty; `/launch` opened only the system browser; launching `react-vite-node-express` failed every service with `bfsh: command not found: npm install` (exit 127), with no way to copy diagnostics.
- **Live `/` `@` `#` typeahead.** One primitive `packages/brain-ui/src/mention/useTriggerAutocomplete.tsx` (+ `TriggerPopup.tsx`); `@`, `#` and the new `/` (`CommandAutocomplete.tsx`, fed the host's `/help` model through `options.commands`) are thin adapters, the old duplicated mention/ticket machinery is deleted. `/` opens only at line start (not `//`, `/api/x`), ranks exact id first, runs a no-arg command on pick and inserts `insertText` otherwise; Enter on a disabled row submits `/<id>` so the host says why. `@`/`#` stay closed with no candidates, show a no-match row otherwise; no re-open after a pick; IME and Shift+Enter left alone. `#` rows show the real status and a pick keeps the following text. Labels in VS Code, web (5) and Chrome (5).
- **`/starter-kit`** ignores `.builderforce` (`DIRECTIVES_DIR`), `.git`, `.vscode` for the emptiness test but still names a kit file that already exists, even inside an ignored folder.
- **`/launch`** opens VS Code's native integrated browser (`workbench.action.browser.open`, detected once via `getCommands`, a failed probe is retried) when the launcher's certificate is trusted, else the system browser with the reason; replies carry `actions` (contract changed from one `action`): "Open in VS Code" / "Trust certificate and open in VS Code" / "Open in external browser"; `/launch external`. `external`/`stop`/`trust` are reserved over environment names. The launcher page is now localized in VS Code (`launcherLabels.ts`). `simpleBrowser.show` is not used: it is an iframe and the launcher sends `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- **Launch failure (webcontainers 2026.11.8).** A manifest `command` is a command line: `splitCommandLine` (core `shell/commandLine.ts`) splits plain words into program + args at the one seam `manifest/serviceCommand.ts`; shell lines run via `bfsh -c` only for node on the browser target, else typed `shell-command-unsupported` (services and jobs); `shell-command-with-args` and `command-backslash` issues. The node decline list sees inside `bfsh|sh|bash -c` lines and command substitutions.
- **Copy diagnostics** on the launcher page's Logs card: plain-text report (header, start error, services, issues, all logs), redacted through the shield's `scrubCredentials` (now catches `*_TOKEN=`, `*_PASSWORD=`, JSON keys, `Authorization` of any scheme), clipboard API with a focus-safe fallback and a live-region status.

### ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21 — second report: preview link "Not Found", blank preview, manifest location and stale `$schema` (webcontainers 2026.11.11, commits 5f2a7087a + b58522b66, VSIX 2026.10.204 → 2026.10.206 → 2026.10.207)

Follow-up report on the same launch flow, with screenshots: the launcher's preview link answered "Not Found"; the preview page itself stayed blank; the app manifest lived at the repo root; every manifest showed one problem ("Unable to load schema"); and the shipped VSIX carried the dev `.builderforce/` folder.
- **Preview link "Not Found".** The launcher now serves a `/preview` page (`launcher/server/previewPage.ts`): a user-started top-level navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Site: none`) to a preview root is redirected there with a 60 s HMAC ticket (`PREVIEW_TICKET_TTL_MS`, `<expiry>.<HMAC(secret, expiry, src)>`); deeper paths and cross-site navigations are refused, so the page cannot be used as an open redirect or a CSRF surface.
- **Blank preview.** `es-module-lexer`'s WASM/eval fallback was blocked by the preview CSP. Import rewriting now decodes specifiers with the eval-free `importSpecifier` (`core/src/importSpecifier.ts`, used by `rewriteImports.ts` and `node/esm.ts`), so it works under a CSP that forbids `eval`.
- **Manifest moved to `.builderforce/builderforce.json`.** One reader `locateManifest` (`browser/src/manifest/locate.ts`) prefers the canonical file and falls back to a legacy root read; `/manifest move` migrates a legacy file (a target that appears after the approval is refused, never replaced); kits and `/manifest init` no longer write `$schema`; `jsonValidation` narrowed to the real manifest names (agent-runtime's home config and `node_modules` excluded), so the editor association validates v1 without a document `$schema`.
- **Stale `$schema` stripped (b58522b66).** Manifests written before 5f2a7087a carry `"$schema": "https://builderforce.ai/schema/app.v1.json"`, which 404s until the frontend deploys (Worker 10 MiB limit — see the Gap Register). `/manifest move` removes exactly that top-level member with a minimal text edit (formatting and every other key kept; the URL constant is the runtime's `APP_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_URL`, defined once); an already-canonical manifest carrying it is offered the removal through the same seam, reached from `/launch`'s "Remove its $schema" reply action. Errors are reported, never swallowed; l10n in all 5 bundles.
- **`.builderforce/**` excluded from the VSIX** (`.vscodeignore`) — the dev folder's 2.6 MB code-analysis cache no longer ships.
- Close-out (2026-11-21): fresh Opus review of b58522b66 passed all checks (minimal edit, exact-URL-only strip, one constant, one shared seam, errors surfaced, real translations in all 5 bundles, ignore pattern verified against vsce's matcher); its only findings were 4 untested cases, added as 6 regression tests (no-trailing-newline, CRLF-last-member, prefix/substring URLs left untouched, `/launch` advisory read failure). VSIX 2026.10.207 packages and installs that coverage; `tsc -p ./`, `tsc -p webview/tsconfig.json` and the three composer test files (58/58) pass; the packaged VSIX contains no `extension/.builderforce/` entries.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21: PRD → tickets reliability — chat #157440 review (api 2026.10.105, brain-embedded 2026.10.94, agent-tools 2026.10.22, agent-run 2026.10.88, pipeline-route 2026.10.1, VSIX 2026.10.200)

"Review the PRD and create tickets for all incomplete items" left P25-09, OUT-02, OUT-03 and four Blocked items unticketed. Seven pipeline causes, all fixed:
- **Ticket tools survive role caps.** `chatWorkObligationTools` (create, update, from_delta, list on a linked chat) ride the preamble's required set as `promptTools.obligation`, so capped code/verify turns keep them (`runPreamble.ts`, `brainPlatformTools.ts`, `roleCap.ts`). `TICKET_FROM_DELTA_TOOL` lives once in `ticketToolVocabulary.ts`.
- **Ticket-filing requests plan first.** `pipeline-route` `ticketIntent` feature (weight 3.0); patterns need exact filing verbs + tickets/work items, or spec words (PRD/spec/roadmap/requirements/gap register) — 15 ordinary coding phrasings are negative tests.
- **Spec coverage finish gate.** One parser `parseSpecOpenItems` + `specTicketCoverage` in `packages/agent-tools/src/specs/` (gapRegister and nearDuplicateTitle moved there; repeated tokens merge, short tokens need a separator, leading-status classification). `brain-embedded/src/runStore/specTicketCoverageGate.ts` holds a run that was asked (ticketing + spec language) to ticket a spec until every incomplete/blocked item has a ticket; backstop "Code change" tickets never count; bounded (2 repeats, 4 holds), parse cached per run. `roadmap.align_tickets` takes `specPath`/`chatId`.
- **Forced finish records work.** A finish turn offers the obligation tools for up to 3 record turns, then one no-tools report; `finishingTurn` pre-empts change-budget/no-progress/hand-off forced turns and carries no steer note.
- **Builtin tool args answer 400.** `builtinToolArgs.ts` `prepareBuiltinToolArgs` validates required args and coerces against each tool's schema (JSON array text, single string → [string], never split; strict numerics; 1/0 booleans; object JSON text; `minLength: 0` allows empty); `BuiltinToolArgError extends ValidationError` → gateway 400 naming tool + field. `tickets.from_delta` no longer drops string `files`.
- **Injected resume turns never set the publish hold.** VS Code resume turns persist `metadata.injected`; `personMarkedRunTurns` skips them; `>`-quoted lines are ignored by `declinesShipping`/`asksToShip`; diagnostics, "Send again" and draft give-back honour the mark.
- **Plan turns get a context window.** `gatewayModelWindows` matches a served ref by path suffix (ambiguity incl. windowless rows → none); `/v1/models` now carries OpenRouter-connection `contextWindow` from the OpenRouter catalog (`connectionModelWindows`).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-21: Agent execution efficiency — ticket-cleanup run review (api 2026.10.104, frontend 2026.10.105, brain-embedded 2026.10.93, agent-tools 2026.10.21, VSIX 2026.10.199)

A 1,246-ticket cleanup took 124 turns, 237 tool calls and ~10M prompt tokens where 15–20 calls should do; ~700 of the 984 archived tickets were persona fan-out copies. All eight recommendations shipped, each through an Opus review and fix round.
- **Fan-out at the source** (`ticketParticipants.ts` `materializeWorkItems`): at most one child per role per root; an existing live `[Role] <title>` child is reused; an archived linked child no longer counts; a fan-out child never fans out (`skipped: 'fanout_child'`); links are compare-and-set, so a lost race archives its surplus child and reports it. The coordinator for a role staffed across stages is deterministic (lane position, then id).
- **`tasks.list` server-side filters** pushed to SQL (`taskListFilter.ts`, `TaskRepository.findPage/findIndexRows`): `parentTaskId`, `topLevelOnly`, `titlePrefix`/`titleMatch`, `createdBefore`/`createdAfter` (ISO), `assigned: none|any`, `isFanoutCopy`, `taskType`. Paged in SQL with `count(*) over()`. Title/assignee filters exclude SECURITY tickets for a viewer without clearance, so they cannot be used as an oracle. The tools moved out of `builtinMcpService.ts` into `taskBulkToolCatalog.ts`.
- **`tasks.archive_where({filter, dryRun = true})`** returns count + an index-line sample; it requires a selective field and refuses a whole-workspace match. It and `archive_many` go through ONE bulk path, `TaskService.archiveMany` (a single tenant-scoped `UPDATE … WHERE id = ANY`), followed by `afterTaskBulkWrite` (tree version, projects list, PMO, broadcast, completed-by-assignee, ROI).
- **`roadmap.align_tickets`**: a pure Gap Register parser (`domain/roadmap/gapRegister.ts`; 304 gaps in the live ROADMAP) and a use case that reports matched gaps, gaps without a ticket, open tickets matching no gap, dangling spec links and missing spec files, in one call. It reads from the project's repo (cached by commit sha) or a Brain attachment.
- **Tool availability:** one resolver (`packages/agent-tools/src/toolNaming.ts`) accepts `builtin_x_y`, the `x.y` catalog id and bare `x_y` in the router, gateway, VS Code native path and preflight. The Brain pins up to 8 tools called or named in the prior conversation, filtered by the role cap and ordered so the tool block only grows at its end.
- **`deploy.status`** (platform-operator only): API and frontend commit (stamped at deploy via `wrangler deploy --var GIT_SHA:…`, read from `/health` on both workers), the latest Release run, and whether a given commit is live (including superseded by a newer deploy).
- **Dev tooling:** `.githooks/pre-commit` regenerates `api/container/toolOutputPolicy.mjs` when its sources are staged (wired by `scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs`; agent-runtime's dead hooks deleted). `edit_file` gains unescape and whitespace-tolerant tiers (unique match, token boundaries, refuses an indentation-ambiguous match). The push gate passes an already-on-upstream HEAD as a no-op, refuses when touched files are uncommitted, computes outgoing for the named branch, and gates `git_push {branch: base}` from a feature checkout.
- **Delta tickets close on a direct push** to the default branch (`completeDeltaOnPush.ts`) by an explicit `task-N` / `ticket/N` reference or by full coverage of the delta's recorded files. PR merges and reverts are excluded (the merge path owns those). This shares one close loop with the merge path.
