## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-20: Runs stop to ask "continue?" or "may I ship?" instead of finishing and following a ship policy (PRD 48, VS Code chat #157440)

Chat #157440 finished, verified and committed its work, then stopped on a progress-guard `ask_user` pause ("no progress — how should it proceed?") and a "push needs approval" card. Cloud project merge settings never reached the run, and cloud merging hung off a platform-wide env flag, which is wrong for a multi-tenant product.
- **Progress guard never asks a person.** The ladder is steer → escalate (or a second steer when no stronger model exists) → finish. Finish is a no-tools final report, marked verified or stalled. Delegated work counts as progress (`changedFiles`/`reports` in delegation results and injected child reports). Waits are neutral up to `MAX_WAIT_TURNS = 12`. A stalled planner hands to the coder once before finishing. `pendingPause`, `PAUSE_OPTIONS` and the brain pause are deleted.
- **One `ShipPolicy` (`leave_uncommitted | commit | commit_push | pull_request`)** in `packages/run-guards/src/shipPolicy.ts`, carried on `RunPolicy.ship`. It is a per-project, per-tenant DB setting (`ship_mode` on `project_manager_configs` and `tenant_manager_defaults`, migration 1356), read and written through `GET/PUT /api/manager/:projectId`, `PATCH /defaults` and the `manager.policy` / `manager.configure` MCP tools. It is never a VS Code setting or an env var. Unset means `commit`, with no mid-run ask. The VSIX fetches it per run; children run `leave_uncommitted` and the owner ships once. `publishAllowed` refuses publish calls the policy forbids, and a merge by any agent tool is refused in every mode.
- **Cloud runs open a PR and never merge.** `cloudShipGate` refuses raw shell push/PR/merge in the cloud. Every `CLOUD_AUTOMERGE_ENABLED` / `CLOUD_AUTOMERGE_REQUIRE_GREEN` branch is deleted (`mergeOnGreen`, `securityVerdictCatchup`, `mergeBranchToBase`), so `prMergeSweep` is the only automatic merge writer, per project manager policy. The manager's merges and the human Merge button are untouched by the ship rules.
- **Per-run merge grant (§4.6).** A person dispatching a cloud run from the web app can grant "merge into main" for that run (security fix, urgent feature). It overrides project merge settings the way the Merge button does, through the same `gateHumanMerge` check plus green CI on the pinned commit. It is bound to the PR that run opened at the commit it pushed, claimed atomically once, and voided on cancel, failure, a moved head, a closed PR, expiry or a revoked granter. The granted cohort of `prMergeSweep` executes it. It is web-UI and person only, and refused for on-prem targets, API keys, agent tools and multi-repo tickets.
- On-prem `buildCodingPrompt` uses the server's `shipDirective`; the on-prem host never merges.

**PRD 48 spec, archived word for word from make.md on 2026-11-20:**

### PRD 48 — Ship policy: autonomous runs ship by rule, never by mid-run question

> Opened 2026-11-19 from VS Code chat #157440: an orchestrator implemented and verified a whole PRD, committed it, then
> stopped twice for a human — a progress-guard "how should it proceed?" (fixed separately: the A3 ladder now ends in a
> final report, never a question) and "a push needs approval". Operator rule: a run finishes on its own. What it does
> with finished work is a **standing policy**, not a question. `ask_user` is for genuine business questions only.

#### §1 The rule

| Host | Who sets the ship policy | Where it lives | How the run gets it |
|---|---|---|---|
| VSIX (local) | The **person**, through the project's settings (the Manager tab, the API, or by telling the agent, which calls `manager.configure`) | **The database:** the project's `ship_mode` setting (§4.0), tenant default + project override, in the same manager-policy fold as the merge flags | Fetched per run for the chat's project through the policy-gate fetch/cache seam (`clients/vscode/src/policyGates.ts`, offline snapshot) → `EditorRunSettings` → the run request (`runRequestFields`) → `BrainRunContext.shipPolicy` (every enforcement seam reads the context), mirrored into `RunPolicy.ship` by `brainRunPolicy` |
| Cloud | The **project's settings** | The database: the same fold (`managerPolicy.ts` → `getEffectiveManagerPolicy`): `allowAutoMerge` (ceiling), `requireSignoffToComplete` (floor), `prMergePolicy` | Loaded at dispatch into `CloudRunOpts` → `RunPolicy.ship` (descriptive: the prompt and the push refusal). **`prMergeSweep` stays the single merge writer** |

No ship or merge decision reads a Cloudflare env var or secret, and none reads a VS Code setting. Every one is a
tenant/project row read and written through the API and the MCP.

A chat-scoped **publish hold** (`brain-embedded/src/runStore/publishHold.ts` — "don't commit until I validate") stays as
the person's per-chat override ABOVE the VSIX rule: it can only narrow (hold), and a later explicit ship order in the same
chat lifts it back to the rule. Nothing else overrides the policy: not a sub-agent, not a nudge, not the model. Tenant
governance (`PolicyGate` `require-approval` / `block` on publish tools) still outranks the person's setting.

#### §2 Contract — one type, both hosts (`packages/run-guards/src/shipPolicy.ts`)

`run-guards` already owns `PUBLISH_TOOLS` (`inRunVerify.ts`) and `gitCommandPattern`, and depends on `agent-tools` — so
the contract lives in `run-guards` (an `agent-tools` home would be a cycle). `agent-run`, `brain-embedded` and
`clients/vscode` already import `run-guards`. `RunPolicy` (`packages/agent-run/src/contract.ts`) gains `ship?: ShipPolicy`.

```ts
export type ShipMode = 'leave_uncommitted' | 'commit' | 'commit_push' | 'pull_request';
export interface ShipPolicy {
  mode: ShipMode;
  /** pull_request only: when the PR merges. 'never' = a human merges. */
  merge: 'never' | 'immediate' | 'on_green';
  /** pull_request only: a recorded independent review/sign-off is required before merge. */
  review: 'none' | 'required';
  /** Provenance, shown in the directive and diagnostics. */
  source: 'project_settings' | 'chat_hold' | 'subagent' | 'person_grant' | 'default';
}
export const DEFAULT_SHIP_POLICY: ShipPolicy;                    // mode 'commit', source 'default'
export type ShipHost = 'editor' | 'cloud';                       // cloud = the platform opens the PR (cloud + on-prem agent hosts)
export function shipDirective(p: ShipPolicy, ctx?: { chatId?: number | null; host?: ShipHost }): string; // the ONE ship directive for every host
export function shipNudge(p: ShipPolicy, host?: ShipHost): string | null; // the ONE "you left it unshipped" nudge (null when the mode ships nothing)
export function publishVerbOf(tool: string, args: unknown): 'commit' | 'push' | 'pull_request' | 'cleanup' | 'merge' | null;
export function publishAllowed(p: ShipPolicy, tool: string, args: unknown, host?: ShipHost): { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string };
export function narrowShipPolicy(p: ShipPolicy, to: ShipPolicy | null): ShipPolicy; // stricter of the two
export function narrowByHold(p: ShipPolicy, hold: { messageNumber: number; text: string } | null): ShipPolicy;
```

- `publishVerbOf` is THE publish matcher: `git_commit` / `git_push` / `open_pull_request` / `git_cleanup_merged` by name
  (`PUBLISH_TOOLS` + `REPO_PUBLISH_TOOLS`), and a `run_command` whose command is a raw `git commit`, `git push`,
  `gh pr create` / `gh pr new` or `gh pr merge` (verb `merge`). `brain-embedded` `isPublishCall` (`publishHold.ts`) and
  the duplicate `RAW_PUBLISH` in `selfReviewShip.ts` are deleted and their callers migrated.
- `publishAllowed`: `merge` is refused in every mode (runs never merge; `prMergeSweep` does). `leave_uncommitted`
  refuses every verb; `commit` refuses push/PR; `commit_push` refuses PR; `pull_request` refuses a direct push to the
  base branch — a refspec naming main/master, no refspec, or a bare `HEAD` / `@`. `cleanup` follows `push`.
- `host: 'cloud'` (cloud runs and on-prem agent hosts, whose platform opens the PR) words the directive, nudge and
  refusal without git tools; `editor` (default) is the VS Code wording.
- **Sub-agents (new rule, not current behaviour):** brain-embedded derives a child's policy from `req.lineage` (the input
  `toolScope: 'subagent'` already uses) as `leave_uncommitted` / `source: 'subagent'`. The OWNER ships once, after
  verifying the fan-out.
- `shipDirective` replaces `selfReviewShipDirective` + `publishHoldDirective`; `shipNudge` replaces
  `unshippedChangeNudge`; `leftChangeUnshipped` reads only the policy (no separate `declinesShipping(requestText)`).
  This closes PRD 45 §4.5 (its `builtin_reviews_record complete` wording moves here) — §4.5's "leave
  `unshippedChangeNudge` unchanged" is superseded by this section.

#### §3 VSIX wiring

1. No VS Code setting. The host reads the project's `shipPolicy` from `GET /api/manager/:projectId` (§4.5) through the
   same fetch/cache seam as `resolveRunPolicyGates` (`clients/vscode/src/policyGates.ts`, cached, offline snapshot).
2. No project, no snapshot while offline, or no stored value → `DEFAULT_SHIP_POLICY` (source `default`). Into
   `EditorRunSettings` → `runRequestFields` (`stageModels.ts`, spread at `nativeBrainRun.ts`) → the run request.
3. `runPreamble.ts`: beside `c.publishHold`, compute `c.shipPolicy = narrowByHold(childOrRequestPolicy, hold)`; copy it
   onto `BrainRunContext`; `brainRunPolicy` (`run/webAdapter.ts`) mirrors it into `RunPolicy.ship`. The directive branch
   becomes `shipDirective(c.shipPolicy)`.
4. `runStore/callPreflight.ts`: the hold refusal becomes `publishAllowed(run.shipPolicy, …)` — same position (before the
   confirm gate), so `acceptEdits` and child contexts cannot waive it.
5. `clients/vscode/src/nativeRunTool.ts` `nativeNeedsConfirm`: a publish call the policy ALLOWS is not confirmed in
   `ask` mode — the setting is the person's standing approval — UNLESS a governance gate says `require-approval`. The
   `shipGatePreflight` evidence that only the approval card showed is written to the trace instead when the card is skipped.
6. `runStore/deliveryGates.ts` `brain.ship`: fires only when `shipNudge(policy)` is non-null and the run did not ship.
7. **No value yet:** the run never asks. It ships under `DEFAULT_SHIP_POLICY` (`commit` — local and reversible), and its
   final report says the project's ship policy is unset and can be set in the project's settings or by asking the agent.
8. **The agent changes it when the person tells it to.** "From now on commit and push" → one `manager.configure`
   call with `shipMode` (§4.5), and every later run on that project follows it. The route's existing manager-role gate
   applies. A sub-agent's widening call (the VSIX tool gate, by lineage) is refused with the reason, never turned into a
   question.
9. Diagnostics: `chatDiagnostics.ts` / `gatherChatDiagnostics.ts` replace `publishHold` with
   `shipPolicy { mode, source, hold? }` read from the run record, so an uncommitted change under `leave_uncommitted` is
   reported as policy, not as a parked ticket.

#### §4 Cloud wiring

0. **Storage — `ship_mode`.** Expand-only migration: a nullable `ship_mode` (`leave_uncommitted | commit | commit_push |
   pull_request`) on `project_manager_configs` and on the tenant tier that holds `allowAutoMerge`
   (`schema/identity.ts`). The fold (`managerPolicy.ts`) resolves it as a plain override (project beats tenant beats the
   built-in `commit`), stays pure, and exposes `shipMode`. It is read and written ONLY through the existing manager
   config route, the workspace-defaults route and `manager.configure`, which keep their role gate, normalizer, tri-state
   `null` = inherit, and audit. The Manager tab and workspace defaults (`ManagerAutonomyControls.tsx`,
   `ManagerDefaults.tsx`) get the control, localized in all five catalogs, working in both themes and on narrow screens.
   VSIX runs use `shipMode`. Cloud runs always open a PR (`mode: 'pull_request'`), whatever `shipMode` says.

**One merge writer.** `api/src/application/repos/prMergeSweep.ts` already merges by project settings — `prMergePolicy`,
sign-off, `allowAutoMerge`, the security verdict, the manager-enabled join, `MERGE_QUEUE_DEPTH` and `merge_blocked`
dedupe — and is documented as the single writer. Runs never merge.

1. Dispatch loads the effective manager policy (`getEffectiveManagerPolicy`) into `CloudRunOpts`
   (`runtime/cloudRunOpts.ts`); `cloudAdapter.policyOf` maps it to `RunPolicy.ship` with ONE pure mapper beside the fold
   (`manager/shipPolicyOf.ts`): `mode: 'pull_request'`;
   `merge = !managed || canary || !enabled || !allowAutoMerge || prMergePolicy === 'queue' ? 'never' : prMergePolicy === 'on_green' ? 'on_green' : 'immediate'`
   (`managed` = `isProjectManaged`, the sweep's own opt-in; canary holds every merge — so `merge` says exactly what the sweep does)
   (`immediate` = whatever the sweep does for it today); `review = requireSignoffToComplete ? 'required' : 'none'`;
   `source: 'project_settings'`.
2. The cloud system prompt carries `shipDirective(policy, { host: 'cloud' })`: the platform opens the PR when the run
   ends, who reviews, when it merges — and that it must not ask, merge or push to the base branch. The cloud tool gate
   (`publishAllowed(…, 'cloud')`) refuses EVERY raw shell push, `gh pr create` and merge from `run_command`
   categorically. A run that wrote code but whose PR failed to open lands `failed` with the reason.
3. Retire the `CLOUD_AUTOMERGE_ENABLED` / `CLOUD_AUTOMERGE_REQUIRE_GREEN` merge branches at every site —
   `finalizeCloudRun` (`cloudFinalize.ts`), `ingestRepoCiEvent.ts`, `openTaskPullRequest.ts` (Done-drag `taskFinalize.ts`,
   on-prem `agentHostRoutes.ts`, dispatch PRs), `securityVerdictCatchup.ts` — and `cloudAutoMergeEnabled` /
   `cloudMergeOnGreenCi` with them. A run opens its PR and ends; the sweep merges it per the project's settings.
   (The flag is in no committed config. If it is set as a Worker secret, projects without an enabled manager stop
   auto-merging — intended: project settings now decide.)
4. On-prem agent hosts build their own prompt: they get the same `shipDirective` from the same mapper through the
   agent-host run payload (`agentHostRoutes.ts`).
5. **The project's flags live behind the API, and agents can change them.** Merge authority is the project setting
   (`allowAutoMerge`, `prMergePolicy`, `requireSignoffToComplete`, `canary`) — read and written through
   `GET/PUT /api/manager/:projectId` and the built-in MCP tools `manager.policy` / `manager.configure`, which replay that
   same route (role gate, normalizers, tri-state inherit, audit), now including `shipMode`. No env var decides it.
   `GET /api/manager/:projectId` and `manager.policy` also return the derived `shipPolicy` — the VSIX-run policy built
   from `shipMode`, and the cloud-run policy from the §4.1 mapper — so an agent reads exactly what a run would follow.
   The VSIX agent reaches both through its platform tool router; a test pins that `manager.configure` is in the VSIX
   catalog.
6. **A person can grant "merge into main" for ONE cloud run** (operator, 2026-11-19: a security fix or a high-priority
   feature must not wait for the manager). Decisions:
   - **The grant is a pre-approved human merge.** It overrides the project's merge settings (`allowAutoMerge` off, the
     manager off, canary, sign-off), exactly as the in-product Merge button is not bound by them, and applies exactly
     that button's checks (`humanMergeGate`, shared) plus green CI. There is no tenant governance merge gate outside run
     tool calls (`require-approval` / `block` gate a run's own tools, which never merge), so none applies here — the
     same as for the button.
   - **Checks: the security verdict passes AND CI is green.** A failing or missing check holds the merge, and the run's
     report and the PR timeline say why.
   - **Who:** only a PERSON may grant, with the same role the in-product merge route requires
     (`POST /pull-requests/:id/merge`), from the web UI only — never through an agent tool (a Brain run calls tools
     with the person's own token, so a model or a prompt injection could otherwise grant one), never a run or a machine
     caller, never an API key and never a non-web client surface. Cloud runs only: every entry point asks ONE predicate
     that mirrors the dispatcher's own routing (`runtime/runHostBinding.ts` `wouldRunOnHost`: a pinned host AND an
     agent that allows host execution) before dispatch, so a ticket assigned to a host refuses a grant on run-now too
     (400 `merge_grant_not_cloud`). Single-repo tickets only: a ticket bound to more than one repo refuses a grant
     (400 `merge_grant_multi_repo`). RBAC: the control is disabled, not hidden, with the reason as its tooltip, for a
     role that cannot grant, a non-cloud target and a multi-repo ticket.
   - **Storage:** one `merge_grants` row per granted execution — `execution_id`, `granted_by` (nullable, `ON DELETE
     SET NULL`, so the audit row survives the user's deletion) with `granted_by_label` (the granter's name at grant
     time), `reason` (required, CHECK non-blank in SQL and Drizzle), `created_at`, `consumed_at`,
     `voided_at`/`void_reason`, `last_considered_at` — plus `merge_grant_pull_requests` (the PR the granted run
     opened, `head_sha`, `hold_code`), in the domain that owns executions. Audited as an activity record.
   - **Execution — still one automatic merge writer.** The run never merges; it opens its PR as always.
     `prMergeSweep` gains a second cohort: open PRs the granted execution itself opened (bound at finalize), selected regardless of the
     manager opt-in, ahead of the queue, merged through `mergeRecordedPr` once the security verdict passes and CI is
     green (the CI verdict already arms the sweep's tick via `ciMergeQueueSignal`). The grant is consumed on merge.
   - **The run knows.** A granted run's `RunPolicy.ship` has `merge: 'on_green'` with `source: 'person_grant'`, so its
     directive says a person authorized the merge, the platform merges it when the checks pass, and it must still not
     merge or push the base branch itself.
   - **UI:** the web app's cloud-run dispatch control gets "Merge into main when done" plus a required reason, in all
     five catalogs, both themes, at 360px.
   - **As built:** the role is ONE constant (`repos/prMergeAuthority.ts` `PR_MERGE_MIN_ROLE`, also the in-product merge
     route's gate). Grants arrive on `POST /api/runtime/executions` (written before the run starts, so prep reads it)
     and `POST /api/tasks/:id/run-now`. On both, the grant is written after the execution is submitted and BEFORE it
     starts (the dispatcher's `onSubmitted` hook), so prep always reads it. A failed write never fails the
     dispatch: the response says `mergeGrant: 'failed'`. No agent tool carries a grant.
   - **Binding.** The grant BINDS at the run's finalize to the PR that run opened, or, on a re-run of a ticket that
     already has an open PR, to that PR. Either way it is pinned to the last commit THIS run pushed, proven by SHA and
     never by commit text (the subject marker is a public string). Every platform write records the commit SHA its
     provider returned (`task_file_changes.commit_sha`, migration 1358). The PR head must be a SHA recorded for THIS
     execution, otherwise the grant voids `head_moved`, and with no readable head it voids `no_head`. Every commit ahead
     of base must be recorded for a run of the same ticket, otherwise it voids `foreign_commits`; commits from before
     1358 and platform base-sync merge commits count as foreign, so such a PR is merged in-product after review. There is no fallback to whatever head the provider
     reports. A run that ends without a PR voids `no_pull_request` / `cancelled`. A run that dies before finalize
     voids at the central terminal transition (the execution repository's terminal and reaper hooks): an unbound
     grant voids `run_failed` / `cancelled`.
   - **The sweep.** The sweep merges only a bound PR at its pinned commit, with no base sync (a sync would move the
     head off the pin). Grants are visited in `last_considered_at NULLS FIRST` order and stamped on each visit, so no
     tenant starves another under the per-tick cap. Before the claim, the sweep re-checks that the granter is STILL a
     tenant member with the merge role. If not, the grant voids `granter_revoked`. It then claims the grant atomically.
     The claim is released only on a definite refusal (`ok:false`): on a thrown merge the claim is KEPT. Once it is
     30 minutes old with its PR still open, the sweep asks the provider: merged keeps the grant spent; not merged
     releases the claim back to live and reports the release.
   - **Settle and expiry.** Each tick settles grants whose bound PRs are all closed or merged: one merged elsewhere
     consumes the grant, all closed voids `pr_closed`. A grant still open 7 days after `created_at` voids `expired`.
     When a PR was already merged, the journal says it was settled without a merge, never that the platform merged
     it.
   - **Managed queue.** The managed queue skips a PR bound to a live grant, so only one cohort ever touches it.
   - **Holds and the run view.** A hold is the binding's current `hold_code` plus a `merge_grant_held` timeline line
     (deduped on change) — its own type, so it never feeds the managed queue's `merge_blocked` ceilings.
     `GET /api/runtime/executions/:id/merge-grant` serves the run view (codes, not prose). It shows `merged` only when a
     bound PR's status is `merged`, and the view refetches when the run's status changes.

#### §5 Done checks

- VSIX, project `shipMode: commit_push`, `permissionMode: ask`, no governance gate: a run commits and pushes with no confirmation card and no question.
- VSIX, a governance `require-approval` gate on `git_push`: the card still shows despite `commit_push`.
- Tenant default `commit_push`, project `leave_uncommitted`: the project value wins; `null` on the project inherits the tenant.
- VSIX, project `leave_uncommitted`: `git_commit` and a raw `gh pr create` refused before the confirm gate; final report lists changed paths.
- VSIX, no value anywhere (or offline with no snapshot): no question in any run; it commits locally and the final report says the project's ship policy is unset.
- "From now on commit and push" in a VSIX chat → one `manager.configure { shipMode: 'commit_push' }`; the next run reads it from the API.
- VSIX, a sub-agent calls `git_commit`: refused; the owner commits once after the fan-out.
- VSIX, chat says "don't commit until I check": held for that chat regardless of setting; "ok commit and push" restores the setting.
- Cloud, project `allowAutoMerge: true, prMergePolicy: on_green`, manager enabled: the run opens a PR and ends; `prMergeSweep` merges on green.
- Cloud, defaults: the PR opens, nothing merges, the run's prompt says so, and it ends without asking.
- `git grep -E "CLOUD_AUTOMERGE|cloudAutoMergeEnabled|selfReviewShipDirective|publishHoldDirective|unshippedChangeNudge|RAW_PUBLISH"` → nothing outside the shared module and tests.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-19: A run ends with its linked tickets still open; open epics and containers read 100% (VS Code chat #276)

Chat #276 ("implement the full PRD") ended its last run in prose while epic #6902 was `in_progress` and the open slices were listed in the reply; the epic's ring read 0% beside two done code-change tickets.
- **47642b1d5:** a work-mode top-level run is held (prose or `finish`) while a ticket it owns, filed or touched — or a linked `in_progress` ticket when the ask is a change request or the run made progress — is still open. It may end once each is done, `in_review`, `blocked` with a reason, or after asking the person; at most 6 holds, a re-hold only after real progress, and a hold is not a model failure. The chat-ticket selectors read the real `list_tickets` envelope (they read only bare arrays, so the advance and close-on-ship backstops never acted) and now act only on run-owned tickets, through one `listChatTickets`. `tickets.from_delta` takes `parentTaskId`, so auto-minted code-change tickets file under the chat's sole open epic (mint only; a refused parent is retried without). Only a closed task/gap/epic lane emits 100%; `unsupportedDelivery` and its query are deleted.
- **Follow-up:** every chat-linked ticket kind closes on its own status words (one `TICKET_CLOSED_STATES` registry in agent-loop: portfolio, initiative, objective, roadmap, spec, retro, poker); an open container at 100 reads the claimed-complete rung (75) on the api, the chat rollup, the `openOnly` filter and the VS Code rail. A missed objective is cancelled-equivalent. Parity snapshots carry the epic-parent directive bullet (scripted, `apply-intended-snapshot-change-epic-parent.mjs`).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-19: VS Code 3D text worker failed in the webview (troika `init did not return a callable function`)

The webview's 3D stage logged `Worker module function was called but init did not return a callable function` more than 35 times (VSIX .193, `chunk-StageHost.js`).
- **Cause:** troika-three-text lays out text in a `blob:` Worker and rebuilds each module there with `importScripts(blob: URL)`. A blob worker inherits the page CSP, and `importScripts` is checked against `script-src`, which `worker-src` does not cover.
- The webview's `bundleCsp` `script-src` had no `blob:`, so every module came back `undefined` and every text layout failed. The web app's CSP already allowed `blob:`, which is why the web app was unaffected.
- **Fix:** `blob:` added to `script-src` in `clients/vscode/src/webviewBundleShell.ts`, after a security review. A blob: URL can only be created by code already running in this origin, and its name is an unguessable UUID, so injected markup gains nothing. The accepted cost is that already-running code can turn a string into script this way, which is equivalent to eval.
- **Test:** a regression test pins the exact `script-src` source list.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-19: VS Code "Webview is disposed" uncaught error (VSIX .193 Runtime Status)

Cause: the Visualization panel's KnowledgeBridge posted with `postToWebview(this.panel.webview, …)`. A knowledge review run that outlived the panel then read the `WebviewPanel.webview` getter on a disposed panel, and that getter throws. The same lazy reads, plus view chrome writes after an `await`, existed in several more places. Fixes:
- `WebviewPanelBase` captures the webview once and owns `isDisposed`. `postMessage` on a captured webview returns false after dispose instead of throwing. Messages that arrive after teardown are dropped.
- `VisualizationPanel` and `BuilderForcePanel` post only through the captured webview. A per-session tab no longer repaints or re-registers once it is closed.
- The chat view (`chatView.ts`):
  - It does not build a surface for a view that has already closed.
  - A failed board lookup is reported, and the view shows a localized warning instead of producing unhandled rejections.
  - An intent sent while the lookup is in flight survives that view closing.
- `evermindView` and `voiceMarketplaceView` `sendInit` stop if the view changed while awaiting.
- A `webview.reload` on a disposed webview is logged; any other reload error is reported.
- The silent catches in `WebviewPanelBase.teardown` and `WorkspaceSurface.dispose` now report the error.
- Regression tests: `chatView.test.ts`, `visualizationPanel.test.ts`, `webviewHostBridge.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-19: Agent pipeline — hand-offs, run guards, ratchet integrity, ticket reads, diagnostics (VS Code chats #273, #275)

Triage of two VSIX runs found:
- a `--update` that grandfathered about 11 new react-hooks warnings;
- a plan-role model that mutated files;
- scratch scripts written into the repo, and a full guard suite run twice;
- sub-agents that defaulted to the `code` role and hopped models;
- sub-agents that re-derived their owner's facts, ended on `ask-user` and were marked done, and lost their data;
- a run that promised its report and stopped;
- 13 status-guessing probes, and 5-row pages;
- a ticket opened before any real change;
- a diagnostics report with misleading verdicts and a budget that dropped mutations.

The fixes:
- **0188ec1ea (frontend):** react-hooks `--update` is lower-only (`--allow-raise "<reason>"` to raise). The baseline is restored and the grandfathered warnings are fixed. The silent catch in ImplicatedTicketsSection now reports.
- **2c6a51a2d (run-guards, agent-run, VS Code):**
  - Announced-deliverable steer at settle.
  - A plan turn's mutating `run_command` is re-asked on code (`mutatingShell`).
  - The `git_commit`/`git_push` baseline-raise gate (`baseline-raise:` to override).
  - `$BF_SCRATCH_DIR` for throwaway scripts.
  - An advisory against repeating a full-suite command.
- **fc939c496 (sub-agents):**
  - `role` is required.
  - Per-child model stickiness, released after 2 misses.
  - An owner hand-off block and a coverage/data-file result packet, both redacted and bounded.
  - An ask-user or unkept-claim reply is incomplete and gets one report turn; settle always completes.
  - One `ignoredCacheDir` helper.
- **4d5313506 (diagnostics):**
  - A recovered-failure healthy verdict, matched by target.
  - No verdict mid-run.
  - Latest-run labels and chat totals.
  - Mutation-first budget with a tail reserve.
  - `self-served` staffing.
  - A data-derived plan signal and sub-agent end-state flags.
  - `brainTriage.ts` split.
- **babb3a0cc (tickets):**
  - `tasks.census`.
  - `tasks.list` index pages of 300 rows under a 24K cap scoped to tasks.list's format.
  - The agent-run cap is result-aware.
  - `from_delta` refuses a fileless delta.
  - One `isScratchScriptPath`.
- **Release:** VSIX 2026.10.193, api 2026.10.102, brain-embedded 2026.10.91, brain-ui 2026.10.34, frontend 2026.10.103.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-18: PRD 31 §W10 Security Shield phases 1–4 (browser run tier)

These close the 2026-11-18 browser-run-tier findings, which are tracked out of source control.

**webcontainers**
- **24f6d1d:** SW routing integrity: relay-only attach, id→client and client→preview binding, and a 32 MiB body limit.
- **v2026.11.4:**
  - Identity is assigned at spawn; `SecurityContext` is the record.
  - Port ownership plus the `dependsOn` service graph.
  - An authenticated database gateway with per-service credentials.
  - VFS scoping per service root, with protected paths.
  - Spawn count and depth quotas, attribution for detached children, and `killApplication`.
- **v2026.11.5** (bce8f64, 497bf07, fb6e56f, e24c0b4, dbcf2ef):
  - **Origins:** per-application preview origins, mandatory unless the embedder opts out with `sharedPreviewOrigin: 'unprotected'`; same-origin mode is refused.
  - **Attach:** the nonce is acknowledged and recovers from staleness. Egress is never taken from an attach.
  - **CSP:** the SW stamps the preview CSP plus `nosniff` and `Origin-Agent-Cluster` on every response, and narrows cookie `Domain`. The relay page cannot fetch.
  - **Policy:** signed `?policy=` on worker URLs.
  - **Events:** one `SecurityEvent` / `SecurityEventSink` across every page-side denial.
  - **Limits:** body limits on loopback and host requests, and a WebSocket message cap.
  - **Misc:**
    - page-assigned listening URLs;
    - `messageerror` surfaced as a process error;
    - required per-app identity through every process kind (per-app pip records, a workspace-only PHP platform);
    - stable application ids.

**Builderforce**
- **Incidents:**
  - Migration 1354: a NULLS NOT DISTINCT index for `finding:` and `shield:` refs, plus attestation and evidence columns.
  - The `/api/security/shield-incidents` ingest: developer+, server-side severity covering all 20 reason codes, and a per-project cap.
  - A read-only "Client-attested" badge.
- **Egress and CSP:**
  - The worker egress CSP: no `'self'` or `/__bfwc/`; GitHub read hosts and NuGet read hosts allowed; the .NET worker path-scoped to `/dotnet/`.
  - The CSP-report endpoint plus its CORS preflight.
- **Policy minting:** `POST /api/runtime/worker-policy`. The server derives the origin key and signs a payload bound to tenant, project, application and host (0a0305c19).
- **Bump:** webcontainers ^2026.11.5 with `runtime`, and .NET and Rust providers.
- **Port reallocation:** token-level, propagated to dependents, and declining any service that can't bind.
- **Preview hosts (f4226c68a):**
  - Per-app preview hosts serve exactly the package's README headers.
  - `sw.js` is gated by its signed policy.
  - The `PREVIEW_PER_APP_ORIGINS` flag defaults to off.
  - Every package reason code goes through the shield sink to the incident route, with localized copy in all five locales.
  - Snippets are updated.
- **Per-app origins live, on the free certificate:**
  - The app host is `<key>-preview.builderforce.ai`, one label under the zone, instead of `<key>.preview.builderforce.ai`, which needed a second-level wildcard (Advanced) certificate.
  - The existing `*.builderforce.ai` wildcard (DNS, Universal SSL, the sites Worker's route) delivers it. `isReservedSubdomain` keeps `<32 hex>-preview` from ever being a site, so the sites Worker forwards it to the API. The `*.preview` route is gone.
  - The host shape lives once, in `domain/shared/previewHosts.ts`.
  - `PREVIEW_PER_APP_ORIGINS` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PREVIEW_PER_APP_ORIGINS` are on, so cross-app isolation is in force without an ops step. The same-site trade-off is recorded in make.md › W10 control 1.
  - `release.yml`: `deploy-frontend` now waits for `deploy-api`, which serves the app hosts the frontend opens.
- **Cookie tossing closed:**
  - Same-site preview code could set `Domain=builderforce.ai` cookies that shadow published-site cookies.
  - The site session, site preview, container-preview and A/B cookies are now `__Host-` cookies, through ONE helper (`domain/shared/hostCookie.ts`).
  - Readers prefer the new name and fall back to the legacy one until 2026-12-18. A validated, unambiguous legacy cookie is re-issued as `__Host-` and the legacy one expired, on read.
  - Sign-out collects every value under both names, revokes them all, and deletes both cookies.

**Status on archive (verified 2026-11-18).** These sections describe the hired.video-era email service. Builderforce built the same ideas in a different shape, so every section below is either built or superseded and none is open:
- Provider interface — built: `EmailMessage`/`EmailProvider` (`api/src/infrastructure/email/EmailService.ts:25-34`); Resend is primary over direct `fetch` (`:53-97`), SendPulse is an API-key quota fallback (`:115-168`, `getEmailProvider` `:180-189`). The SendPulse OAuth2 `client_credentials` token flow and `EMAIL_CLIENTID`/`EMAIL_SECRET`/`EMAIL_FROM`/`FRONTEND_URL` no longer exist; the env is `RESEND_API_KEY`, `SENDPULSE_API_KEY`, `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM`, `APP_URL` (`api/src/env.ts:717-724`, `:791`).
- Layout + body templates — superseded by `HEADER` + `footer()` + `deliver()` (`EmailService.ts:261-348`) rendering copy from the five-locale catalog `emailMessages.ts`; `ctaButton` is `cta()` (`:250`).
- Templates 1–4 — superseded: sign-up verification is a 6-digit emailed code (`sendVerificationCodeEmail`, `:389`; `email_otp_challenges`, `api/src/application/auth/EmailVerificationService.ts`); there is no self-serve password reset email — a magic link (`sendMagicLinkEmail`, `:364`) or the admin reset link (`sendAdminPasswordResetEmail`, `:547`) signs the user in; 2FA is TOTP + recovery codes (`/api/auth/mfa/*`, `authRoutes.ts:1082-1138`), not an emailed code. Template 5 is `sendWorkspaceInviteEmail` (`:577`).
- Token tables `email_verification_tokens`, `password_reset_tokens`, `two_factor_codes` — never created here; one-time codes live in `email_otp_challenges`, links in `magic_link_tokens` (`identity.ts:776`).
- Error handling — superseded by `EmailDeliveryError` and the `email_delivery_failures` ledger (`api/src/application/email/sendEmail.ts:100-111`).
- Postmark / non-edge adapters — illustrative only, never planned.
- The fire-and-forget rule and the add-an-email checklist stay in `docs/specs/platform.md` ("Design — Email Implementation Guide").

**Email Implementation Guide** (the doc's opening, kept for context):

This document covers the complete email architecture used in hired.video — provider setup, templates, token management, and patterns for adapting this system to any TypeScript application.

---

#### Architecture Overview

The email system uses a **Provider Interface pattern** to decouple sending logic from the rest of the application. Swapping providers (SendPulse → Resend, Postmark, etc.) means changing a single implementation class.

```
EmailProvider (interface)
    └── SendPulseEmailProvider (implementation)
            └── sendpulse.com REST API (OAuth2 + SMTP endpoint)
```

##### Core types

```typescript
interface EmailMessage {
  to: string;
  subject: string;
  html: string;
  fromName?: string;
  fromEmail?: string;
}

interface EmailProvider {
  send(message: EmailMessage): Promise<void>;
}
```

---

#### SendPulse Setup

##### 1. Create an account and API key

1. Go to [sendpulse.com](https://sendpulse.com) → **Settings → API**
2. Generate a Client ID and Client Secret
3. Verify your sender domain/address under **Email → Senders**

##### 2. Environment variables

```bash
# .env / wrangler secrets
EMAIL_CLIENTID=your_sendpulse_client_id
EMAIL_SECRET=your_sendpulse_client_secret
EMAIL_FROM=noreply@yourdomain.com
FRONTEND_URL=https://yourdomain.com
```

For Cloudflare Workers (wrangler), store secrets via:
```bash
wrangler secret put EMAIL_CLIENTID --env production
wrangler secret put EMAIL_SECRET --env production
```

For non-sensitive values, use `[vars]` in `wrangler.toml`:
```toml
[vars]
EMAIL_FROM = "noreply@yourdomain.com"
FRONTEND_URL = "https://yourdomain.com"
```

##### 3. SendPulse OAuth2 token flow

SendPulse uses OAuth2 `client_credentials` grant. Tokens expire after 3600 seconds. Cache them in memory and refresh 60 seconds before expiry.

```typescript
// Token cache (module-level singleton)
let cachedToken: string | null = null;
let tokenExpiresAt: number | null = null;

async function getSendPulseToken(clientId: string, clientSecret: string): Promise<string> {
  const now = Date.now();
  // Refresh if expired or within 60s of expiry
  if (cachedToken && tokenExpiresAt && now < tokenExpiresAt - 60_000) {
    return cachedToken;
  }

  const response = await fetch('https://api.sendpulse.com/oauth/access_token', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      grant_type: 'client_credentials',
      client_id: clientId,
      client_secret: clientSecret,
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`SendPulse token request failed: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { access_token: string; expires_in: number };
  cachedToken = data.access_token;
  tokenExpiresAt = now + data.expires_in * 1000;
  return cachedToken;
}
```

##### 4. Sending an email via SendPulse SMTP API

SendPulse's SMTP endpoint requires the HTML body base64-encoded.

```typescript
async function sendViaSendPulse(
  message: EmailMessage,
  clientId: string,
  clientSecret: string,
  fromEmail: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const token = await getSendPulseToken(clientId, clientSecret);

  const payload = {
    email: {
      html: btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(message.html))), // base64 encode UTF-8 HTML
      text: '',
      subject: message.subject,
      from: {
        name: message.fromName ?? 'Your App',
        email: message.fromEmail ?? fromEmail,
      },
      to: [{ name: message.to, email: message.to }],
    },
  };

  const response = await fetch('https://api.sendpulse.com/smtp/emails', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const body = await response.text();
    throw new Error(`SendPulse send failed: ${response.status} — ${body}`);
  }
}
```

> **Note on `btoa` encoding:** `btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(html)))` handles non-ASCII characters correctly. In Node.js you can use `Buffer.from(html).toString('base64')` instead.

#### Template System

##### Layout + body composition

All emails share a **layout** (header + footer) with the body swapped per email type. The layout is composed at render time — there are no external template files.

```typescript
const LAYOUT_HEADER = `
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
</head>
<body style="margin:0; padding:0; background:#f8fafc; font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif;">
  <table width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="background:#f8fafc; padding:40px 20px;">
    <tr><td align="center">
      <!-- Header bar -->
      <table width="600" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="background:#1e293b; border-radius:8px 8px 0 0; padding:24px 40px;">
        <tr>
          <td>
            <a href="{{AppUrl}}" style="color:#ffffff; font-size:22px; font-weight:700; text-decoration:none;">
              YourApp
            </a>
          </td>
        </tr>
      </table>
      <!-- Body wrapper -->
      <table width="600" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="background:#ffffff; padding:40px;">
        <tr><td>
`;

const LAYOUT_FOOTER = `
        </td></tr>
      </table>
      <!-- Footer -->
      <table width="600" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="background:#f1f5f9; border-radius:0 0 8px 8px; padding:24px 40px;">
        <tr>
          <td style="color:#64748b; font-size:13px; text-align:center;">
            <p style="margin:0 0 8px;">© {{Year}} YourApp. All rights reserved.</p>
            <p style="margin:0; font-size:12px;">
              You received this email because you have an account at YourApp.<br>
              This is a transactional email — it cannot be unsubscribed from.
            </p>
          </td>
        </tr>
      </table>
    </td></tr>
  </table>
</body>
</html>
`;
```

##### Variable substitution

```typescript
function render(body: string, vars: Record<string, string>): string {
  let out = LAYOUT_HEADER + body + LAYOUT_FOOTER;
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    out = out.replaceAll(`{{${key}}}`, value);
  }
  // Always inject year and app URL
  out = out.replaceAll('{{Year}}', new Date().getFullYear().toString());
  out = out.replaceAll('{{AppUrl}}', process.env.FRONTEND_URL ?? '');
  return out;
}
```

##### Template 1: Email Verification

**Trigger:** User registers
**Variables:** `RecipientName`, `VerifyUrl`

```typescript
const VERIFY_EMAIL_BODY = `
  <h2 style="margin:0 0 8px; color:#1e293b; font-size:24px;">Verify your email</h2>
  <p style="margin:0 0 16px; color:#475569;">Hi {{RecipientName}},</p>
  <p style="margin:0 0 24px; color:#475569; line-height:1.6;">

  <p style="margin:24px 0 0; color:#94a3b8; font-size:13px;">

  </p>
`;

export async function sendVerificationEmail(
  to: string,
  recipientName: string,
  token: string,
  env: Env,
): Promise<void> {
  const verifyUrl = `${env.FRONTEND_URL}/verify-email?token=${token}`;
  const html = render(VERIFY_EMAIL_BODY, {
    RecipientName: recipientName,
    VerifyButton: ctaButton(verifyUrl, 'Verify Email Address'),
  });
  await sendViaSendPulse(
    { to, subject: 'Verify your email address', html },
    env.EMAIL_CLIENTID,
    env.EMAIL_SECRET,
    env.EMAIL_FROM,
  );
}
```

#### Token Management

All one-time tokens follow the same DB pattern.

##### Schema (Drizzle ORM)

```typescript
export const emailVerificationTokens = pgTable('email_verification_tokens', {
  id: uuid('id').defaultRandom().primaryKey(),
  userId: uuid('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  token: varchar('token', { length: 64 }).notNull().unique(),
  expiresAt: timestamp('expires_at').notNull(),
  used: boolean('used').notNull().default(false),
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').notNull().defaultNow(),
});

export const passwordResetTokens = pgTable('password_reset_tokens', {
  id: uuid('id').defaultRandom().primaryKey(),
  userId: uuid('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  token: varchar('token', { length: 64 }).notNull().unique(),
  expiresAt: timestamp('expires_at').notNull(),
  used: boolean('used').notNull().default(false),
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').notNull().defaultNow(),
});

export const twoFactorCodes = pgTable('two_factor_codes', {
  id: uuid('id').defaultRandom().primaryKey(),
  userId: uuid('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  code: varchar('code', { length: 6 }).notNull(),
  expiresAt: timestamp('expires_at').notNull(),
  used: boolean('used').notNull().default(false),
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').notNull().defaultNow(),
});
```

##### Token generation

```typescript
import { randomBytes } from 'crypto'; // Node.js / Cloudflare Workers

function generateToken(bytes: number = 32): string {
  return randomBytes(bytes).toString('hex'); // 64-char hex string
}

function generate2FACode(): string {
  return String(Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000)); // 6-digit numeric
}
```

##### Token validation pattern

```typescript
// Generic: works for email verification, password reset, magic links
async function validateToken(
  db: Database,
  table: TokenTable,
  token: string,
): Promise<{ userId: string } | null> {
  const record = await db.query.table.findFirst({
    where: and(
      eq(table.token, token),
      eq(table.used, false),
      gt(table.expiresAt, new Date()),
    ),
  });

  if (!record) return null;

  // Mark used immediately to prevent replay attacks
  await db.update(table).set({ used: true }).where(eq(table.id, record.id));

  return { userId: record.userId };
}
```

##### Rate limiting resend requests

Prevent resend abuse at the DB level without a cache:

```typescript
async function canResendVerification(db: Database, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const oneMinuteAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 60_000);
  const recent = await db.query.emailVerificationTokens.findFirst({
    where: and(
      eq(emailVerificationTokens.userId, userId),
      gt(emailVerificationTokens.createdAt, oneMinuteAgo),
    ),
    orderBy: desc(emailVerificationTokens.createdAt),
  });
  return !recent; // true = can resend
}
```

---

#### Error Handling Strategy

| Scenario | Handling |
|---|---|
| Token request fails (network) | Throw — caller will catch and log |
| Token request fails (401 bad credentials) | Throw with descriptive message |
| Send fails (invalid email address) | Throw — log, don't retry automatically |
| Send fails (rate limit / 429) | Throw — implement exponential backoff if needed |
| Email send failure on registration | Log, don't fail the registration response (user can resend) |
| Email send failure on password reset | Log — the user will just see "if your email exists, we sent a link" |
| 2FA send failure | Surface as error to user ("Failed to send code — try again") |

#### Adapting to Other Providers

The `EmailProvider` interface makes switching trivial:

##### Resend

```typescript
import { Resend } from 'resend';

class ResendEmailProvider implements EmailProvider {
  private client: Resend;
  constructor(apiKey: string) {
    this.client = new Resend(apiKey);
  }
  async send(message: EmailMessage): Promise<void> {
    await this.client.emails.send({
      from: message.fromEmail ?? 'noreply@yourdomain.com',
      to: message.to,
      subject: message.subject,
      html: message.html,
    });
  }
}
```

##### Postmark

```typescript
import * as postmark from 'postmark';

class PostmarkEmailProvider implements EmailProvider {
  private client: postmark.ServerClient;
  constructor(serverToken: string) {
    this.client = new postmark.ServerClient(serverToken);
  }
  async send(message: EmailMessage): Promise<void> {
    await this.client.sendEmail({
      From: message.fromEmail ?? 'noreply@yourdomain.com',
      To: message.to,
      Subject: message.subject,
      HtmlBody: message.html,
    });
  }
}
```

##### Provider factory

```typescript
function getEmailProvider(env: Env): EmailProvider {
  switch (env.EMAIL_PROVIDER ?? 'sendpulse') {
    case 'resend':
      return new ResendEmailProvider(env.RESEND_API_KEY);
    case 'postmark':
      return new PostmarkEmailProvider(env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN);
    case 'sendpulse':
    default:
      return new SendPulseEmailProvider(env.EMAIL_CLIENTID, env.EMAIL_SECRET, env.EMAIL_FROM);
  }
}
```

---

#### Adapting to Non-Edge Runtimes

##### Node.js / Express

- Replace `c.executionCtx.waitUntil(...)` with `Promise.resolve().then(...)` or a job queue (BullMQ, etc.)
- Replace `btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(html)))` with `Buffer.from(html).toString('base64')`
- Replace `randomBytes` import from `'crypto'` (already the same)
- Token caching in module-level variables works as-is

##### Next.js (App Router)

- Use `after()` (Next.js 15+) or a background job for fire-and-forget email
- Keep the service layer as-is; just inject env vars from `process.env`

### Multi-Auth Implementation Guide: finished sections archived on consolidation (2026-11-18)

Source: docs/guides/MULTI_AUTH_IMPLEMENTATION.md

**Status on archive (verified 2026-11-18).** Built. The routes were ported from this guide and still carry its comments: `api/src/presentation/routes/oauthRoutes.ts` (providers `:79-139`, signed state `:165-205` over `infrastructure/auth/oauthState.ts`, initiate `:308`, callback `:356`, magic link `:609`/`:675`, `linked-accounts` `:725`, `unlink` `:749`, `add-password` `:782`); tables `oauth_accounts` and `magic_link_tokens` (`api/src/infrastructure/database/schema/identity.ts:753`, `:776`); PBKDF2-SHA256 100k (`api/src/infrastructure/auth/HashService.ts:54`, `:62`); pages `frontend/src/app/auth/callback/page.tsx` and `frontend/src/app/auth/magic-link/page.tsx`; the Settings connect button sends `link_token` (`frontend/src/lib/auth/credentials.ts:286`). Drift from the text below, all deliberate:
- The callback never puts the JWT in the URL: it redirects to `/auth/callback?code=` with a 60-second exchange code, swapped at `POST /api/auth/oauth/exchange` (`oauthRoutes.ts:535-604`).
- The web JWT (`signWebJwt`, `api/src/infrastructure/auth/JwtService.ts:163`) lives 24 h (30 days with "trust this device"), carries `{ sub, email, username, sa?, act?, jti, sid, mfa?, amr }`, and every issued token is persisted as a revocable session (`persistWebSessionToken`, `auth_user_sessions`/`auth_tokens`, `identity.ts:217`, `:230`).
- Password login is `POST /api/auth/web/login` with TOTP MFA (`authRoutes.ts:651`, `:740`); sign-up verification is an emailed 6-digit code (`email_otp_challenges`); `refresh_tokens`, `email_verification_tokens`, `password_reset_tokens`, `two_factor_codes` were never created.
- `users` has `display_name`, `username`, `email_verified_at`, `is_suspended`, `locale`, `account_type` instead of `name`, `email_verified`, `role`, `is_active`; there is no `job_seeker` default role.
- `API_URL` is not used (callback from the request origin); `FRONTEND_URL` is `APP_URL`; `redirect` is open-redirect-guarded; the chosen locale and the return origin ride the signed state.
The Security Checklist, Environment Variables and Provider Setup sections stay in `docs/specs/platform.md` ("Design — Multi-Auth Implementation Guide") with this drift corrected.

**Multi-Auth Implementation Guide** (the doc's opening, kept for context; its Table of Contents is dropped):

A complete reference for implementing email/password, OAuth social login, and magic link authentication in a Hono + Cloudflare Workers + Drizzle ORM + React SPA stack. Every pattern here is derived from a working production implementation.

---

#### Architecture Overview

```
Browser
  │
  ├─ Email/Password ──────────────────────────────▶ POST /api/auth/login
  │                                                  Returns JWT in JSON body
  │
  ├─ OAuth (login/signup) ────────────────────────▶ GET /api/auth/oauth/:provider?redirect=/dashboard
  │                                                  302 → provider consent screen
  │                                                  Provider → GET /api/auth/oauth/:provider/callback
  │                                                  API finds/creates user by email, issues JWT
  │                                                  302 → /auth/callback?token=JWT
  │                                                  Frontend page writes token to localStorage
  │
  ├─ OAuth (connect from Settings) ───────────────▶ GET /api/auth/oauth/:provider?redirect=/settings&link_token=JWT
  │                                                  JWT is verified, userId embedded in HMAC state
  │                                                  Provider → GET /api/auth/oauth/:provider/callback
  │                                                  API links provider to existing user (no email lookup)
  │                                                  302 → /auth/callback?token=NEW_JWT
  │
  └─ Magic Link ──────────────────────────────────▶ POST /api/auth/magic-link
                                                     Email sent with /auth/magic-link?token=...
                                                     Frontend page calls GET /api/auth/magic-link/verify
                                                     Returns JWT in JSON body
```

**Key design decisions:**

- JWT stored in `localStorage` (not HttpOnly cookies) — required if you also support a browser extension or non-browser clients that share the same API
- OAuth state is HMAC-signed (no DB) — works correctly in stateless edge runtimes
- `passwordHash` is nullable — users who sign up via OAuth have no password
- Magic link tokens are single-use and invalidated immediately on verify
- All "not found" paths return the same generic message to prevent email enumeration
- Connect flow (adding a provider to an existing account) uses `link_token` to bypass email matching — critical when the provider email differs from the account email

---

#### Database Schema

##### Core users table

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email           VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name            VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  password_hash   TEXT,                         -- NULL for OAuth-only users
  email_verified  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  role            VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'job_seeker',
  is_active       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  is_suspended    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  mfa_enabled     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  last_login_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

##### OAuth accounts (one user → many providers)

```sql
CREATE TABLE oauth_accounts (
  id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id             UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provider            VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,   -- 'google' | 'linkedin' | 'github' | 'microsoft'
  provider_account_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,   -- the `sub` or `id` from the provider
  email               VARCHAR(255),
  display_name        VARCHAR(255),
  avatar_url          TEXT,
  access_token        TEXT,
  refresh_token       TEXT,
  token_expires_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  scope               TEXT,
  created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

##### Magic link tokens

```sql
CREATE TABLE magic_link_tokens (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  token      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  used       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  redirect   VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '/dashboard',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

##### Supporting tables (also needed)

```sql
-- Tracks active sessions; populated on every login
CREATE TABLE refresh_tokens (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  revoked    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Email verification tokens
CREATE TABLE email_verification_tokens (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  used       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Password reset tokens
CREATE TABLE password_reset_tokens (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  used       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- TOTP / email 2FA codes
CREATE TABLE two_factor_codes (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  code       VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  used       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

---

#### Password Authentication

##### Hashing — PBKDF2 via Web Crypto API

Works natively in Cloudflare Workers (no bcrypt npm dependency needed).

```typescript
async function hashPassword(password: string): Promise<string> {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
  const keyMaterial = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    "raw", encoder.encode(password), "PBKDF2", false, ["deriveBits"]
  );
  const bits = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(
    { name: "PBKDF2", salt, iterations: 100_000, hash: "SHA-256" },
    keyMaterial, 256
  );
  const saltHex = Array.from(salt).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
  const hashHex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(bits)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
  return `${saltHex}:${hashHex}`;
}

async function verifyPassword(password: string, stored: string | null | undefined): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!stored) return false;           // OAuth-only accounts have no password
  const [saltHex, hashHex] = stored.split(":");
  if (!saltHex || !hashHex) return false;
  const salt = new Uint8Array(saltHex.match(/.{2}/g)!.map(b => parseInt(b, 16)));
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const keyMaterial = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    "raw", encoder.encode(password), "PBKDF2", false, ["deriveBits"]
  );
  const bits = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(
    { name: "PBKDF2", salt, iterations: 100_000, hash: "SHA-256" },
    keyMaterial, 256
  );
  const candidateHex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(bits)).map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
  return candidateHex === hashHex;
}
```

> **Note:** Always return the same error message for wrong email AND wrong password — `"Invalid email or password"`. Never leak which one was wrong.

##### Login endpoint

```typescript
// POST /api/auth/login
app.post("/login", async (c) => {
  const { email, password } = await c.req.json();

  const [user] = await db.select().from(users)
    .where(eq(users.email, email.toLowerCase()))
    .limit(1);

  if (!user || !user.isActive) {
    return c.json({ error: "Invalid email or password" }, 401);
  }

  const valid = await verifyPassword(password, user.passwordHash);
  if (!valid) {
    return c.json({ error: "Invalid email or password" }, 401);
  }

  // Optional: 2FA step (see auth.ts)

  const token = await createJwt(user.id, user.email, user.role, !!user.emailVerified);
  return c.json({ token, user: { id: user.id, email: user.email } });
});
```
