#### D14. People scores for managers

*Decided 2026-11-06: managers need people scored.* This covers humans and agents alike.
An agent is a first-class worker here: the manager is an agent, and agents are hired and
unhired. The section defines how scoring is done fairly enough to act on.

**D14.1 Attribution.** Every run records its roles:
- `requester`: who started it;
- `approvers`;
- `reviewer` (PRD 23);
- `agent`: the executing agent;
- `manager`: the supervising manager agent, if any.

Each outcome label (D1) and each delta finding is attributed to every role on the run, and
a score is always reported **per role**. Being the approver of a reverted run is a different
fact from being its requester.

**D14.2 Measures** per person or agent, per role, per period (rolling 90 days):

| Measure | Definition |
|---|---|
| Run quality | Share of runs whose headline is `worse` |
| Follow-up-fix rate | `followup-fix` labels ÷ final-labelled runs |
| Revert rate | `reverted` ÷ final-labelled runs |
| Integrity rate | Runs with a C8.2 error ÷ runs. Agents mainly. |
| Security introductions | Introduced measured security errors per run |
| Review rejection rate | `review-rejected` ÷ runs with a PR |
| Fix effectiveness | Share of *Fix with agent* runs whose finding is resolved in the next delta |
| Approval accuracy (approvers) | Share of approved runs not later `reverted` or `followup-fix` |

**D14.3 Risk adjustment: observed ÷ expected.** Raw rates punish whoever takes the hard
work. Each rate is **indirectly standardized**, the method used for hospital standardized
mortality ratios:

```
E = Σ_{runs of p} P̂(outcome | case-mix features)       O = observed count
SR = O / E          95% CI: exact Poisson (Garwood) on O, divided by E
```

- The **case-mix model** (`ml/tasks/case_mix`) is a separate logistic model of the same form
  as D5. It uses every factor **outside the scored person's control in their role**:
  - *change* features: size, entropy, centrality, entry points, churn, layer and dimension
    flags;
  - for human roles, also the **executing agent and model tier**. A requester or approver is
    not penalized for an agent's quality.
- It deliberately **excludes the scored person's own identity and experience features**.
  Otherwise it would explain away the very person effect being measured.
- It is trained in WS22 from the WS16 labels. It does not wait for the D5 gate.
- The D5 risk model may use experience features for prediction. The two models are
  different by design.

**D14.4 Shrinkage.** Small samples are pulled toward the team. The rate posterior is
Gamma–Poisson (empirical Bayes):

```
λ_p | data ~ Gamma(α₀ + O, β₀ + E)        shown: posterior mean of λ_p and its 95% interval
```

- The prior comes from everyone in the same tenant and role.
- **Minimum sample.** Below 20 final-labelled runs in the window, the score is
  `insufficient-data` and is not shown.
- **Shrinkage still matters above the minimum.** A person with 25 runs is pulled toward the
  team average in proportion to their small expected count, rather than showing an extreme
  rate.
- **One interval rule.** The posterior interval is 95%, matching the inner funnel limit. The
  99.8% funnel limit is used only to call a point "outside limits".

**D14.5 Presentation.**
- **Funnel plot** (Spiegelhalter, 2005): standardized ratio against expected volume, with
  95% and 99.8% control limits. Only points outside the limits are called out.
- A ranked table is never the default view. When a table is shown, it is sorted by the
  posterior, with the interval drawn, and an "outside limits" flag.
- Every score links to the runs behind it and their deltas, so a manager can see *why*.
- The trend per person uses the D7 control charts: is this person's ratio drifting?
- **Surface.** A **People** view on the team (`dev_teams`) page, which is the only
  manager-to-reports structure. It is not the ticket "Sign-off & Accountability" tab
  (`AccountabilityTab.tsx`), which is per ticket. The manager agent reads the same scores
  through an application port for its coaching and stall-triage loop.
- The manager agent may use agent scores to route work and to coach. It may not act on a
  *human's* score automatically.

**D14.6 Access and audit.**
- **Reporting line.** Today's only reporting line is `dev_teams.manager_id` → contributors
  (`schema/canvas.ts:850`).
  - WS22 adds one application-layer policy, `mayViewPersonScore(viewer, subject)`.
  - It resolves a contributor to the user and agent identities that runs record. Where that
    mapping is missing, WS22 adds it as an id reference, not a copied table.
  - The server enforces the policy in the route. The frontend `RoleGate` only disables the UI.
  - `resolveMembership` (private in `gatewayAccess.ts:128`) is not reused for this; it answers
    a different question.
- **Who sees what:**
  - a person sees their own scores;
  - a manager sees their team's contributors;
  - a tenant admin sees everyone in the tenant;
  - superadmin sees nothing cross-tenant without the existing audited cross-tenant scope.
- Every view of another person's score is audit-logged (viewer, subject, time).
- **Human scoring is off by default for enterprise plans** and on by default for others.
  - A tenant admin can switch it on or off.
  - Enabling it on an enterprise tenant shows a DPIA notice: lawful basis, purpose limited to
    coaching and capacity, and the works-council consultation the tenant owns.
  - Agent scoring cannot be disabled.
- **Data-subject rights.**
  - A person can export their own scores, inputs and the audit rows about them (access).
  - On erasure, their person scores and person-feature values are deleted. Their identity in
    run roles is pseudonymized, so aggregate models are not invalidated. Audit rows keep the
    pseudonym.
- No automatic consequence follows from a human score: no blocking, no reassignment and no
  notification to others.

**D14.7 Done-checks.**
- [ ] A person with 3 runs shows `insufficient-data`. A person with 25 runs, all
      high-risk, does not come out worse than the team on raw size alone (a case-mix test).
- [ ] An approver whose runs all used a weak agent and model tier is not flagged when the
      agent is the cause (a case-mix test).
- [ ] A unit test on the case-mix feature schema enforces that it contains none of the scored
      person's identity or experience features.
- [ ] Erasure: after the person's erasure request, their scores and person features are gone
      and their run roles are pseudonymized.
- [ ] An enterprise tenant has human scoring off by default.
- [ ] A manager cannot see a non-report's score (an RBAC test), and each view writes an
      audit row.
- [ ] With the tenant setting off, every human-score endpoint returns 404 for that tenant.
      Agent scores are unaffected.

#### D15. Adoption order

| Phase | Ships | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | D0 rule and guard, D1 labels pipeline, D2 deterministic statistics, D13 package | WS7 (the delta exists) |
| P2 | D3 rule precision, D4 calibration, D7 statistical process control | About 4 weeks of votes and runs |
| P3 | D5 risk model, survival view, D10.2 similar runs | At least 500 final-labelled runs (global) |
| P4 | D9 scheduling, D10.1 ranking | WS12 (the optional tier exists) and click data |
| P5 | D6 naturalness, D8 reliability growth | A logprob-capable local model; at least 10 runs per dimension |
| P2–P3 | D14 people scores: case-mix model, then views | WS16 labels; at least 20 final-labelled runs per scored person |

### 6. Sequences

**Open a folder, offline.**
activate (policy `local-only`) → `backgroundIndexer.start(root)` → reconcile plan, using the
stat prefilter and the git fast path → L0 published → visible and open files extracted (L1)
→ visualizer opens on `localSession` and renders L0/L1 → L2 rules → L3 analyzers from the
bundled tools → snapshot projection → codebaseScan projection files written. Zero
platform requests.

**Edit a file.**
watcher event → 100 ms coalesce → stat changed → hash → facts changed?
- No (early cutoff): done.
- Yes: file rules → neighbourhood rules for 1-hop neighbours → global rules whose read kinds
  changed → derived traces updated → visualizer receives the changed nodes and findings.

**Agent run.**
run start → `runChangeBaseline` (+ dirty pre-images) → the indexer keeps running → run ends →
`recordChangeSetAroundRun` finalizes → `computeRunDelta`:
1. Resolve before facts (C1 steps 1–3).
2. Compute the impact set.
3. Run the static rules per dimension.
4. Run L3 analyzers on the after side, and on the before side via cache or the materialized
   tree.
5. Match lineage.
6. Apply comparability.
7. Compute verdicts, the headline and the blast radius.

Then the card is posted to the chat in "measuring" state and filled as each analyzer settles.
After that: an optional narrative, then the delta is stored as a local record, with sync if
granted. A policy check on autonomous runs can then block finalization.


Source: `docs/specs/41-prd-offline-understanding-and-run-delta.md` lines 1984–2043.

### 8. Done-checks

**Part A**
- [ ] The packaged VSIX passes A6 with egress denied: zero BuilderForce and zero npm requests.
      The graph renders, a local-model run completes and a delta appears.
- [ ] Signed out with a persisted project selection, a review completes on the local store
      (regression test for `NOT_SIGNED_IN`).
- [ ] No view or command uses `builderforce.signedIn` except account-only ones, as listed in
      the capability table. A guard script fails on a new `signedIn` `when` clause outside an
      allowlist.

**Part B**
- [ ] Warm plan of the `agentic` tree takes under 3 s; cold plan in git under 30 s.
- [ ] Saving one file in a 16k-file tree: p95 under 200 ms to updated L1/L2 facts for that
      file. Global rules are skipped when the read fact kinds did not change (asserted by a
      trace test).
- [ ] Determinism oracle (B8.6): the `canonicalDump` of the incremental store equals the
      scratch build and equals a second OS (Windows with autocrlf), byte for byte, over 500
      seeded edit sequences.
- [ ] A body-only edit reruns `body`-reading rules (for example `io-in-loop`) and skips
      `structure`-only rules (a trace test).
- [ ] The repo's own `.gitignore` is untouched, and `.builderforce/cache/.gitignore` contains
      `*`.
- [ ] `scan.json` and its version token are gone. `codebaseScan` tests pass unchanged against
      the projection.
- [ ] An analyzer failure shows as `not_measured` with a reason, never as zero findings.

**Part C**
- [ ] A clone group gaining a member reads as `changed (grew)`, not resolved plus introduced.
- [ ] A fixture run that removes `requireAuth` from a route gives security `worse` with
      `guard-removed` and the route key in evidence.
- [ ] A fixture run that adds `.skip` to a test and loosens a matcher gives quality `worse`
      with the headline "tests were weakened".
- [ ] A fixture run that adds an awaited DB call inside a `.map` gives `io-in-loop`.
- [ ] A fixture run that changes an exported signature gives `ilities.compatibility`
      `api-breaking`.
- [ ] An analyzer version bump between sides makes that kind `not_comparable` and emits no
      introduced or resolved entries.
- [ ] The same before/after on Windows and Linux CI gives the same `RunDelta.digest`.
- [ ] SARIF export validates against the 2.1.0 schema, and `baselineState` round-trips through
      import.
- [ ] Static tier p95 under 10 s for runs touching 50 files or fewer on the `agentic` tree.
      The card shows "measuring" rows until L3 settles.
- [ ] Card and panel are localized in 5 catalogs, readable in both themes and free of
      horizontal overflow at 360 px.

**Part D**
- [ ] `check:run-delta-layers` fails when any `verdict/` file imports `predict/`. A fixture
      shows a high predicted risk leaving every verdict unchanged.
- [ ] The same features and model artifact give a byte-identical `Prediction` on Windows and
      Linux CI, offline.
- [ ] Below the data threshold, every model returns `insufficient-data` and the card shows
      nothing for it.
- [ ] The leakage guard fails a fixture feature that reads data later than `finalizedAt`.
- [ ] SZZ labeller: on a fixture history with a known fix-inducing run, that run gets
      `followup-fix`. A comment-only later edit does not.
- [ ] Chapman estimate: unit tests against textbook values. `m < 3` gives
      `insufficient-data`.
- [ ] Rule precision: a rule with 3 votes is never demoted. A rule with 200 votes at 30%
      precision is demoted, and its per-repo posterior shrinks toward the global one.
- [ ] Risk model replaces `v1` only when it passes the D5.3 gate. The gate result is
      recorded in the model card.
- [ ] `prefetch/calibrate.ts` and the learned-routing sampler import from `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory/stats`.
      No second implementation remains (grep check). Their existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The SPRT stops early on a fixture with a 20% regression, and runs to the maximum on a
      no-change fixture.

### 9. Non-goals

- Full-precision inter-procedural taint analysis or symbolic execution. Taint-lite is a
  heuristic signal. Deep analysis comes in through SARIF from Semgrep or CodeQL when
  installed.
- Running the project's full test suite or build by default. The dynamic tier is opt-in or
  policy-driven, runs only in a trusted workspace, and never runs in the user's working tree
  (C6.2 "Safety and trust").
- Proving functional correctness. The delta reports measured change, not whether the feature
  is right. Acceptance evidence (PRD 23/37) stays the place for that.
- Replacing the knowledge review's docs judgement. L4 is unchanged except for caching and
  capability gating.


Source: `docs/specs/41-prd-offline-understanding-and-run-delta.md` lines 2124–2166.

### 10. Measure

- **Use.**
  - The share of runs that produce a delta, by entry point: VSIX, cloud, web.
  - Delta cards opened, and panel opens per card.
  - Offline sessions, meaning sessions with the platform denied for their whole life. These
    are counted locally and reported in the next granted sync batch.
- **Value.**
  - Fix-with-agent clicks from delta findings, and the share that resolve the finding in the
    follow-up run's delta.
  - Introduced error-level findings caught per 100 runs, split by dimension.
  - Autonomous runs blocked by policy that were later confirmed as correct blocks.
  - Integrity findings (C8.2) per 100 autonomous runs, trending down as prompts and policies
    adapt.
- **Precision.** The Beta posterior precision per rule (D3). Demotion and restoration follow
  its credible bounds, and demoted rules are listed for rework.
- **Prediction quality.** For each model:
  - Brier score, ECE and PR-AUC on the trailing 30 days;
  - Popt for run risk;
  - NDCG@5 for ranking;
  - coverage of the KM interval;
  - PSI drift.

  Report also the share of verdict-changing optional checks the scheduler ran versus random
  scheduling, and the count of labelled runs per week, which gates P3.
- **Cost.**
  - Plan time.
  - Per-save update latency.
  - Indexer CPU share.
  - Delta p50/p95 per tier.
  - Cache hit rate for extract, rules and analyzers.
  - Pre-image bytes per run.
- **Kill condition.** After 8 weeks, if fewer than 15% of delta cards are opened **and**
  "mark as wrong" exceeds 30% across rules, cut the scope back to quality and integrity (C8)
  plus security `guard-removed`, `secret` and `capability-added`. Retire the rest.
- **Kill condition for Part D.** Each model stands or falls on its own:
  - **Run risk:** if it has not passed the D5.3 gate after 2,000 final labels, retire it and
    keep `v1`.
  - **Ranking:** if it does not beat severity-then-centrality ordering on NDCG@5 after 8
    weeks, retire it.
  - **Naturalness:** if fewer than 5% of "unusual" lines appear in later `followup-fix` blame,
    retire it.

### 13. Methodology references

- Local-first software — Kleppmann, Wiggins, van Hardenberg, McGranaghan (Ink & Switch, 2019).
- *Build Systems à la Carte* — Mokhov, Mitchell, Peyton Jones (ICFP 2018): verifying traces,
  early cutoff.
- Salsa / rust-analyzer; rustc red-green incremental queries.
- Merkle trees; git's index and the racy-git problem.
- tree-sitter incremental parsing; GitHub stack graphs (file-incremental name binding); SCIP.
- Datalog semi-naive evaluation; DRed (deletion and re-derivation); CodeQL and Meta Glean as
  fact-plus-rule code models.
- Tarjan's SCC; PageRank for code centrality (as in Aider's repo map).
- Attack-surface metric — Manadhata and Wing (IEEE TSE 2011); STRIDE (Microsoft threat
  modelling); taint analysis (source, sink, sanitizer).
- ISO/IEC 25010:2023 product quality model.
- Robert C. Martin's package metrics (Ca, Ce, instability, abstractness).
- Change coupling and hotspots — Tornhill, *Your Code as a Crime Scene*; Gall et al. on
  logical coupling.
- Wilcoxon signed-rank test, paired Hodges–Lehmann estimator, paired bootstrap CIs for
  interleaved benchmark comparison.
- Mutation testing (StrykerJS incremental mode).
- SARIF 2.1.0 (OASIS): `baselineState`, `partialFingerprints`.
- Just-in-time defect prediction — Kamei et al. (IEEE TSE 2013); McIntosh and Kamei (TSE 2018);
  effort-aware evaluation (Popt).
- SZZ — Śliwerski, Zimmermann and Zeller (MSR 2005).
- Change entropy — Hassan (ICSE 2009).
- Naturalness — Hindle et al. (ICSE 2012); Ray et al., "On the Naturalness of Buggy Code"
  (ICSE 2016).
- Maintainability Index — Oman and Hagemeister (1992); Halstead (1977).
- Capture–recapture — Lincoln–Petersen; Chapman (1951); its use in software inspection by
  Eick et al. (1992).
- Goel–Okumoto NHPP software reliability growth (1979).
- Beta–Binomial, empirical Bayes and hierarchical shrinkage — Efron and Morris.
- Platt scaling (1999); isotonic regression (Zadrozny and Elkan 2002); Brier score; ECE
  (Guo et al. 2017).
- Kaplan–Meier (1958) with Greenwood's variance; Cox proportional hazards (1972).
- EWMA (Roberts 1959); CUSUM (Page 1954); Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams and
  MacKay 2007).
- Mahalanobis distance; Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage (2004); population stability index.
- Thompson sampling (1933; Agrawal and Goyal 2012); Laplace approximation for Bayesian logistic
  regression.
- Wald's sequential probability ratio test (1945).
- Indirect standardization (standardized mortality ratio); Garwood exact Poisson intervals;
  funnel plots for institutional comparison — Spiegelhalter (Statistics in Medicine, 2005);
  Gamma–Poisson empirical Bayes.
- Pairwise learning to rank (RankNet, Burges 2005); unbiased LTR with inverse propensity
  weighting (Joachims et al. 2017); NDCG.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-17: the WebContainers ML modules ship (2026.10.14), and Studio uses them (studio 2026.11.2)

- **WebContainers 2026.10.14 is on npm.** The phase 1–8 ML modules (inference, adaptive, memory, prefetch, kvcache, learning) now live under the `./ml` subpath, and the root export is back to the dev runtime only. The worker bundle is `./ml/worker.js`.
- **Review fixes in the package:**
  - The worker bundle no longer overwrites `worker.js`.
  - An AbortSignal is no longer posted to the worker.
  - The SIMD probe works.
  - Prefetch, kv-cache and learner state are bounded.
  - The IndexedDB helper handles blocked, versionchange and late-success opens without leaking.
  - `createModelCache` gained `valueFormat: 'raw'` and custom db/store names.
- **Studio's weight cache** goes through `createModelCache` on the same `builderforce-studio-weights` database. It still stores raw ArrayBuffers, so old and new builds read each other's entries.
- **Session budget:** `SessionResidency` (`createMemoryManager`) budgets live ORT sessions at 0.8 × the device memory hint and reports pressure and headroom. Sessions are pinned for life and never evicted.
- **Refinement weight warm:** `WeightPrefetch` (`createPrefetcher`) runs only when a refinement model is set.
  - It warms one file at a time, only while the engine is idle (`EngineActivity` around `generate` / `generateStoryboard`).
  - A warm that is in flight when generation starts is cancelled and requeued.
  - It pauses under memory pressure.
  - It skips any file whose size × 2 exceeds the headroom.
  - It retries a transient persist failure once.
  - It never overlaps draft generation, which is an OOM risk for multi-GB UNet weights.
- **Out of scope by design:** kvcache, knowledge memory, the inference client, the adaptive controller and the learner. Studio runs no local text LLM.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-16: the progress guard no longer pauses a finished, verified run (VS Code 2026.10.187)

- Chat #146477: the run edited AuthShell, the login page and the register page, and `tsc` passed, yet three progress checks fired and parked it on `ask_user`. The second check's change-tools-only turn made the model invent an edit.
- **Batched edits now count.** `packages/agent-tools/src/callShape.ts` is the one reader of which files a call changes, re-exported by run-guards `callChanges.ts`. It covers `edit_file({edits:[…]})` and the `file_path` aliases, and normalises paths. editRevert, noProgress, progressDetector, writeLedger and `editedFilesOf` all use it.
- A check pass must come from a real runner (`run-guards/src/checkCommand.ts`). It replaces the loose `TEST_COMMAND` regex, which matched `ls tests/`.
- **Background checks now count.** The detector remembers the job ids of background check commands and judges the `command_status` poll that reports the result.
- **New `finish` action.** `verifiedWork.ts` marks a run verified once a write is followed by a passing check. A pass must come from a real test or type-check runner, and git bookkeeping does not count as a write.
  - On a verified run, the first trip is a steer: finish if done, otherwise make the next change.
  - From the second trip on, the run gets a no-tools final turn on its own model. It is bound in brain-embedded, in agent-run's guards and kernel, and in the cloud adapter.
  - A repeated finish falls back to the normal escalate-then-pause ladder.
- **No forced edits after a change.** `forcedProgressTurn` no longer forces change-tools-only turns once the run has changed code.
- `handOffForcedClash.e2e.test.ts` was updated for the read-only-streak escalation that shipped on 2026-11-15.
- Tests: `progressFinish.test.ts` in run-guards and agent-run, and `progressGuard.finish.test.ts`. They include a regression replay of the incident.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-15: "Retry analyzers" really re-runs them

- **On-disk cache:** a fresh job wraps the worker's on-disk analyzer cache in `writeOnlyBinding()`, so reads miss and writes replace the old entries. The in-thread fallback passes `fresh` to `analyseWorkspace`'s own cache too.
- **Real key:** `shaCache.getOrRun(key, work, signal, { fresh })` starts a new run over a cached or in-flight entry and replaces it; later askers join it.
- **One fresh run per key:** `l3FreshHold.ts` tracks started keys per hold, so a prefetch can neither steal the retry's fresh pass nor start a second worker for the same key. A run without `l3RootPath` can't stand in for the retry. The ticket returns as soon as every asker stops, or on failure.
- **Old quarantine records:** `sha: null` records without `until` get the 24 h expiry on load (undatable ones are dropped), which also fixes a `q.sha!.slice` TypeError.
- Tests: `l3FreshRetry.test.ts`, plus new cases in `l3CrashGuard.test.ts` and `shaCache.test.ts`.
- Residuals closed: every null-key ask under a hold runs fresh; a fresh run whose result isn't kept (`keepOf`) returns its ticket; a prefetch still in flight when the retry arrives keeps its own askers while the retry gets an equipped fresh run that later asks join.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-15: the extension host no longer crashes every ~13 minutes, and the heavy analyzers run only on demand (VS Code 2026.10.174, installed)

- **Cause, from 25+ Crashpad minidumps:** every dump showed 0xE0000008 (Chromium OOM) on a Node `WorkerThread`, with a failed allocation of 0x93ffffc0. That is V8 `ValueSerializer` growth: the L3 worker posted its whole `WorkspaceExtracted` for a ~20k-file scope in one `postMessage`.
  - Worker `resourceLimits` don't bound off-heap serializer buffers, so the failed allocation killed the whole host and every chat with it.
  - The host had about 8.6 GB committed at the crash.
  - It looped because `c:/code/agentic` isn't a git repo, and a dead host records no failure.
- **Fix:** `a8af9c8dc` + `d8af13ef9`:
  - `workers/boundedTransfer.ts` is ONE bounded transfer: 8 MB parts, a 2× JSON size estimate, a 256 MB budget, and an oversize item counts as over-budget. The L3, run-delta and TypeScript-analyzer workers all use it.
  - `l3CrashGuard.ts` writes a persisted in-flight sentinel. A host that died mid-pass quarantines that root (git: until the sha moves; non-git: 24 h). The sentinel is cleared on a clean shutdown. OOM and over-budget count as permanent failures.
  - **BuilderForce: Retry Code Analyzers** lists the quarantined roots and lifts the chosen one.
  - **User decision:** the heavy L3 analyzers run only on demand (knowledge view, review, chat code action), never on idle.
  - A failed analyzer counts as a failed pass, and sub-folder roots analyse only their sub-folder.
  - The gate is single-flight. Retries wait for idle after the session's first reconcile, and an explicit retry forces a pass.
- **Reviews:** three Opus rounds found nothing blocking, and the findings were fixed. Typecheck is clean and 113 targeted tests pass. The VSIX was built with the source unchanged during the build (hashes verified) and is installed as 2026.10.174.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-14: the knowledge plan no longer runs its ignore matching and fact load as one long block (builderforce-memory 2026.10.81, released and consumed)

- **Review:** Opus found no blocking issues (0 mismatches against the old matcher over 600k randomized rule sets). Its 2 low findings were fixed before release. The fallback yield is captured at load and uses `MessageChannel` / `scheduler.yield` before `setTimeout(0)`, so hidden browser tabs don't throttle it. New `cooperative.test.ts` covers it.
- **Release:** builderforce-memory `608ec6b`, tag `v2026.10.81`. Release and CI passed, and npm `latest` = 2026.10.81 (memory + memory-mcp + MCP registry).

- **Cause, from 30 VS Code CPU profiles:** VS Code flagged the extension host unresponsive 110 times on 2026-11-14, 108 of them blamed on BuilderForce, with blocks of up to 12 s.
  - `ignoreMatcher` regex-tested every rule × every ancestor folder × every file: about 88 s of CPU over a 34,588-file multi-repo workspace.
  - The derived-facts load read every fact object in one synchronous `getObjects` call: about 30 s.
- **Fix (`packages/memory/src/knowledge/`):**
  - `ignoreMatcher.ts` (extracted from `sources.ts`): semantics unchanged (last matching rule wins; a negation still re-includes). Each folder caches the highest rule that hit it or an ancestor, plus the rules still live below it, so nested `.gitignore` rules drop out outside their base. A literal prefix/suffix check runs before any regex.
  - `cooperative.ts`: ONE 12 ms yield budget (`setImmediate` or `setTimeout(0)`; portable to browsers). It is used in `plan.ts` (walk, classify loop, before the merkle step) and in `rules/factStore.ts` `loadOnce`.
  - `getObjects` now runs in batches of 512. The result is identical and in the same order.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-14: agent commits no longer open Terminal/CMD windows on Windows (VS Code 2026.10.171)

- **Cause, proven by a live window and process trace:** `cmd.exe /d /s /c vitest run src/brainRunStore.test.ts` ← `Code.exe` running npx-cli.js ← extension host.
  - Since 54812ae25, `verify/execRunner.ts` `launchPlan` ran npm/npx as `process.execPath`. Inside VS Code that is `Code.exe`, a GUI-subsystem binary, so `windowsHide` gives it no console at all.
  - npx's unhidden `cmd` child therefore got a new visible console, which Windows Terminal opened.
  - `runDelta/analyzers/nodeAnalyzerExec.ts` did the same for the bundled analyzers (knip, watskeburt and codeowners call `git` unhidden).
  - A static scan found every one of our spawns hidden, and replays from a `node.exe` parent did not reproduce it. Only the live trace did.
- **Fix:** `src/process/consoleNode.ts`, Windows only, so other platforms are unchanged.
  - JS CLIs and analyzers run under a console `node.exe` found by the hijack-safe PATH search, now in `src/process/programSearch.ts`.
  - The Node version must be 20 or newer. It is probed per realpath+mtime in `src/process/nodeVersionProbe.ts`, and failures are cached for 60 s.
  - Otherwise it falls back to `execPath`, logging one warning per reason.
- **Hardening in the same pass (`verify/execRunner.ts`):**
  - Bare programs (`node`, `git`) resolve to absolute PATH entries. libuv searches the current folder first, so this stops a planted exe in the verified repo from running.
  - `.cmd` shims run through the absolute system `cmd.exe` with `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1`.
  - The verifier's own `node` uses any PATH node, with no version floor.
  - `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is set only when the Electron binary is spawned.
- **Tests:** `src/process/{consoleNode,nodeVersionProbe,programSearch}.test.ts` and `src/verify/execRunner.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-10: a never-synced 263 MB store drains safely, and settled receipts are pruned (Local-first · Sync)

- **Context.**
  - The store had 88,898 imports that were never synced.
  - The old drain spent about 5 s per round and stopped after 20 rounds per pass.
  - Every queued import held a full copy of its payload.
  - 88,898 receipts duplicated what the row mappings already say.
- **Fix (13f8b3057, ad02c2efe, plus the earlier sweep commits).**
  - **Drain speed:**
    - running per-partition pending counts;
    - `syncRound` picks a batch in about 15 ms;
    - the drain loop runs on a time budget, keeps a rate reserve and honours 429s.
  - **Retry-After:** accepts both delta-seconds and an HTTP-date, capped at 1 h. Scheduler timers are clamped to 2^31-1 ms.
  - **Payload markers:**
    - a bound import is queued as a marker and materialized at push time, with the same bytes on a resend;
    - an empty payload is self-healed;
    - markers are fenced from old builds. This was proven by running `87e4b88cc`'s own coordinator: it never sends a null payload.
  - **Backlog migration:**
    - one-time, flag-guarded and skips materialized events;
    - takes a backup first;
    - the backup is kept until the store syncs, with a restore path.
  - **Settled receipts:**
    - pruned at compaction, both on disk and in memory;
    - row status is unchanged, because a mapped row reads as synced (`deriveRecordSyncStatus` is identical in the old build);
    - the legacy merge guards against re-sending on mapped rows.
- **Proof (store copy, fake server).**
  - The 88,898 imports drained with 0 hash mismatches.
  - The compacted base went from 263 MB to 199.8 MB.
  - 726 local-first tests pass, plus the vscode sync suites.
- **Still open (ROADMAP):** an idle-machine re-measure of open and drain time.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-10: code links on real repos — aliases, route handlers, constructor and JSX calls (PRD 43 P0c · Knowledge)

- **Context.** Validating against hired.video found four gaps:
  - tsconfig `paths` aliases were treated as packages, which hid 86% of cross-file imports;
  - route and listener callbacks had no owner, so their calls were dropped;
  - `new X().m()` produced no edge;
  - JSX renders were recorded as `uses`.
- **Fix (a86d976ef plus earlier sweep commits).**
  - **Aliases:**
    - Resolved once, at extract time, through one ordered `aliasCandidates` list.
    - Cached per root and invalidated by the tsconfig/jsconfig watcher.
    - Every extract path passes them through `rootModuleResolution`: review, live, run delta and on-prem.
  - **Callback owners:** flagged `function` symbols named `callee "literal"`.
  - **Calls:** `new X().m()` and JSX renders are now `calls` edges with call sites.
  - **Extraction:** always uses the regex extractor, with masking through `maskSource`.
  - **Test paths:** decided by one `isTestSourcePath` rule.
  - **Size:** `symbolRelations` is split into `callScan`, `symbolImports` and `ownerSpans`.
- **Proof on hired.video.**
  - The API-side and VS Code rollups are identical: 23,244 edges each, 0 mismatches.
  - 21,992 relations resolve through aliases.
  - 1,560 route/listener owners own 5,790 calls.
  - Sampled precision was 10/10 for each new family.
  - Sequences now start at `PATCH /me/profile-mode` and at the `fillComposer` listener.
- **Still open (ROADMAP):** a config change re-extracting unchanged files; this waits on memory 2026.10.72.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-10: typed entity ids, Phase A (LocalId UUID / SyncId bigint) (Local-first · Sync · Agents)

- **Context.** Chat #61651 filed duplicate tickets: a tool result's ids were read by several hand-rolled regexes and `Number()` guesses, so a client UUID and a server integer were mixed up. Design: [typed-entity-ids.md v2](./docs/design/typed-entity-ids.md).
- **One primitive, one resolver.** `packages/local-first/src/entityId.ts` owns `LocalId` (UUID), `SyncId` (positive safe integer), `parseSyncId`, `isLocalId`, `parseEntityRef` and `mintLocalId`. `entityIdResolver.ts` is the one lookup (`syncIdOf` / `localIdOf` / `resolve`) over the store's mapping rows. `clientEntityIdentity.ts` is deleted.
- **Mappings.** `ServerMapping.syncId` is nullable. One normaliser (`normalizeServerMapping`) reads legacy rows and drops none. A run step's receipt says `syncId: null` explicitly, so its step id is never read as a message SyncId. "Earliest mapping" is ordered by a persisted `mappedSeq` (`compareMappingAge`), so the order is the same after a restart.
- **Account-scoped resolution.** Lookups take an `EntityScope`: a destination, or an account `{ tenantId }` (its destinations plus unbound). The editor passes the active workspace's tenant (`activeEntityScope`) in the domain tools, the ticket-id bridge, the chat ticket scope and the chat rail, so another tenant's SyncId 40 is never picked.
- **Server (expand push).** Migration 1339 adds `sync_id bigint` to `sync_entity_mappings` with a non-unique index. Receipts and pulled records carry `syncId`. The api re-exports the shared `SyncReceipt` (one definition). `idArg` reads the id arguments of 177 builtin tools through `parseSyncId`, with an error the model can act on.
- **Tool results.** `brain-embedded/src/toolResultRecord.ts` `entityIdsOf` is the one reader of a tool result's ids, which fixes the chat #61651 duplicate tickets.
- **Guard.** `scripts/check-entity-id-parsing.mjs` (`check:entity-id-parsing`) refuses new hand-rolled id parsing outside the allowlist.
- The contract push (drop `server_id`, read `sync_id` first, stop sending `serverId` text) stays in ROADMAP.md. It is blocked until push telemetry shows no client below the version that reads `syncId`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-10: editor run #70776: planned work reaches local sub-agents, its tickets move, and it syncs (Local-first · Agents)

- **Context.** In editor run #70776, `hand_off` filed 4 tickets, coded everything in the session, stalled, and was stopped. The tickets stayed in backlog at 0%, and nothing ever synced (389 events queued, "Last push: never").
- **Fan-out.** One task's `paths` named a parent folder of the others', so `canRunInParallel` silently sent the whole plan inline.
  - The first overlapping `hand_off` now gets one correction naming the two tasks and the path. This is skipped on a forced turn, so it cannot dead-end the run.
  - If the plan comes back unchanged, the leading disjoint tasks fan out to local `spawn_agents`, and everything from the first overlapping or pathless task runs inline in plan order.
  - The mode and the clash are recorded as a `hand_off.mode` trace step, in the plan message, and in the routing report.
  - Ticket descriptions carry at most a 600-char summary excerpt.
  - Code: `handOffParallelism.ts`, `handOffFanOut.ts`, `handOffNext.ts`; `planHandoff.ts` is now 356 lines.
- **Ticket status.**
  - The hand-off moves its tickets to in_progress through one `ticketStatusMove` helper: `ticket-move` for local tickets, `builtin_tasks_update` for server tickets.
  - The close-out moves only the hand-off's own local tickets, never overrides blocked/cancelled/review, and every move goes through one `moveTicket`.
  - `deterministicFinish` returned at its gate before every step (since 7c32705c5), so an unshipped run never advanced tickets, attached later touched files, or wrote held notes. The gate now applies only to the review and the move to done.
  - The driver-run `finishCloseOut` computes `verified` from evidence instead of hard-coding `true`.
- **Duplicate delta tickets.** `recordCodeChangeTicket` reads `taskId ?? id` through the one `serverTicketId` parser. Chat #61651 had 17 duplicates.
- **Progress guard.**
  - The first read-back of a just-written file is no longer `reverifying`.
  - `claimsReady` recognises #70776's readiness wording.
  - Advisories and trips are traced through one `progressTraceStep` in brain-embedded and agent-run.
- **Sync.** Hybrid and Specific grant `synchronize` when signed in. An explicit `false` still wins, it is always off while signed out, and Local only stays locked. Commit 4d833df68.
- **Staffing line.** It no longer claims local tickets are "staffed after they sync".
- **Tests.** New tests: `handOffClash.e2e`, `handOffForcedClash.e2e`, `handOffParallelism`, `localTicketCloseOut`, `runBackstops.deltaTicketId`, `progressGuard.advisory`, `progressAdvisoryEvent` (agent-run). `brainCloseOut.test.ts` is ported off the deleted `closeOutRun`. Named `regression:` tests cover each defect.

- **One replica host.** The editor's replica stack moved to `packages/agent-tools/src/knowledge/replicaHost.ts` (`createReplicaHost({ lock?, report? })`, per-instance state) with `replicaLock.ts`, `replicaAdoption.ts` and a pure `manifestBuffer.ts`. VS Code's `knowledgeReplica.ts` is a shim over one instance; its quiet, retry and lock tests moved with unchanged assertions. agent-tools types the client structurally (`ReplicaHostClient`), so it does not import knowledge-client.
- **On-prem.** `onPremReplica.ts`: one `nodeKnowledgeStore` per workspace folder, one process-wide host, queues resumed on start (each queue file records its own `rootId`), a bounded flush on exit that leaves other signal handlers' shutdown intact, and a drain after each review.
- **Web and Rovr.** IndexedDB `RowPersistence` (`knowledgeRows.ts`), `KnowledgeFiles` (`knowledgeFiles.ts`), a memory fallback that stays additive, and `webLocksReplicaLock` over `navigator.locks` (in-tab holder count; a pump yields to a waiting review). `rememberFact` goes through `client.writeRows`; `syncStatus` includes the replica; the web canvas, `KnowledgeDestination` and Rovr dispose their source. `manifestStore.ts` deleted.
- **Data safety on adoption.** A root reviewed against the server before this change is pumped in additive mode: no server-only deletes and no `targetDigest` until a complete, non-aborted full local review (judgement settled) clears it. `shouldStayAdditive` is the one rule; `markAdditive` binds the project first so a project switch cannot clear it; a pump re-reads the persisted queue so a second tab cannot overwrite it.
- **Deleted.** The API `PUT extracted/:hash` handler, `knowledgePerception.putExtracted` and its test, the per-hash heal hook (`LedgerBinding`, `onHealed`, `invalidateHealedBody`), and from knowledge-client `putExtracted`, `store.write`, `markStale`, the skip counter and `MAX_WRITE_ROWS`; `client.store` is now the read-only `KnowledgeClientStore`. The sanitise cases moved to `knowledgePrivacy.test.ts` and the `#`-path heal case to `sync/applyKnowledgePack.heal.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: knowledge review stores binary files, reads PDF and Office text, and no longer stalls the judge (Knowledge · builderforce-memory 2026.10.62 · VSIX 2026.10.146)

- **Symptom.** A hired.video review listed 30 files as "not stored" (png, ico, pdf, docx). `plan.ts` skipped every binary extension with no node, `mediaTypeOfPath` returned `text/plain` for `.png`, no host extracted PDF or DOCX text, and the judge's flat 60 s timeout tripped the 5-in-a-row breaker on large README and package.json requests (0 sections judged).
- **Assets.** Binaries are planned, not skipped: each is a file node with badges `asset`, `mediaType` and `size` (`oversized` for a claimed document over the size cap). `EXTRACTOR_VERSION` 4 re-plans old manifests. Assets cost no model calls, sort last in importance, and are excluded from system metadata. `ReviewPlan.assets` lets hosts subtract them from ETAs.
- **Documents.** `@builderforce/agent-tools/documents` extracts PDF (unpdf) and OOXML (streaming fflate, capped per entry, in total and by entry count) text. `withDocumentText` wraps any `DirectorySource`; `hashOf(text, path)` returns the hash of the bytes actually read, and `readTimeoutMs(path)` gives document reads a longer deadline. Wired in VS Code (extract pool), the browser review worker (READ_BYTES proxy, byte hashes in listings), cloud drive and the API résumé reader (old error codes kept).
- **Judge timeout.** `defaultJudgementTimeoutMs`: 60 s plus 15 s per 4,000 characters, capped at 300 s; a bad function-valued timeout falls back to 60 s.
- **Visualizer.** The node panel shows media type and size for assets; the sync drawer no longer reports assets as "not stored"; labels in all five catalogs.
- **Release.** builderforce-memory 2026.10.60 → .61 (CI failure: the pool deadline always added the read default) → .62; every Builderforce.ai manifest and lockfile on ^2026.10.62.
- **Known limits.** Two hosts with different pack sets re-extract documents in turn; streaming unzip ignores the central directory; fsAccess listing hashes document bytes on the page thread (≤2 MB each).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: the knowledge view no longer freezes the screen on a real graph (Knowledge · VSIX 2026.10.144)

- **Symptom.** On `agentic` (3138 nodes, 158,663 edges, 20,738 findings, 389 stations), every camera blocked the main thread for 1.5–4.5 s.
- **Measured.** The `src/perf` harness (`KG_PERF=1`) found these culprits: `insightsOf` 1.5 s, the `rankTask` sort as one 1.07 s step, `pathOfStations` 1.3 s, `canonicalEdges` computed three times, and the surface model built synchronously.
- **Algorithms.**
  - One memoised `canonicalEdges` with a stepped typed-array sort (`scene/chunkedSort.ts`).
  - Packed-key ranking (`scene/rankStages.ts`).
  - A station-pair index for paths.
  - Single-pass insights (`insights/hotspots.ts`).
  - Stepped springs and plane order.
  - Shared `pairKey` and incident-edge helpers.
- **One compute worker (`src/compute/`).**
  - Results come back as indices into the main thread's own arrays.
  - Graphs are uploaded in 500-element slices.
  - Ranked-edge incident lists are decoded lazily (`LazyIncident`).
  - Every heavy call site uses `useComputed`: layouts, edge paths and buffers, ranking, mind map, surface, path, insights, partition matrix, anti-patterns, focus.
  - Failure handling:
    - every failure path re-runs the request instead of dropping it;
    - one unclonable request no longer disables the worker;
    - a graph whose upload fails runs in-process alone.
  - The VS Code webview gets a blob worker via `setWorkerFactory`.
- **Edit contract.** Graphs are immutable: an edit produces new node, edge and finding arrays. In development, `isDevBuild()` (`src/devBuild.ts`) freezes resident arrays, so an in-place edit throws.
- **Wheel and pinch zoom.** These now write the viewBox per animation frame and commit to React once on settle, instead of re-rendering on every tick.
- **Result.** In the cold harness the longest main-thread step is 46 ms, with every step under the 50 ms budget. Layout steps swing on a cold first run. Tests cover the client (cancel, eviction, clone errors, failover), residency, codecs and zoom.
- **Reviews.** Two Opus reviews; all their findings were fixed.
- **Next.** PRD 43: one shared 3D stage for every camera.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: a posting links to every board it lands on, applicants come home with their source, and Workable is a connector (Hiring)

- **Public board URLs.** `resolveBoardUrls.ts` builds the public link from each board's posting id: Greenhouse, LinkedIn (Rest.li `ids=List(...)`), Ashby (job-id filter), Lever and Workable. A failed lookup retries on `resolve_retry_at` alone, and a success clears the error. Indeed has no public URL by design, so it shows as link-less instead of broken.
- **Applicants are imported, with source attribution.**
  - **Import:** `importBoardApplicants.ts` pages each board's applicants. The supporting code is split into `importCursor.ts`, `importWorklist.ts`, `importFilterId.ts`, `importBudget.ts` and `importDistribution.ts`.
  - **Resuming:** the import keeps its cursor, sort order, resume page and resume token, so it picks up where it stopped. A run whose saved token fails on its first page clears that token and starts over. Lever's `hasNext` ends paging through `nextToken.done`.
  - **Overlap and budget:** the sweep takes a lease on `import_checked_at`, so two runs never import the same distribution. Both entry points stay under the per-request query limit: the sweep budget is 700 queries and a manual import is 900.
  - **Fair queue:** tenants are worked oldest-check-first, five catalogs at a time. A board that can't be imported is stamped as checked, so it doesn't stay at the front of the queue.
  - **Resume after failures:** a 429, a 5xx or a network failure keeps the saved resume point. Only a 400, 404, 410 or 422 on the first resumed page clears it. A board that echoes its own paging token ends the walk.
  - **Matching:** applicants are matched against the board's posting ids, not exact-match source strings.
  - **Candidate refs:** each ref is an HMAC under a per-tenant salt in `hiring_ref_salts` (migrations 1332 and 1334). The salt is deleted when its tenant is deleted.
- **Workable connector.** Workable is a link-only hiring connector, listed with the other boards in `connectorBoardAliases.ts`.
- **Connector manifest hardening.**
  - **Parsing:** a stored manifest parses leniently on read (`connectorStoredManifest.ts`) and strictly on write (`connectorActionValidation.ts`).
  - **Paging and filter params:** the paging-token and filter-id params may only go in the query string or the request body. A filter-id lookup must be a sibling action that changes nothing. The posting param that receives the board-returned id must be a query, body or path param, so a board response can never choose the request URL.
  - **Request code split:** query building moved out of `connectorRuntime.ts` into `connectorRuntimeQuery.ts` and `connectorLookupTargets.ts`.
- **Still open in the roadmap:** the LinkedIn and Ashby request shapes come from the vendors' docs and haven't been checked against the live APIs. Blocker: a tenant's credentials for those two boards.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: a knowledge review reports its post-write analysis instead of freezing on the last write (Local-first · knowledge: builderforce-memory 2026.10.59 + the Reviews panel)

- **Root cause:** after the per-file writes, memory `review()` ran `retire()` and every pack's analyzers with no progress event. On a 6285-file root that is minutes of repo-graph re-reads plus dependency-cruiser/jscpd/knip, and the view sat on `write 6284/6285`.
- **Fix (builderforce-memory `36b6b32`, tag `v2026.10.59`):** new `ReviewPhase` `analyse`.
  - It opens at 0/1 right after the write loop, forwards summed per-pack progress through a new optional `AnalyzerPort.analyse(rootId, signal, onProgress)` (`AnalyzerProgress`), drops late callbacks, and always closes at done == total before `resolve`.
  - A Stop during the analyzers now aborts the run: resolve/compare are skipped and the digest is not stamped.
- **Proof:** contract-test + `regression:` tests fold the events through the run record. The `analyse` row stays active while an analyzer that never reports is pending. Jest passes 146/146 (contract, review*, reviewRun), and an Opus review returned ship.
- **Part 2, the Builderforce.ai consumer:**
  - **Analyzer progress:** `knowledge/analysisProgress.ts` counts repo-graph file reads plus one unit per tool (`runCodeAnalysis` `onToolSettled`) and feeds `AnalyzerPort.analyse`'s `onProgress`. `done` only grows, and a stopped run never reports done == total.
  - **The Reviews panel opens on `planning`**, over no other drawer. Closing it while counting discards the plan, and a later `running` (Count and start) does not reopen it.
  - **Progress bars:** the planning state has a progress bar, indeterminate until the walk has a total. `Bar` gained an `indeterminate` mode, styled in `tokens.css` (`kg-bar-slide`; a static fill under reduced motion).
  - **"Map the code" step:** the Now card shows it from the run record's `analyse` phase. `analyse` is in `RUN_PHASE_ORDER` and the phase labels in all five catalogs.
  - **ONE Copy diagnostics,** in the Diagnostics tab. The Server-footer copy and the RunDetail copy are gone (RunDetail links to the tab), along with the dead `diagnosticsText` / `extra` props.
  - **Proof:** targeted vitest passes (agent-tools 26/26, knowledge-graph-view 40/40 after fixes, 70/70 on the first pass), the i18n key check passes, and a Sonnet review found nothing blocking. Its five findings are fixed.
- **Shipped in VSIX 2026.10.145** (installed and verified with `code --list-extensions --show-versions`; HEAD contains `3574c0d77`). The extension pins memory `^2026.10.60` (brain-embedded and clients/vscode), and `GitShellCtx` takes `Pick<ShellCapability, "run" | "trackedBranch" | "defaultRepo" | "git">` so `git-tools.ts` typechecks.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: a folder's knowledge lives in one SQLite file the editor and on-prem agent both open (Local-first · G03 · PRD 41 WS2)

- **The floor and the store.** `engines.vscode` is `^1.101.0`, so `node:sqlite` is always present. The agent-tools subpaths `./node-local-sqlite` (opener) and `./node-knowledge-store` keep one file per folder at `.builderforce/cache/knowledge/index.sqlite`, with tables `meta`, `scope`, `fact`, `relation`, `recheck`, `extracted` and `manifest`. Extract bodies live in the `extracted` table, not in object files; that deviation from PRD 41 §B4 is recorded in the PRD. The VS Code folder store (`folderKnowledge.ts`), the replica stack and on-prem (`onPremKnowledge.ts`) all open it. `agent-runtime`'s own `memory/sqlite.ts` and the editor's `localRecordTransaction` are gone.
- **Writes are atomic with their manifest.** Manifest writes are buffered and commit in the same transaction as the facts they describe. Same-key writes upsert, and a fact-free manifest change does not move the generation.
- **Legacy JSON migrates once, safely.** Migration is insert-only and runs once per root behind a `migrated:<rootId>` marker. Rows are built with yields, then written in one transaction without yielding. A root with no legacy files leaves the generation alone, and a chunk that only deletes is still written.
- **A damaged or newer file is never made worse.**
  - A corrupt file (SQLITE_CORRUPT/NOTADB) is moved aside all-or-nothing. Any other open failure (READONLY, IOERR) leaves the file in place.
  - A file written by a newer format opens read-only. Nothing is written at open (no schema statements, no WAL pragma), and every write path refuses: apply, manifest set/delete, transaction, setMeta. A refused manifest write never lingers in the read buffer.
  - The integrity check and WAL are opt-in. UNC and `\\wsl$` paths use `journal_mode = DELETE`. The cache folder gets its own `.gitignore`.
- **Shutdown closes in order.** One memoized `shutdownKnowledge()` stops the replica pumps, flushes their queues, then closes every folder store. `deactivate` and the subscription dispose both await the same close. Opens are refused while it runs, and a late pump timer logs instead of throwing.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: one tool classifier fails closed, security gates every merge, and shipped milestones reach the investor update (Governance · Finance)

- **One tool classifier, failing closed.** `packages/agent-tools/src/tool-side-effect.ts` is the only classifier.
  - `classifyTool(name, declared?, args?)` resolves in this order: the shared catalog, then the host's own declaration, then the host's read-only tools, then a read-only `action` (honoured only on tools that dispatch on one: `process`, `cron`, `canvas`, `gateway`, `nodes`, `browser`, `*_actions`). Anything else counts as `mutate`.
  - The VS Code copy (`clients/vscode/src/policy.ts`) is deleted, and its callers use `toolMutating.ts`.
  - `BrainActionsContext` requires each action to declare `mutates`, and agent-runtime's heuristic now goes through the classifier.
  - `scripts/check-single-tool-classifier.mjs` fails CI on a second copy.
- **A gate can govern a whole class.** `policy_gates.side_effect` (migration 1327) lets a gate cover read, verify or mutate tools as well as named tools.
  - Gate ids on the wire are `packId:gateKey` and carry `baseGateId`. Changing the id asks for each existing approval once more.
  - Hosts that ask for `?gates=2` get the compact form. Older hosts get the gates expanded per tool by the relay.
  - The tenant's gates are always resolved for a run. Gates sent by the caller are merged in alongside them, never in their place, and are removed from route bodies. A follow-up run resolves the current gates instead of reusing its parent's.
- **Security automation ([PRD 08 §10](./docs/specs/08-prd-agentic-governance.md)).**
  - **PR checks:** `SECURITY_SCAN` (a secrets and OSV dependency scan at the PR's head SHA, which marks a truncated or failed scan) and `SECURITY_REVIEW` produce one verdict per PR, head SHA and check type (migrations 1320–1322).
  - **Merge gating:** `evaluateSecurityGate` blocks merges on HIGH and CRITICAL findings, on a scan that is stale, failed or truncated, or on a head that has moved. The gate applies to every merge path: merge-on-green, the sweep, human merges and the cloud finalize step. A merge re-checks the head SHA it expects.
  - **Overrides:** only an OWNER can override the gate for a whole tenant, and every override is recorded as evidence.
  - **Catch-up:** `security-verdict-catchup` fills missing verdicts, 5 PRs every 90 seconds, and skips a PR whose task still has a live run.
  - **Audit and evidence:** `mutationAudit` is the shared audit envelope for governance and security writes. `automatedSocEvidence` and the SOC 2 control baseline feed `governance-auditor`, a cron job that records gaps.
  - **Data subject requests:** a request runs as a private export, identity verification and delivery, and the private export key never leaves the tenant's asset store.
  - **Findings:** a CRITICAL finding opens an incident once.
- **Shipped milestones reach the investor update.**
  - Tasks carry an `investor_milestone` tag (migration 1325).
  - `listShippedMilestones` merges tagged tasks with board milestones (`listBoardMilestonesSince`) over a half-open window, newest 50 plus a count of the rest. It is not cached, because the window moves every send.
  - A delivery stores its window end, so the next update starts where the last one stopped. The board-pack period follows each schedule.
  - `GET /api/investor-updates/milestones/pending` and `POST …/send` require MANAGER.
  - The canvas inspector previews what the next update will say.
- **Main's red build, cleared on the slices above.** These fixes went into `24f6bb8c6` and `dcb6432fe`:
  - a duplicate `body` in `findOpenPr`;
  - apostrophes inside single-quoted test names;
  - the gate fetch URL a test expected;
  - tenant scoping on the DSR purge and on PR-scan updates;
  - catches that now record a reason instead of swallowing the error.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: autonomous delivery closes its loops: one lane door, one landing path, reviews that reopen work, and boards that earn budget (Autonomous delivery)

- **Backlog lanes no longer spend tokens.** `templateCatalog.ts` derives a lane's gate from its key, so `backlog` seeds `human` (`BACKLOG_LANE_GATE` in `defaultSwimlanes.ts`). Migration 1311 re-gates every live `backlog` lane that was `auto` and records `gate_source = 'seed'`, because the operator chose to re-gate them all.
- **The census names the real refusal.** `never_started` tickets are classified from the latest `auto_run_skipped` row (`autoRunSkipReader.ts`, one batched `DISTINCT ON` read), not assumed `will_run`. Workspace-level reasons expire after 1 hour, and `lane_requirement_gate` after 6 hours, so a plan upgrade isn't escalated with a stale sentence. `trigger_error` is a modelled reason.
- **One landing path for every status write.** `executionLandedEffects.ts` (extracted from `RuntimeService.update`) is used by `update()`, the orphan repair and the stale-run reaper. The reaper's guarded UPDATE lives in `ExecutionRepository` and is no longer on the `check-execution-landing` allowlist. Failed runs are settled in chunks of 100, 5 at a time, with one batched ticket read per chunk (`findByIdsAcrossTenants`, tenant-checked). Validator review runs post their `failed` milestone again.
- **One door into a lane.** Every caller goes through `routeLaneEntry`, and `check-dispatch-budget` fails on any direct import, re-export or dynamic import of `maybeAutoRunOnLaneEntry`. The coordinator branch:
  - re-reads the live lane;
  - stays out of lifecycle-managed boards;
  - re-checks the lane gate;
  - applies the evaluator's admission gates (execution switch, token budget, failure breaker and cooldown, which also count stage failures with no execution row) in `laneCoordinatorAdmission.ts`;
  - records refusals in the skip ledger.
  
  Only a human drag forces a stage. Lane routing is one cached read per project and tenant (`laneRouting.ts`). It is invalidated by every lane, staffing and board writer, including the new `boardWrites.ts` seam.
- **Live board scoping.** Staffing changes publish to the board (`boardChangePublisher.ts`), so chips update without a reload. Ticket owners who aren't staffed on a lane show as owner chips (`GET /api/boards/:boardId/ticket-owners`, cached under the board-live version token). The legacy per-lane agents GET stays as a cached compatibility shim for shipped VSIX bundles.
- **Priced kanban templates are licensed through the listing checkout.** Install, apply and fork return 402 until the tenant holds a licence. A foreign priced template's GET returns a preview of lane names and price, unlocked through `useKanbanTemplateCheckout`. The publisher of record is set once (migration 1313 backfills it), and checkout return URLs must be same-origin.
- **A reviewer's `changes_requested` reopens the producer slot and starts one run** (`onReviewerVerdict.ts`, from the sign-off route and approval decisions). The stage choice is deterministic.
- **Stakeholder notifications are routed.** `stakeholderVoice.ts` and `incidentVoice.ts` route these sites through the coordinator voice: chat milestones, approval gates and requests, escalations, incident notes, execution approval and pause.
- **PR conduct is a registry sweep.** The `pr-conduct` cron (`prConductSweep.ts`, `prConductTicket.ts`) rotates through projects and tickets on a durable id cursor, and stamps a `conduct_seen` marker. That marker is a bookkeeping type, so the decision feeds hide it. Triage defers only to a ticket the sweep conducted recently. `ManagerService.ts` shrank by about 380 lines.
- **A delta on a non-platform branch completes.** `deltaBranchMatch.ts` matches the merged PR's head branch on the merged repo only. It skips default and long-lived branches and refuses an ambiguous branch. `shipVerification` takes the repo's default branch.
- **PRD 23 recovery is built and dry-run only.** §8 "Validator acceptance evidence is linked or bridged to its lifecycle slot" is met: `task_reviews` links to the lifecycle slot, execution and reviewed head SHA (migration 1312). A push invalidates stale acceptance, and the Validator review posts to the PR once. A Manager canary flag (off by default) holds the unattended merge. Backlog dispositions are computed nightly into `ticket_dispositions` and applied only through the superadmin `POST /api/admin/backlog-dispositions/apply` with `confirm: true`.
- **Boards earn budget.** Closing a ticket credits its board through the account ledger (`accountLedger.ts`, `board-earn:<taskId>`, earned once), and `GET /api/boards/:boardId/budget` shows earned against run spend. `listBoardMilestonesSince` gives investor updates their delivery milestones, rolling nested epics up.
- **Teammates have profiles.** `/people/[id]` shows role, personality and open work. The mention autocomplete shows each person's personality hint, and the hint cache clears when a personality is saved.
- Release notes 2026.10.141/142 (migration 1314) and the post `boards-earn-budget-and-teammates-have-profiles` in five locales.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-08: sync pulls never skip a late commit, a push batches its events, and a purged dependency stops waiting (Local-first · sync residuals)

- **Commit-ordered watermark.** Migration `1304_sync_changes_commit_watermark.sql` adds `sync_changes.txid xid8`. Existing rows are backfilled `'0'`, and new rows default to `pg_current_xact_id()`. Pull (`SyncPullRepository.ts`, `deltaWatermark.ts`) pages on the tuple `(txid, seq)` and returns only rows whose transaction is below `pg_snapshot_xmin(pg_current_snapshot())`, so a slow transaction holding a lower `seq` can no longer be stepped over. The cursor codec is v2 (txid as a decimal string). A v1 cursor `S` reads as `('0', S)`, so existing clients resume without a resync. An xmin age over 10k is reported, at most once a minute.
- **One transaction per chunk, not per event.** `handleSyncPush` writes 25 events per transaction (`syncChunking.ts`) with a SAVEPOINT per event, so one refused event rolls back alone. The transaction opens lazily. Deadlock and serialization failures (40P01/40001) retry twice, and effects run after each chunk commits. `uniqueViolation.ts` unwraps drizzle's `DrizzleQueryError.cause` so the SQLSTATE is actually seen.
- **A purged dependency dead-letters.** A write whose dependency can never resolve dead-letters as `dependency_unresolvable` after 90 days (`holdLimits.ts`). Dependencies resolve through the idempotency key. `requeueJournalDeadLetter` puts back one non-permanent dead letter. It is wired into the VS Code dead-letter export command as a "Retry a journal dead letter" picker (`journalDeadLetters.ts`, `deadLetterExport.ts`).
- **Chat-ticket links sync both ways.** Groundwork for G21 + G23: `chat-ticket-link` is a local-first entity with a deterministic id (`chatTicketLink.ts`). The API importer `importSyncedChatTicketLink` makes the pair immutable and settles a delete of a missing link as already satisfied. Server records are ingested with server-observed provenance, and `lastPullAt` is kept beside the cursor (`ingestServerRecords.ts`, `syncStatus.ts`).

They now appear in the History panel as an "Interrupted runs" section, showing the chat's title and when the run stopped, in the editor's locale. The list is host state, read from the journal with `listInterruptedRuns`, so it survives a webview reload and an editor restart (`interruptedRunsView.ts`; message `run.interrupted`).

That is the same door a typed turn uses, so the chat's history seed, model, project and spec come along. Composer attachments and the selected sub-agent are left out. - **A lost stored body heals for every project that used it.** When an unreadable body (lost R2 object) is re-supplied by one root's pack, every affected leaf of every root that named it, the applying root's other paths included, is invalidated in the same transaction and its generation advanced; the pack ack carries `reconcile`, a cheap generation-only read (`?view=generation`, no-store) lets a quiet linked root notice the change every 10 minutes (VS Code arms one timer per healthy root), refs split exactly by the known root (`#` paths and `cloud:<id>:` roots handled), and the legacy upload reaches the same heal through an injected hook. Regression tests cover each case. This closes the replica stuck at `failed=3` / `extracted_missing`.
- **The review no longer sticks at "Counting files…" on a large root.** On a 15,960-file root the plan awaited five unbounded setup steps (partitions, symbol index, judge start-up, git history, knowledge index) before walking, then hashed every file serially through the extension host. Now `reviewPortsFor.ts` builds the plan from source, manifest, packs and a judge-configured flag only (no server call); run-only ports start in the background with a 120 s bound each (a timeout is logged and dropped, a failure fails the review as before); the walk hashes 16 at a time with node:crypto, skips reading files over the size limit, and keeps a persisted hash cache, so a restart is not a cold walk; every plan logs per-step timings to the BuilderForce output channel.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — One folder reads as many systems, a review maps in minutes, and sync is one compact pack (PRD 41 A9 + A10 + A11 · WS25 + WS26 · builderforce-memory 2026.10.46–48 · VS Code 2026.10.140)

- **A9: a folder of many systems reads as many systems.**
  - Each child repository or manifest is its own system. Lines are grouped by system and shared out fairly, there is no file-count cap, and the header starts at the system you are in.
  - Near-identical copies are detected, the likely stray is named with the reason, and the user gets a one-click Exclude. The visualizer surfaces directory problems instead of us fixing them in the directory.
  - Ship: release note migration 1303 and the blog post "one-folder-many-systems" (5 locales).
- **A10: the map completes in minutes, and judging follows in the background.**
  - Bug: a ~240 s stall per file made a review take 78 h. The causes were shared I/O, extraction coupled to judging, and timeouts recorded as judged.
  - Fix:
    - Pass 1 is a mechanical `mapped` pass, with per-job deadlines (read 5 s, extract 10 s).
    - Pass 2 judges within a budget (500 files by default, capped by `KNOWLEDGE_REVIEW_MODEL_CALLS`). `JudgeBreaker` stops after 5 failures in a row, and a judge timeout leaves the section owed.
    - The extract log `.extracted.jsonl` is append-only.
    - Workers do an in-thread changed-since-plan sha256 check.
    - `reviewRunLock` releases at `mapped`, and a new run pre-empts pass 2.
- **A11: sync to the server is one compact BFKP pack, and only the exact delta.**
  - Memory codec: front-coded strings, columnar sections, LEB128 varints and deflate-raw. A CRC covers header and body. There is a 4,096-bucket manifest tree, plus content-addressed `have` and within-file diff.
  - In 2026.10.48:
    - relation keys are `r:`+JSON, because NUL was rejected by Postgres;
    - bucket digests are incremental;
    - multi-part decode is streamed;
    - limits are 24 MB / 200k rows.
  - Server (`POST …/knowledge/sync`, `…/sync/manifest`, `…/sync/have`):
    - one transaction under a per-project advisory lock with a 10 s timeout, answering 503 `sync_busy` with Retry-After;
    - a conditional index upsert, so a race returns 409 `body_conflict`;
    - root-scoped tombstones, and a model-only cascade with leaf cleanup;
    - removal markers, and migrated-root reconciliation;
    - the legacy PUT merges bundle-first, then does a locked upsert;
    - the sweep takes the lock per project.
  - Migrations: 1300, 1301, and 1302 (the `leaf_key_hash` PK and `knowledge_sync_buckets`).
  - Client: one pack per sync with size halving. A file with a control character is skipped and recorded instead of stopping the sync. The browser worker trusts only declared content hashes.
  - Reviews: three Opus passes. The last said ship. Real-SQL ledger tests run on pglite.
- **Also closed:**
  - migration 1298 (identity on a uuid column), which blocked every API deploy after it;
  - memory contract and regression tests (`src/contract/`);
  - stale knowledge tests;
  - the brain-embedded dist now ships `.d.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — The editor files tickets on the device, and a copied chat report fits a paste

- **Bug: a signed-in VS Code run filed tickets one server call at a time and hit HTTP 429.** Chat #210 filed a 26-ticket program (an epic and 25 tasks) as `builtin_tasks_create` + `builtin_chats_link_ticket` pairs on the tenant's 300 rpm window, and both tools failed. The local `ticket-*` adapter ran only when sync was denied.
- **Fix: tickets are written on the device and reach the account in batches.**
  - `ticket-*` and `project-*` always write the local store (`clients/vscode/src/localDomainToolRouting.ts`).
  - The editor hides `builtin_tasks_create` and `builtin_chats_link_ticket`.
  - The creating chat (`chatClientId`) and the epic or gap `taskType` ride on the ticket.
  - A UUID passed to a `builtin_*` tool is translated to the synced server id (`localTicketIdBridge.ts`).
  - `ticketToolVocabulary` (brain-embedded) tells the prompt, the hand-off, the triage check and the reply nudge which create tool is present.
- **Sync** (`@builderforce/local-first` `journalRules` / `workBinding`, `chatSyncHost` drain):
  - binds projects, then tickets;
  - resolves each dependency at send time to the dependency entity's creating write in the same destination (an entity the server already mapped counts as satisfied);
  - drains up to 20 batches of 100 events;
  - dead-letters only on an explicit list of permanent refusals; dependents are blocked, not killed, and unblock when the entity is filed again;
  - holds every other refusal with backoff saved on the event (30 s doubling, capped at 1 hour), sent after fresh work, giving up only after 7 days (never for `dependency_pending`);
  - rebases edits made during a push or after a lost receipt onto the server version.
- **Server** (`importSyncedTicket`):
  - writes `tasks.task_type` and the 'created' `chat_ticket_links` row in one savepoint (`upsertChatTicketLink`, shared with `linkTicket`);
  - links the chat on a best-effort basis;
  - holds an unmapped UUID reference for up to 10 minutes;
  - bumps caches after commit.
  - Board-write MCP calls (REST and an all-board JSON-RPC batch) go to the 4× `:board` bucket.
  - The repository was split into project, ticket, ownership and shared modules, and the platform-caller plumbing was removed.
- **Bug: a copied chat report was 110 KB, over the 50,000-character paste limit.** Only tool payloads were budgeted.
- **Fix:**
  - one 48,000-character ceiling for the whole report (`PASTE_SAFE_REPORT_CHARS`);
  - reply and reasoning text are charged against it;
  - compact diagnostics JSON with an `_elided` marker and a skeleton fallback;
  - a 10-ticket list in the header;
  - the error and the chat title are capped;
  - a last-resort middle cut (`cutMiddleToFit`) that never splits a surrogate pair.
- **Also fixed:**
  - the unused `ManifestTree` import that blocked brain-embedded's d.ts build;
  - 9 unscoped `annotations` queries in `canvasComments.ts`, which failed `check:tenant-scope`.
