## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — The knowledge view works offline, and a review is a run you can watch, in parallel (PRD 41 A7 + A8 · WS14 + WS23 · builderforce-memory 2026.10.44 · VS Code 2026.10.139)

- **A7: the local copy is the source and the server is a replica.**
  - Bug: a linked review kept no local snapshot, so the view drew `GET /knowledge-graph`. On 2026-11-07 the `agentic` map drew 119 of 3,038 files.
  - The cause: `selectKnowledgeStore` returned the client store or the local store, never both.
  - Fix: `replicatedKnowledgeStore` (agent-tools `src/knowledge/`) writes locally first. It also queues replica ops on a persisted queue, which a pump drains in FIFO order:
    - the queue is bound to a project;
    - writes go in chunks of 500 rows or fewer, and a 413 halves the chunk down to one row;
    - 401 and 403 pause the queue until sign-in;
    - 429 and 5xx back off and retry;
    - writes are atomic (temp file then rename), and a corrupt queue triggers a re-enqueue;
    - a `<root>.replica.lock` lock goes stale after 2 minutes;
    - the pump waits for any review of that root.
  - "Use the server's copy" is a local review with a `preloadExtracted` read-through plus the human facts. It is offered only when the workspace is linked, allowed and reachable.
  - A root the server has but this machine does not is drawn read-only. Diagnostics name the map's source.
- **A8: a review is a run you can watch, and it runs in parallel.**
  - Memory 2026.10.44:
    - `onStep` events, and `extractPool(job, signal)`;
    - `judgeConcurrency` 4 with one ordered writer, so the stored bytes are the same at any width;
    - one shared AIMD `createModelLimiter` (6 calls in flight);
    - failures are tolerated (`failures[]`) and there is a `compare` phase;
    - the pure `reviewRun` recorder.
  - VS Code:
    - a `worker_threads` extract pool (`out/knowledgeExtractWorker.js`, `clamp(cores-1,1,8)`);
    - a worker that fails to start falls back to the editor's own thread, and a machine with 2 cores or fewer runs no pool;
    - one symbol rule on both paths (the index's symbols when it has the file, otherwise the regex extractor), pinned by a parity test;
    - a run recorder and an atomic run store (`.builderforce/knowledge/runs/`, the last 20 per root; a crashed run shows "interrupted").
  - The Run panel drawer shows the timeline, lanes, steps, failures with Retry (plan, estimate, confirm; latest run only) and history.
- **Also closes "Knowledge review of `agentic` fails".** One 429 or 413 used to end a linked review. A linked review now writes locally. The replica sends chunked `writeRows`, halves its chunks on a 413, and backs off on 429 (`retryAfterMs`), so a rate limit never ends a review.
- **Ship.** Release note migration and the blog post "watch-your-codebase-review-run".

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — "Use my connected accounts" uses the accounts the editor calls itself (routing eb3f3f487 shipped in VS Code 2026.10.137 · wording in 2026.10.138)

- **Bug.** In VS Code, picking "Use my connected accounts" (`routingMode: 'byo_pool'`) sent the turn straight to the gateway's strict BYO pool. That pool only holds providers the workspace connected on the server. When the person's only account was one the editor calls itself (Kimi Code), the turn failed with "BYO execution is required, but no provider is connected on this workspace".
- **Fix.**
  - `isAccountPoolCall` in `brain-embedded/src/localFirstTransport.ts` identifies an account-pool call.
  - For those calls, `createHostModelStream` tries the host-called accounts from `editorAccounts(secrets).hybridAccounts()` first, then the gateway pool with `byo_pool` intact. Device models and the free pool are never tried.
  - `clients/vscode/src/modelRouting.ts` hands those accounts over for byo_pool in Hybrid and Specific mode.
  - When an account failed and the gateway then refused, the error names the account and its reason.
  - An account that has already streamed owns the turn.
- **Wording.** The fallback notice no longer says "on this device". The account may be hosted.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — The knowledge view matches its design and explains what it shows (PRD 38 · VS Code 2026.10.137)

The design audit of 2026-11-07 (the B-Surface mockup compared region by region, 14 items) is closed.

- **Layout.**
  - The scene starts below the floating controls (`--kg-scene-top`, measured by `useSceneTop`). The bars no longer wrap over content.
  - The System view is drawn as tier rows. Each row holds up to 6 cards plus "+N more", arrow sentences run between tiers, stores sit in a dashed row, and "Not layered · N parts → List" collects the rest.
  - The left rail has two-line line rows. Stop rows show the station's colour dot plus a pin tag or a coverage tag.
  - The legend says what each "Not set up" costs.
  - The spine carries a line crumb.
- **Tower and 3D.**
  - Tower is the transit map with 2.5D station towers (`TowerMark`):
    - height comes from size, or from complexity when size is missing;
    - coverage shows as a fill, and a measured 0% shows as a dashed shell;
    - the side face uses the `--kg-tower-side` token;
    - labels keep off tower bodies.
  - The WebGL view stays as its own "3D" camera.
  - The camera order is `transit · system · graph · map · tower · 3d · heat · list`.
- **Type and colour.**
  - Inter and JetBrains Mono (400–700) are bundled through @fontsource in the web, VS Code and Rovr hosts. All text goes through `surface/ui/type.ts` roles.
  - The neutrals are the mockup's dark and light literals, set in `tokens.css` alone. VS Code high-contrast themes re-point text, muted and border.
- **Act rail.**
  - The title reads "At {scope} · N issues" or "On this path · N to act on", with a Fix queue link beside it.
  - At most 3 cards, a ✓ empty state and a footer.
  - Findings that touch more than 25% of stations (at least 8) are listed once as system-wide.
  - Details is collapsed by default.
  - The Act counts never pass through a hidden lens. When Details is lens-scoped, its heading names the lens and shows "{shown} of {total}".
- **Words.**
  - Station names drop the shared prefix. Root config files fold into one "repo config" station.
  - Every count goes through `counted()`, with singular and plural forms in all five catalogs.
  - The sync pill reads "On the server only" when nothing is reviewed locally and "Out of sync" on a real mismatch. It never says Synced next to a mismatch.
  - Importance is shown as a rank. Anti-pattern levels are words.
- **Explained gaps.**
  - `dataCoverage` is the single decision for map source and per-channel coverage. The diagnostics, the legend, the overlay menu and `metricStatus` all read it, so they agree.
  - `staticReach` gives a heuristic coverage fallback, labelled "reached".
  - Copy diagnostics explains the picture.
- **Tests.**
  - `.css?raw` loads real text in the kgv vitest config. Before this, vitest stubbed it as empty.
  - New suites cover tokens and contrast, plurals, dataCoverage and reach, TowerMark, system tiers, rail rows, labels placement and the sync pill.
- **Still open.** Offline drawing for linked workspaces (PRD 41 A7 / WS14) stays in the roadmap.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-07 — PRD 42: the browser's own model in every modality — on-device first for background work, client-first server routes, and content translation (api 2026.10.99 · brain-embedded 2026.10.79 · brain-ui 2026.10.33 · VS Code 2026.10.136)

Every part of PRD 42 shipped. Section numbers below are the PRD's own, kept intact.

- **A1/A2** — Vendor identity as data (Chrome → Gemini Nano, Edge → Phi-4-mini, unknown → "Built-in model"; brands trusted when present). Probe rows carry `state`; only servable rows are routed (`isServableLocalModel`). `PIN_REMAPPED` through `onFallback`. Opt-in Download in the "On this device" picker through the one store path, starting the chat model and every task model inside the click.
- **B1–B3** — ONE `OnDeviceTasks` port (`brain-embedded/src/onDevice/*`), one adapter per built-in API (`builtInAi/*`), routes as data (`ON_DEVICE_TASK_ROUTES`), chunked summaries with output reserve, re-measure and a non-recursing splitter. A deterministic `heuristicLanguage` tail for `detectLanguage`. Bound once per host: web `browserOnDeviceTasks()`, Rovr `PanelServices.onDeviceTasks`, VS Code `onDeviceTasks` over Synapse (`completeOnDevice` is private). One shared validator package `@builderforce/json-schema` (both old copies deleted).
- **C1–C3** — Summarizer calls stamp `role: 'utility'`; `onDeviceFirst` tries the device before the stream; a declined utility call reaches the run's own model exactly as before.
- **D1–D2** — `clientResult` on the D2 routes through one parser (`clientResult.ts`) and one client helper (`withClientResult`, retry once on `invalid_client_result`). Owner-only acceptance for shared content: chat owner, agent-host registrar, meeting organizer or sole human attendee — anyone else gets the server path. Accepted results write a zero-cost `local/<engine>/<model>` utility usage row. Résumé prompts extracted to `@builderforce/resume-ai` (+ `@builderforce/score-math`). Excluded: résumé grade, legal enhance, `classifyTask`, replay summaries (the server holds their source).
- **E1–E5** — `TranslatableText` (brain-ui) on chat messages, canvas comments and canvas import (a translated copy as a new document; the original is untouched), on all three hosts. On-device first; cloud fallback `POST /api/translate` on the free Workers AI tier with per-tenant and global daily budgets that fail closed, a concurrency cap, required `from`, and per-text caching. Message authorship is now a fact of the message: `brain_chat_messages.author_user_id` (migration 1296, server-stamped for human turns only, `NOT VALID` FK + partial index); unknown author is never translated. Release note (migration 1295) and the five-locale blog post `read-anyones-message-in-your-language`.
- **F** — Per-call served-engine provenance, `served`/`declined`/`replaced` observe events, VS Code utility rows through the run ledger, and the "On-device utility" series in cost insights. Web and Rovr have no client usage ledger, so their on-device calls are not metered locally (accepted client results are metered server-side).

Reviews: Opus (server trust boundary, migration 1296, core), Sonnet (WS1). Security findings from review (shared-content rewrite, translate cache oracle) are in `SECURITY-FINDINGS.local.md`; the first was fixed before commit.

<details><summary>PRD 42 design as built (archived from docs/specs/42-prd-browser-built-in-models.md)</summary>

# PRD 42 — The browser's own model, in every modality

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | In progress — WS1 core shipped: A1 (vendor identity table and labels "Gemini Nano (Chrome)" / "Phi-4-mini (Edge)" / "Built-in model", the vendor-aware `browserEngine`, `PIN_REMAPPED` through `onFallback`) and the A2 probe `state` with routing limited to servable (`ready`) rows. A2 Download shipped (the built-in model is a downloadable row in the "On this device" picker, downloaded through the ONE model store); task-API language packs on the same click, and WS2–WS6, are still open. Metering: web and Rovr have no client usage ledger, so their on-device calls are not metered locally (an accepted client result IS metered server-side, in the server's row); VS Code meters through the run ledger. Review before each workstream ships. |
| Owner | Agents program. Model roles are in CLAUDE.md. |
| Roadmap | `ROADMAP.md` › Local-first. Builds on PRD 34 (local models everywhere: `bfi`, WebLLM and the `browser` page runtime), the inference modes (Local only · Hybrid · Specific) and the four routing packages (`model-catalog`, `workload`, `model-router`, `run-policy`). |
| Date | 2026-11-06 |

## 1. What and why

Browsers now ship a small language model. Chrome has Gemini Nano, and Edge has Phi-4-mini.
Both expose it through the same web APIs:

- the general **Prompt API** (`LanguageModel`);
- the **task APIs**:
  - `Summarizer`, `LanguageDetector` and `Translator`, stable in Chrome 138;
  - `Writer`, `Rewriter` and `Proofreader`, in origin or developer trials. Edge previews `Summarizer`, `Writer` and `Rewriter`.

A call these models can answer costs nothing, sends nothing off the device and works offline.

Today we use one of these APIs in one place. The `browser` page runtime answers tool-less
chat turns through the Prompt API on the web and in Rovr. Everything else that could run there
goes to a pinned model or to the server.

This PRD makes the browser's model, and on the editor its equivalent Synapse, the first
choice for every call it can answer, in every host. It delivers four things:

1. **The right model, named correctly.** The `browser` runtime knows which browser it is in.
   It names Gemini Nano or Phi-4-mini, uses that model's real window and can be downloaded
   on request.
2. **Background work on the device.** This covers compaction folds, hand-off packs, chat
   Consolidate/Fork, knowledge judgement, meeting summaries, dashboard intent,
   and SOP and résumé rewrites. Each runs on-device first through ONE port, `OnDeviceTasks`,
   whatever model the conversation is pinned to.
3. **Client-first server routes.** A server route that summarizes or rewrites the user's own
   content accepts the client's on-device result. The server spends a model call only when
   the request arrives without one.
4. **Content translation (new feature).** A person reads another person's message, or an
   imported document, in their own language. The translation is detected and translated on
   the device. The original is never altered.

## 2. Principles

1. **On-device first for utility work, in every mode.** A model pin selects the model for the
   *conversation*, not for housekeeping. A `utility` call goes to the device whenever the
   device can take it, under Hybrid, Specific and Local only alike. The device is never less
   private than the pin. (Operator decision 1.)
2. **Never a surprise download.** Probing never starts a download (unchanged). A model arrives
   only when the person clicks Download in the "On this device" picker. (Operator decision 2.)
3. **Null means "not here".** Every on-device task returns its result or `null`. A `null` means
   the caller does what it does today. No caller branches on browser, vendor or API.
4. **Registry data, not branches.** Vendor identity, task-to-API mapping, window fallbacks
   and chunk limits are rows in a table. A new browser or a new API is a row plus an adapter.
5. **One detection per API.** Each built-in API is feature-detected in exactly one adapter file,
   the way `promptApi.ts` is today. Nothing else reads a global.
6. **The client may supply the user's own text, never a decision.** A server accepts
   client-computed summaries and rewrites of the caller's own content. It never accepts a
   client-computed value for billing, authorization, entitlement, or grading that crosses
   tenants. Structured outputs are validated on the server against the same schema or enum.
   (Operator decision 3.)
7. **Measured, not assumed.** Every on-device call writes the existing local usage row, so
   savings and quality appear in the existing telemetry. The local-success predictor learns
   where the device's answers are good enough.

## 3. What exists today

### 3.1 Already built

- **The engine.** `brain-embedded/src/promptApi.ts` detects the Prompt API (the current
  `LanguageModel` global and the legacy `self.ai.languageModel`). It also measures input and
  turns the output stream into deltas.
- **The page engine.** `brain-embedded/src/browserEngine.ts` (`promptApiEngine`) works as follows:
  - It is registered in `pageEngines/pageEngineSet.ts` beside bfi and WebLLM.
  - It is served through the ONE page fetch shim.
  - It refuses tools, oversized prompts and unavailable models before the first chunk, so the
    failover to the cloud is invisible.
- **The registry row.** `packages/local-inference/src/runtimes.ts:197` defines `browser` with
  `automaticRank: 40`, `reach: 'page'`, `catalog: 'declared'` and the label `'Gemini Nano'`.
- **The hosts.**
  - Web: `frontend/src/lib/brain/localFirst.ts` (`createHostModelStream`).
  - Rovr: `clients/chrome/src/host/panelServices.ts:194`. The side panel has the Prompt API
    and WebGPU.
- **The `utility` role.** `packages/agent-tools/src/modelRoles.ts:15` already defines
  `utility`. Nothing in the summarizer path stamps it.
- **The VS Code on-device path.** `clients/vscode/src/modelRouting.ts` provides
  `completeOnDevice` and `onDeviceModelAvailable`, which run Synapse. Knowledge judgement
  (`knowledge/knowledgeJudgement.ts:31`) and local research (`localResearch/editorResearchPort.ts`)
  already use them first.

### 3.2 Gaps found

| # | Gap | Where |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | The engine ignores which browser it is in. Edge's `LanguageModel` (Phi-4-mini) is reported as `gemini-nano`, labelled "Gemini Nano" and assumed to have Gemini's 4,096-token fallback window. | `browserEngine.ts:46,51`, `runtimes.ts:199` |
| G2 | The engine is never offered when the browser reports `downloadable`, and the person has no way to fetch the model. A fresh Chrome or Edge install never uses it. | `browserEngine.ts` `probeOnce` |
| G3 | Compaction folds and hand-off packs ride the run's pinned model. `localFirstApplies` is `!call.model && routingMode==='auto'`, so a picked model (often paid) also does every summary. The calls carry no `role`, so `localFirstWorkload` cannot tell they are utility work. | `localFirstTransport.ts:238,260`, `run/brainFold.ts:54`, `windowFit/packForModel.ts:135`, `transcriptSummarizer.ts:31` |
| G4 | A summary's input is a whole transcript middle, which is larger than the built-in model's window. Without chunking, the device can never take it. | `transcriptSummarizer.ts` |
| G5 | Knowledge judgement on web and Rovr always calls `POST /:projectId/knowledge/judge`, often dozens of short JSON calls per review. Only VS Code tries on-device. | `packages/knowledge-client/src/client.ts:311`, `packages/knowledge-browser/src/knowledgeSource.ts:152` |
| G6 | Server-side summaries and rewrites of the user's own content always spend a server model call. | see §6 Part D |
| G7 | No task API is used: Summarizer, LanguageDetector, Translator, Writer, Rewriter or Proofreader. | — |
| G8 | Nothing translates user content. i18n covers only our own UI strings. | — |
| G9 | The on-device path is VS Code-only. `completeOnDevice` is the editor's private seam, not a shared port, so web and Rovr would need a second copy. | `clients/vscode/src/modelRouting.ts` |

### 3.3 Calls that already need no model (no change)

These need no model and stay as they are: chat titles (`chatTitle.ts`), triage
(`brainTriage.ts`), affect (`limbicAffect.ts`), workload classification (`packages/workload`),
commit and PR messages (`specialists/registry.ts`), and the deck rewriters (`chartRewriter.ts`,
`inPlaceFiller.ts`).

## 4. Modality coverage

| Host | Chat turns | Utility tasks | Translation | On-device engine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Chrome, Edge) | ✓ today; gets Part A | Parts B–D | Part E | built-in task APIs → Prompt API → bfi / WebLLM |
| Rovr (Chrome extension; the same build as an Edge add-on) | ✓ today; gets Part A | Parts B–D | Part E | the same as web; the Prompt API is stable for extensions |
| VS Code | n/a (Electron ships no built-in model) | Parts B–D, through the same port | Part E | Synapse (`bfi-node`), through `completeOnDevice` |
| Web on Firefox and Safari | no built-in model | the port returns `null` → today's path | cloud fallback | bfi / WebLLM when present |
| Cloud runs, on-prem | n/a | unchanged (`gatewaySummarizer` on the free Workers AI tier) | n/a | — |

## Part A — The right model, named correctly

### A1. Vendor identity as data

New file: `brain-embedded/src/builtInAi/identity.ts`.

```ts
export type BuiltInAiVendor = 'chrome' | 'edge' | 'unknown';
export interface BuiltInModelIdentity {
  vendor: BuiltInAiVendor;
  model: string;               // 'gemini-nano' | 'phi-4-mini' | 'built-in'
  label: string;               // brand token, not localized: 'Gemini Nano' | 'Phi-4-mini'
  fallbackContextTokens: number;
}
export const BUILT_IN_MODELS: Record<BuiltInAiVendor, BuiltInModelIdentity>;
export function builtInModelIdentity(nav?: NavigatorLike): BuiltInModelIdentity;
```

- **Vendor detection.** The vendor comes from `navigator.userAgentData.brands`
  (`"Microsoft Edge"` → `edge`, `"Google Chrome"` → `chrome`). When `userAgentData` is absent,
  it falls back to a single user-agent regex. Unknown Chromium builds that expose the API are
  `unknown`, labelled "Built-in model".
- **Model ids.** `browserEngine.ts` reads the id and the fallback window from here, instead of
  `BROWSER_ENGINE_MODEL` and `BROWSER_ENGINE_FALLBACK_CONTEXT_TOKENS`. Those two constants are
  deleted and every caller is migrated.
- **The registry label.** The `browser` row's `label` becomes the generic "Built-in model". The
  probe row carries the vendor's label, so the picker shows "Phi-4-mini (Edge)" or
  "Gemini Nano (Chrome)".
- **Refs.** Model refs become `local/browser/<model>`. A pinned `local/browser/gemini-nano`
  stays valid in Chrome. In another vendor, the pin resolves to that vendor's model, with a
  `PIN_REMAPPED` note through `onFallback`. It is never a silent swap.

### A2. Opt-in download

- **Probe.** The probe reports `downloadable` and `downloading` models as rows with a
  `state: 'downloadable' | 'downloading' | 'ready'` field. Routing considers only `ready` rows
  (unchanged behaviour).
- **Picker.** The "On this device" picker (PRD 34) shows a **Download** action for a
  `downloadable` built-in model. Clicking it calls `LanguageModel.create({ monitor })` inside
  that user activation, which the browser requires to start a download. The picker shows
  progress from `downloadprogress` events and lists the browser's stated hardware requirement.
- **No download from a turn.** A chat turn never calls `create()` on a model that is not
  `available`. This rule is unchanged, and it is now tested.
- **Downloading a task model.** The same Download action covers the task APIs whose
  `availability()` reports `downloadable`, such as the Summarizer and Translator language packs.
  It downloads them on the same click.
- **Localization.** All new strings are localized in the five catalogs, in the `localModels.*`
  namespace. The picker row uses theme tokens and fits a 360 px viewport.

## Part B — One `OnDeviceTasks` port

### B1. Contract

New file: `brain-embedded/src/onDevice/onDeviceTasks.ts`. It is exported, and its shape is
pure enough to live in `@builderforce/local-inference` if a second package needs the type.

```ts
export type OnDeviceTaskKind =
  | 'summarize' | 'rewrite' | 'proofread' | 'write'
  | 'detectLanguage' | 'translate' | 'json';

export interface OnDeviceTasks {
  /** Which task kinds can run right now (ready models only). Cheap; memoized like probes. */
  available(): Promise<ReadonlySet<OnDeviceTaskKind>>;
  summarize(text: string, o: { kind: 'tldr' | 'key-points' | 'transcript'; maxWords?: number; context?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<string | null>;
  rewrite(text: string, o: { tone?: 'more-formal' | 'as-is' | 'more-casual'; length?: 'shorter' | 'as-is' | 'longer'; instruction?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<string | null>;
  write(task: string, o?: { context?: string; length?: 'short' | 'medium' | 'long'; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<string | null>;
  proofread(text: string, o?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<string | null>;
  detectLanguage(text: string): Promise<{ lang: string; confidence: number } | null>;
  translate(text: string, o: { from?: string; to: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<string | null>;
  /** Structured output. The result is validated against `schema` before it is returned; invalid → null. */
  json<T>(o: { system: string; user: string; schema: JsonSchema; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<T | null>;
}
```

Every method behaves the same way:

- It returns `null` when the task cannot run here: the API is absent, the model is not ready,
  the input is over budget after chunking (B3), the model refused, or the output failed validation.
- It throws only `AbortError`.
- It never touches the network.
- It records one local usage row (§F).

### B2. Implementations

Each adapter owns one API and its detection. The task-to-adapter order is a registry row, not
a branch.

```
brain-embedded/src/builtInAi/
  identity.ts            A1
  promptApi.ts           moved from src/promptApi.ts (unchanged API; callers migrated)
  summarizerApi.ts       Summarizer
  writerApi.ts           Writer
  rewriterApi.ts         Rewriter
  proofreaderApi.ts      Proofreader
  languageDetectorApi.ts LanguageDetector
  translatorApi.ts       Translator
  structuredPrompt.ts    Prompt API + responseConstraint (json; and the generic fallback for summarize/rewrite/write)
brain-embedded/src/onDevice/
  onDeviceTasks.ts       the contract
  taskRoutes.ts          ON_DEVICE_TASK_ROUTES: kind → ordered adapter ids (data)
  pageOnDeviceTasks.ts   web/Rovr implementation: walks taskRoutes, then the page engines (bfi/WebLLM) via the fetch shim
  completionOnDeviceTasks.ts  implementation over any on-device chat completion (used by VS Code with Synapse; also the page engines' tail)
  heuristicLanguage.ts   detectLanguage's deterministic tail (en / de / es / fr / zh)
  chunkedSummary.ts      B3
```

The default routes:

| Task | Adapter order |
|---|---|
| `summarize` | Summarizer → Prompt API → page engine |
| `rewrite` | Rewriter → Prompt API → page engine |
| `write` | Writer → Prompt API → page engine |
| `proofread` | Proofreader → Prompt API → page engine |
| `detectLanguage` | LanguageDetector → deterministic heuristic tail (`heuristicLanguage.ts`: Unicode script for zh, stop-word frequency for en / de / es / fr; unsupported or short text is `null`; never the model) |
| `translate` | Translator only |
| `json` | Prompt API (`responseConstraint`) → page engine with the schema in the prompt and validation |

`translate` has no generic-model fallback. A small chat model's translation is not good
enough to show unlabelled. `detectLanguage` never asks a chat model either: when the browser
has no `LanguageDetector` (Firefox, Safari, the VS Code webview) its tail is the deterministic
heuristic for the app's five locales, so translation can still be offered there.

- **VS Code** gets `completionOnDeviceTasks` bound to `completeOnDevice`. Its existing
  `completeOnDevice` callers in `knowledgeJudgement.ts` and `editorResearchPort.ts` move onto
  `OnDeviceTasks.json` / `.summarize`. That closes G9 with one seam and no second copy.
  `translate` returns `null` in the editor (Part E uses the cloud path there); `detectLanguage`
  is the deterministic heuristic.
- **Hosts** expose the port once:
  - web: `frontend/src/lib/brain/onDeviceTasks.ts` (`browserOnDeviceTasks()`, beside `browserPageEngines()`);
  - Rovr: `panelServices.ts`;
  - VS Code: the extension's service wiring.

  Consumers receive the port through their existing context or constructor. Nothing imports a host module.

### B3. Chunked summaries

`chunkedSummary.ts` lets a small window take a long transcript:

1. Measure the budget: `measureInputUsage`, or `Summarizer.measureInputUsage`, or ≈4 chars per
   token when the build cannot measure.
2. Split on message boundaries into chunks under 80% of the budget, where the budget is the
   window minus the instruction and the expected reply (reserved, never more than half the
   window). Each chunk is re-measured and split again when it is still over.
3. Summarize each chunk with the same instruction.
4. Summarize the concatenated summaries. Recurse when that is still over budget.
5. Stop and return `null` past `MAX_SUMMARY_CHUNKS = 8` leaf chunks. The caller's existing path
   (the cloud) takes it.

The limit is a constant in `taskRoutes.ts`, not a magic number at a call site.

## Part C — Utility calls go on-device first

### C1. Stamp the role

`transcriptSummarizer.ts` `streamSummaryCompletion` stamps `role: 'utility'` on its request.
That one change covers the compaction fold (`brainFold.ts`), the hand-off pack
(`packForModel.ts` via `runWindowFit.ts`), canvas compaction (`frontend/src/lib/canvasModelPort.ts`)
and local chat Consolidate/Fork (`localFirstPersistence.ts`, `clients/vscode/src/chatSummarizer.ts`).

### C2. Route utility before the pin

`localFirstApplies` becomes `role === 'utility' || (!call.model && routingMode === 'auto')`.
For a utility call, `createHostModelStream` (`hostModelStream.ts`) works as follows:

1. **Try the device first.** Call `OnDeviceTasks.summarize` (chunked, B3). This summarizes
   rather than streaming a chat completion, so the Summarizer API takes it when present.
2. **When the device declines**, behave exactly as today: the run's pin, then Auto under Hybrid.
3. **Under Local only**, step 2 is the other on-device engines only (unchanged).

The summary stays silent (`reasoning: off`, never a visible model turn). It is recorded in the
fold the same way whichever engine produced it, and the fold notes which engine that was.

### C3. Cloud runs are unchanged

`api/src/application/llm/gatewaySummarizer.ts` already uses the free Workers AI pool and stays
as it is. There is no browser on that path.

## Part D — Client-first server routes

### D1. The pattern

1. The client's typed API method tries `OnDeviceTasks` first.
2. When that returns a result, the request carries it in one field, `clientResult`, with a
   provenance stamp `{ engine: 'browser' | 'bfi' | 'webllm' | 'synapse', model: string }`.
3. The route's use case validates and stores it, and skips its model call.
4. Without `clientResult`, the route behaves exactly as today.

Shared server pieces:

- **Validation.** One helper, `api/src/application/llm/clientResult.ts`, parses and validates
  `clientResult`: a length cap, a schema or enum when the output is structured, and a
  provenance whitelist. No route parses it inline.
- **Telemetry.** A stored client result records `llm_usage_log` rows with `residency='local'`
  and zero cost through the existing local-usage writer. Savings ride the existing rows, with
  no new table (both migration tracks already carry the columns).

### D2. Routes in scope

| Route (client → server) | Task | Client-side call | Server-side validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/brain/chats/:id/summarize` (Consolidate/Fork) ← `brainRestPersistence.ts:127`, `useBrainConsolidateFork.ts`, VS Code `useSessionActions.ts` | summary | `summarize({kind:'transcript'})`, chunked | length cap |
| `POST /api/brain/agent-host-sessions/:id/summarize` | summary | the same | length cap |
| `POST /:projectId/knowledge/judge` ← `knowledge-client/src/client.ts:311` | judgement (JSON) | `json({schema: JUDGEMENT_SCHEMA})` per item; the shared prompts already exist | the same schema; enum fields checked |
| Meeting minutes (`meetingRoutes.ts:417` → `meetingIntelligence.ts:197`) | structured minutes | `summarize`, then `json` for action items | schema |
| Dashboard intent (`dashboardsRoutes.ts:140` → `gatewayIntentRefiner.ts`) | metric key | `json({schema: {enum: <tenant's metric keys>}})` | must be one of the tenant's keys, else ignored |
| SOP draft and rewrite (`knowledgeRoutes.ts:888`) | write / rewrite | `write` / `rewrite`; streamed in the UI from the device | length cap |
| Résumé bullet rewrite and merge (`careerAiRoutes.ts:78,94`) | rewrite | `rewrite` / `json` | schema |

**Excluded:**

- Résumé *grading* (`careerAiRoutes.ts:103`) stays server-side, under principle 6.
- Replay summaries (`replayAnalysisRoutes.ts`) stay server-side: the server builds them from
  recording events it holds, and the client has no source text to summarize.
- Admin legal "enhance" stays server-side: it is low volume, admin-only and legally sensitive.
- `classifyTask` (ticket action type) stays server-side. It is lexical first, cached on
  `tasks.action_type`, and it drives dispatch.

## Part E — Content translation (new feature)

### E1. What a person can now do

A person reads a message, comment or imported document written in another language in their
own UI language:

- The text shows **"Translated from Spanish · Show original"**.
- **"Show original"** toggles back. The stored content is never altered.
- Translation is **viewer-side**: each reader sees their own locale.

### E2. Where it appears

These surfaces render one shared `TranslatableText` component:

- multiparty and staffed chat messages, on web and Rovr, and in the VS Code chat webview;
- canvas comments;
- imported documents on the canvas (`ImportCanvasFile`), offered at import as "Translate to <locale>".

`TranslatableText` takes `{ text, contentId }` and owns its own state:

- It detects the language and decides its own visibility. It renders the plain text when the
  language matches the viewer's locale or detection is unsure (confidence < 0.6).
- It translates lazily, when the text enters the viewport.
- It caches per `contentId + locale` in the existing local store (IndexedDB), so each message is
  translated once per device.

### E3. Engines by mode

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Local only | `OnDeviceTasks.translate` only. When that returns `null`, show the original and a muted "Translation needs this browser's built-in translator" hint, which links to the picker's Download. |
| Hybrid / Specific | on-device first. On `null`, call a new cloud fallback (E4). |
| Signed out (anonymous) | the same as Local only. No guest token is minted for translation. |

### E4. Cloud fallback

- **Route.** `POST /api/translate`, with body `{ texts: string[] ≤ 20, to, from? }`. It runs on
  the free Workers AI translation model through the existing free-pool client, never a paid model.
- **Cache.** Results go through `getOrSetCached`, keyed by `sha256(text) + from + to`. The
  keyspace is unbounded, so the entry uses a versioned prefix with a TTL. There is nothing to
  invalidate: a text's translation does not change.
- **Rate limit.** The existing per-tenant limiter applies. A `429` falls back to showing the original.
- **Layering.** The route takes an application port (`TranslateText`). The use case owns
  batching and the cache, and the Workers AI binding sits behind an infrastructure adapter.

### E5. Launch obligations

This is a new capability, so the same pass ships:

- a `release_notes` row (`category=new`) authored through the superadmin ReleaseNotesPanel;
- a blog post in five locales on the `run-your-app-on-the-canvas.md` template, with
  `bf-figure` visuals (a `screen` of a translated message and a `devices` figure across Web,
  Rovr and VS Code) and a "Where it sits in the method" section.

### E-note. Author identity of a message

Whether a message is "mine" or a teammate's is `brain_chat_messages.author_user_id` (migration 1296): the user who
sent a human (`role='user'`) turn, stamped server-side from the authenticated caller, never from the request body.
Machine callers (`agentHost:*`, `embed:*`) and a claimed multi-speaker guest room stamp NULL. NULL means unknown, and an
unknown author is never translated (`ownMessageOf`). This is a third author representation, alongside kernel threads'
`authorKind`/`authorRef` and meeting lines' `metadata.authoredBy`; unifying the three is a consolidation candidate.

Parts A–D are improvements, and get at most a `category=improvement` release note.

## Part F — Measure

- **Who meters.** Web and Rovr have no client usage ledger, so their on-device calls are not
  metered locally; an accepted client result is metered server-side. VS Code meters through the
  run ledger. A client-first host never wires an observing port (it would double count with the
  server's row).
- **Usage rows.** Every on-device task writes the existing local usage row, with
  `residency='local'`, `role='utility'`, the task kind and the engine/model, through the host's
  existing local-usage sink.
- **Quality.** The local-success predictor gets one new signal per utility call:
  `accepted`, or `replaced` (the caller fell through to the cloud after the device answered,
  for example because validation failed).
- **Dashboard.** The existing savings view gains an "On-device utility" series, computed from
  existing rows with no new table: utility calls by engine, and the share served on-device.

## 6. Sequences

**A compaction fold in a run pinned to a paid model (Chrome, Hybrid):**
fold needed → `streamSummaryCompletion({role:'utility'})` →
`OnDeviceTasks.summarize` → Summarizer is ready →
`chunkedSummary`: 3 chunks plus a merge → summary recorded in the fold, engine `browser/gemini-nano` →
local usage row. No paid tokens are spent.

**The same fold in Firefox:** `summarize` → `null` (no API, no page model) →
the pinned model, as today.

**Knowledge review on web, 40 items:** each item → `OnDeviceTasks.json(JUDGEMENT_SCHEMA)` →
valid → `POST /knowledge/judge { clientResult }` → the server validates the schema and stores it.
For the 3 items that fail validation, the request is sent without `clientResult` and the server judges them.

**A Spanish message, viewed by an English reader in Edge:** `TranslatableText` enters the
viewport → `detectLanguage` → `es` (0.97) → `translate` returns `null` (Edge exposes no
Translator) → Hybrid → `POST /api/translate` (cached) → "Translated from Spanish · Show original".

| WS6 | Part F: telemetry series | WS3–WS5 | Sonnet |

Each workstream follows the CLAUDE.md loop: Sonnet implements → Haiku verifies (targeted
typecheck, guards and named test files) → review → fixes.

## 8. Done-checks

1. In Edge with Phi-4-mini ready, the picker shows "Phi-4-mini (Edge)". A tool-less chat turn
   is answered on-device, and the run record names `local/browser/phi-4-mini`.
2. With the model `downloadable`, no chat turn starts a download (a unit test asserts that
   `create` is never called). Clicking Download shows progress, and the model becomes `ready`.
3. With a paid model pinned and the Summarizer ready, a compaction fold spends no paid tokens.
   Its fold record names the browser engine (a unit test with a fake Summarizer, plus a trace
   check).
4. A transcript 5× the device window summarizes through chunks. One past
   `MAX_SUMMARY_CHUNKS` falls through to the pin (a unit test).
5. Every `OnDeviceTasks` method returns `null` when its API is absent, and throws only on abort
   (an adapter conformance test runs against each adapter).
6. `completeOnDevice` has no direct callers outside `completionOnDeviceTasks` (a grep guard).
7. Knowledge judge from web with valid `clientResult` makes no server LLM call. An invalid one
   is rejected with `400`, and the client retries without it (route tests).
8. No D2 route accepts `clientResult` for grading or authorization. Résumé grade ignores the
   field (a route test).
9. `TranslatableText` renders the original under Local only when the device cannot translate.
   It never alters stored content. It works in both themes and at 360 px. All of its strings
   are in five catalogs.
10. `/api/translate` serves a repeat request from cache (a test), uses only the free tier, and
    rejects more than 20 texts.
11. The release note row and the five-locale blog post exist for Part E.
12. The savings view shows the on-device utility series from existing rows.

## 9. Non-goals

- Tool-calling agent turns on the built-in model. A many-tool turn does not fit its window,
  and small models are weak at tool calls. A later PRD may add structured-output emulation
  for turns with few tools, gated by the local-success predictor.
- Multimodal Prompt API input (images, audio).
- Built-in models inside the VS Code webview (Electron ships none). Synapse is the editor's
  equivalent.
- Translating our own UI strings. The catalogs remain the single source.
- Moving cloud-run compaction off `gatewaySummarizer`.

## 10. Measure

- **Primary:** the share of utility calls served on-device, per host and engine, and the
  server model calls avoided on the D2 routes. Both come from existing usage rows.
- **Guardrail:** the `replaced` rate (device answered, cloud redid it) stays under 10% per task
  kind. Above that, the task kind's route is demoted to cloud-first by a registry row.
- **Translation:** messages translated per locale pair, the cache hit rate on `/api/translate`,
  and the share served on-device.

## 11. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A small model writes poor summaries | Utility work only. Chunked summarization keeps each call in-window. The `replaced` rate guardrail demotes a task kind. |
| The APIs change (Edge is experimental and behind flags; Writer, Rewriter and Proofreader are trials) | One adapter per API, feature detection, and `null` on any failure. Nothing depends on a trial API being present. |
| Hardware limits (Chrome needs about 22 GB of free disk and a capable GPU or 16 GB of RAM) | The picker states the requirement. `downloadable` is never forced. |
| A client supplies a forged result | Only the caller's own content. Validated with a schema or enum. Never used for billing, authorization or cross-tenant grading. |
| The first session is slow, or battery drain | Sessions are created lazily. A summary stays off the critical path of a turn, as today. |
| Pin semantics surprise someone | `PIN_REMAPPED` and the fold's engine note make the engine visible. Utility work is off the conversation's visible path. |

## 12. Operator decisions (taken 2026-11-06)

1. **Utility calls go on-device even when a model is pinned.** Yes.
2. **The picker offers an opt-in model download.** Yes; never automatic.
3. **Server routes accept client-produced summaries and rewrites of the user's own content.**
   Yes, with validation and the exclusions in D2.
4. **Content translation is in scope.** Yes (Part E).

- Edge Writing Assistance APIs: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/web-platform/writing-assistance-apis

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-06 — Every VS Code `/api` call acts in the selected workspace or fails; mobile handles the workspace-switch refusals (VS Code 2026.10.135)

- **VS Code.** `fetchAuthed`/`authed` default to `asTenant: "current"` — a call whose token isn't the selected workspace's throws `WorkspaceParkedError` (`workspace_parked`, localized "can't be reached right now, will retry"; `reportExtensionError` skips it) instead of silently reading/writing the key's workspace. Opt-out `"any"` only for person-level calls (`/api/vscode/me`, `GET`/`POST /api/tenants`). The dead `rescopeUnsupported` 404 latch is retired, so the workspace header and the acting tenant can't disagree.
- **Android / iOS `CloudSession`.** One classifier for the switch response: 401 → key rejected (sign-out); `session_stale` → re-mint once, then fall back keeping the selection; `editor_key_required` → drop the selection, raise `workspaceSignInNeeded` (Android shows a localized line under the picker; no sign-out — deliberately unlike VS Code); other 403/404 → drop. A stale in-flight exchange can no longer wipe a newer selection.
- **Not compiled here:** the Android Kotlin build (no SDK on this machine) and the Swift build (no toolchain) — reviewed by Opus, compile in CI/on device. iOS has no workspace picker yet (ROADMAP).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-06 — VS Code model turns and platform tools ran in the editor key's workspace, not the selected one; BYO turns failed `byo_unavailable` (VS Code 2026.10.135 · api 2026.10.98)

- **The bug (chat #47863).** `/api/*` re-scoped to the selected workspace through the minted JWT, but every gateway call (`/llm/v1/*`: model turns, the `builtin_*` MCP relay, models, run outcomes) sent the raw `bfk_` key, and `requireTenantAccess` pinned it to the key's tenant. The selected workspace's connected accounts read `other-workspace`, BYO turns 503'd, and platform tools 403'd on its projects.
- **Server.** A `bfk_` key acts in another workspace via `x-builderforce-workspace` only when `keyMayActInOtherWorkspace` holds (unscoped, server-only, device-flow `client`, has a creator) AND the creator is an active member there (shared `resolveMembership`; role, plan and the live superadmin flag come from the target). Refusals: `editor_key_required` / `workspace_not_member` (403), `workspace_invalid` (400). `client` joins the cached bfk payload (`KEY_CACHE_SCHEMA.bfk` 3). The rate limiter shares the resolver and skips the membership read with no override. `modelsRoutes` propagates the refusals.
- **Re-scope route.** Key-derived JWTs carry `kid`; `POST /api/vscode/tenants/:id/token` reads the key live (one loader, `loadTenantApiKey`) — revoked/foreign key → 401 (incl. same-tenant renewal), cross-workspace needs the same predicate (`editor_key_required`), a device token without `kid` → `session_stale` (client re-mints once).
- **Client.** One header builder (`gatewayAuth.ts`) reading a vscode-free `workspaceSelection.ts` leaf; run-outcomes outbox is workspace-scoped and replays with its queued workspace; `/api/llm/models` and `/api/limbic/block` (which always 401'd on the raw key) use the scoped JWT. Refusals: `editor_key_required` → once-per-key, stale-key-checked sign-out + localized prompt; `workspace_not_member` → ONE `dropWorkspaceSelection` (also mintJwt's 403), scoped to the refused workspace, localized notice. The unused `"key"` outbox identity is gone.
- **Accepted.** Usage rows in workspace B carry the key's id from A, so B's per-key breakdown shows a key not in its list and A's per-key view under-counts it. **Deploy order:** API before the VSIX.
- Reviewed by Opus over five rounds; api 101 + vscode 170 targeted tests, 44/44 api guards, 26/26 frontend guards.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-06 — Knowledge view matches the B-Surface design: station cards and levels, termini, staged fix flow, Try it, Sync and Coverage detail (VS Code 2026.10.133 · memory 2026.10.43)

- **Map.** Station card with Callers/API/Patterns/Enter; drill station → files → symbols (`useDrill`, `drillView`, level path and **Out to**); unfold satellites; termini for data stores and the 8 external services (`EXTERNAL_SERVICE_IDS`, memory 2026.10.42); corridor lanes; label and terminus placement; questions and lenses in drilled levels. No "Loading…" screen: the last-seen graph (24 MB cap) and the outline fill in incrementally.
- **Outline.** Memory `outlineOf` carries `externals`; the API caches the outline under its own `kg-outline:v1` key; `areaRollup` keeps stations ≤ 400.
- **Fix flow.** Preview → queue → checks (tsc, tests, knip) → apply → undo by `fixId` only, with a divergence check and literal pathspecs. Simulate steps or runs a path.
- **Drawers.** API Try it (allow-listed dev origins, SSRF-guarded, bounded body), Sync parity and deltas, Coverage config and test shape, provenance badges and pins. Labels split into `labels/*.ts`.
- **Security (Opus review).** Every host op resolves its root through `rootById` (`safePath.ts`), closing a rootId traversal; the symbols op reads code files only.
- **Moved out:** recorded runtime values (Simulate `recordedValues`, `payloadBytes`, Sync Traces) stay on ROADMAP — no trace recorder exists.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-06 — Model-call failures name the real destination; a failing pick asks for another model; Kimi sign-in launches itself (VSIX 2026.10.132)

- **The misleading error.** On a `local/kimi-code/k3` pick, the editor calls `api.kimi.ai/coding/v1` directly. A request with no response headers within 240s still said "the gateway sent nothing", and it carried the bare `k3`. That created a phantom `k3: 0 turns · 2 failed` row in triage.
  - Provider destinations now read like "Kimi Code (api.kimi.ai) sent no response for 240s". The gateway wording is unchanged.
  - Errors from a pinned local target are rethrown under the full ref.
- **Full failure detail.**
  - `StreamInterruptedError.detail` (`brain-embedded/src/streamFailureDetail.ts`) records: phase (headers or body), destination, elapsed time, request bytes, message and tool counts, bytes received, and per-request credential state.
  - It is stored on the `llm.complete` failure step (`runPolicyTraces.ts`) and printed under "Failed step:" in triage (`brainTriage.ts`).
  - It is also logged to the BuilderForce output channel as `[llm] <ref> failed: … — …` (`clients/vscode/src/llmFailureLog.ts`).
- **A failing pick asks for another model.**
  - `chatErrorAction` → `model_unresponsive`, only for a model the person pinned and only on silence or a dropped connection. In-band provider errors keep their own message.
  - The banner says "<model> isn't responding. Choose another model" and its button opens the existing `/` model menu. This applies on web, VS Code and Rovr.
  - The pin is never switched silently.
- **Kimi auth.**
  - **Credential file.** The CLI reader picks the live login with the latest `expires_at` across all `~/.kimi-code/credentials/*.json`. The CLI now writes `kimi-code-env-<hash>.json`, next to a stale `kimi-code.json` whose grant is dead. A refresh writes back to the same file. A CLI token Kimi refuses is skipped for the session, and the editor falls through to the workspace connection.
  - **Sign-in launch.** A turn with no usable Kimi credential goes straight into the device sign-in (browser plus code), with no toast. A cancel is remembered for the session, and sign-ins are single-flight.
  - **401s.** A Kimi 401 maps to `provider_sign_in` ("Kimi Code needs you to sign in again", with a sign-in button) instead of the BuilderForce `auth` re-exchange.
- **Root cause of the stall itself — still open** (see ROADMAP › Local-first, "Kimi Code `k3` sends no response headers").
  - The live probe found that Kimi holds headers until the first token.
  - A ~75K-token prompt with 67 tools answered in 11–27s, so this is not reproducible by size.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-06 — PRD 40 portable knowledge packs: chat, Synapse, Canvas and the platform pack store (VS Code NEXT)

- **§ The format (v1).**
  - `PortableKnowledgePack` lives in `packages/agent-tools/src/knowledge/portablePack.ts`, with canonical serialization: equal content gives equal bytes, and repeated keys are deduped.
  - The relation key uses a real NUL, the same as memory's `localSnapshotStore`. The shipped key used a literal `\\u0000`.
  - `rebasePackRoot` re-keys a pack onto a new root, recomputing claim keys so a moved folder does not duplicate claims.
  - Update merges by fact key, relation triple and extracted hash. It forgets files deleted from the folder and rebuilds the cards from the merged snapshot.
- **§ VS Code surface.**
  - **Load was broken:** it had never indexed anything (`graphOfPack` passed an empty manifest), and chat never queried a pack's index. Both are fixed, so a loaded pack now answers in chat with no folder open.
  - **Loaded packs:** they re-index one at a time at startup and appear as read-only roots in the knowledge view, where writes are refused with a localized message.
  - **Create:** it skips the review when nothing changed. Pack files and loaded-pack records are keyed by root id, so two folders with the same name no longer collide.
  - **Upload and Remove:** new **Upload Knowledge Pack** and **Remove Uploaded Knowledge Pack** commands.
  - **Translations:** every pack string is in all five l10n bundles.
- **§ Synapse and Canvas consumption: the seam.**
  - `packRetrieval.ts` (`PackRegistry`, `PackRetrievalPort`, `withPacks`, `mergeRecalls`) is the one retrieval path.
  - **Consumers:** VS Code `knowledge.ask`, the context pack and Synapse, web chat `knowledge.ask`, and the Canvas Evermind turn (`EvermindPackPicker`, node data `knowledgePacks`).
  - **`/graph`:** it opens a pack when a project has no reviewed folder.
- **§ OD-2: platform pack store (operator decision 2026-11-06).**
  - An uploaded pack is a project knowledge root under the `pack:` host. There is no new table.
  - Pack facts carry `source = rootId`. `DELETE /:projectId/knowledge/scopes/:rootId` removes only those facts, in batches with one cache bump.
  - Removal needs DEVELOPER or higher and refuses host keys.
- **§ Measure.**
  - `packages/agent-tools/src/knowledge/index/packMeasure.test.ts` runs the PRD's end-to-end proof:
    1. Review a docs folder.
    2. Pack it.
    3. Serialize, then parse.
    4. Load into a clean index.
    5. Ask a question.
  - It asserts that the termination section's content is in the model's context and that the answer cites the file.
- **§ OD-1 and OD-3 (operator decisions 2026-11-06).**
  - **OD-1:** no embeddings in the pack. Packs stay model-agnostic and are re-embedded by hash.
  - **OD-3:** optional provenance (`reviewedBy`, `judgeModel`, `policy`, `reviewedAt`).
    - Create and Update fill it in.
    - Upload stores it in the new nullable `knowledge_scopes.provenance` jsonb column.
    - The Evermind picker and the VS Code pack lists show it.
- **Security fixes found in review before shipping.**
  - Deleting a pack had matched facts by path, which would have deleted other sources' facts on the same paths. It now deletes by provenance only.
  - Removal had no role gate. It now requires DEVELOPER or higher and refuses host keys.
  - Upload no longer overwrites any fact it doesn't own.
  - Pack ids are collision-resistant: a slug plus a short hash.
- **PRD 40 has no open decisions.**
- **Unrelated l10n gap found and closed in the same pass.** 9 `vscode.l10n.t` keys (45 bundle entries) were missing from `clients/vscode/l10n/bundle.l10n*.json`. They are now translated in all five bundles:
  - the interrupted-run notice in `chatParticipant.ts`;
  - the dead-letter commands in `extension.ts`;
  - "BuilderForce Visualization" in `visualizationPanel.ts`;
  - "BuilderForce" in `workspaceSession.ts`.

  The checker reports 0 missing keys across `clients/vscode/src`.

- **One surface (PRD 38 "The visualizer, Option B+").**
  - **Views:** a transit map of lines from each entry point through the layers to stores and outside services; questions in place of lenses; Map, System, Graph, Mind map, Tower 3D, Heat, List and Sequence.

  - A vision call reads the text in the image.
  - Each text is matched by exact source and catalog search, then one import hop.

- **Code-pack data.**
  - New per-file badges: complexity and max complexity, coverage (from coverage files), churn (git), owner (CODEOWNERS), patterns, routes, layer rule and entry.

  - Shell scripts are code.
- **Fix queue safety:** knip fixes run only on a clean work tree, one at a time per root. Strays are restored in `finally`. Saves made during the run are kept and reported.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-03 — The knowledge view showed a file list instead of a visual; selected chip unreadable; review processed files serially (VS Code 2026.10.129 · memory 2026.10.39)

- **List instead of a visual.** `useCan3D` combined `hasWebGL() && !prefersReducedMotion()`, so in a webview without WebGL, or under OS reduced motion, the only renderer was `ListFallback`. The view now offers four modes (`ViewMode`): `graph`, the default, a 2D SVG graph (`graph2d/`, laid out from the deterministic `layout3d` into partition bands); `3d`, offered whenever WebGL exists, where reduced motion only skips the camera flight; `map`, a radial folder mind map (`map/`); and `list`.
  - Pan and zoom live in `usePanZoom`: a re-fit happens on a new layout, and a drag writes the viewBox through a ref.
  - Clicks resolve to the nearest node centre (`hitTest.ts`), and only the top 25 nodes are tab stops; arrow keys walk the rest (`useRoving`).
- **Insights.** `insights/insightsModel.ts` is pure and needs no model call. It computes headline metrics with the lens that explains each, the composition of the graph, fan-in/fan-out hotspots, cross-partition coupling and findings by kind. These render as tiles and SVG bar charts in the aside in every mode. The empty right column is gone.
- **Unreadable selection.** The VS Code webview mapped `--bf-accent-soft` to the opaque `--vscode-textLink-activeForeground`, which put light-blue text on a light-blue fill. It is now a `color-mix` tint, and `chip(active)` uses the text colour.
- **Diagnostics.** `graphDiagnostics.ts` reports WebGL and reduced motion separately, nodes drawn versus total and why, kind counts and the last review's throughput.
- **Serial review.** memory `reviewDirectory` prefetches each file's read and extraction through `prefetchOrdered`, bounded at 8 by default and order-preserving. Judging, writes and the manifest stay in file order. Same-hash extraction is serialised so the extract cache never loses an entry. An abort ends at a file boundary after started work settles.
- **Also.**
  - Main CI had been red since `867f254f2` made finding rows lazy: `KnowledgeGraphView.lenses` and `CanvasKnowledgeSurface` read unexpanded rows. Their setup now expands the groups (`expandAllFindings`); expected values are unchanged.
  - `cmp`/`round` were consolidated into `order.ts`.
  - Every consumer moved to memory and memory-engine `^2026.10.39`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-02 — VS Code panel stalled on "Connecting…", and a Hybrid pick silently became free models (VS Code 2026.10.126 · api 2026.10.97 · frontend 2026.10.102)

- **Stall.** `buildWorkspaceInit` awaited every step serially, and the first `init` frame waited for all of them. The ~5 minutes matches undici's 300 s `headersTimeout`, so an unbounded fetch is the likely cause; which one was not captured. Each step now runs concurrently under `initBudget` (2.5 s). A late real answer re-pushes init, capped per surface, and a slow step logs `[init] <step>`. `fetchAuthed`, the personality block and the Kimi refresh are bounded.
- **Degraded frames and tenancy.** A token-less frame keeps the webview's token only for the same tenant (`initFrameAuth`). `boundToken` refuses a token that does not act as the selected workspace, on init and on `token.refresh`, and a mint overtaken by sign-out returns nothing.
- **Silent swap.** A Hybrid pick that cannot be authorized sends a redacted reason through the existing fallback notice, once per run (`pickUnavailable`, `modelFallbackDetail`).
- **a6937d561 repaired.** Removed the unimported `connectedAccounts` wiring in `gateway.ts` / `localModels.ts`, the MiniMax and Moonshot placeholder credential sources and resolvers, the duplicate Anthropic resolve, and the four `*-code` runtimes that had no credential source.
- **Also.** G27 self-check counts only its own probe; every consumer on `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory` 2026.10.38; harness tsconfig paths; frontend cycle, `api-transport` and layering guards (Brain panel hooks moved to `components/brain/hooks`).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-01 — Knowledge review survives agent edits, view changes and slow plans (VS Code 2026.10.122)

- **Auto-swap.** A mutating `run.tool` moved an unpinned panel to Changes mid-review. `visualizationViewState` now has `reviewing`: the mutation counts, the view holds. `useKnowledgeHost` counts live reviews (`reviewCount`), because a superseded review's cleanup runs after its replacement starts.
- **A view change stopped the review.** The Knowledge view unmounted, and `useReviewRun`'s cleanup aborted the run. `VisualizationPanel` now keeps it mounted under `hidden` in `.bf-viz__knowledge-slot`.
- **`knowledge.call` timeout.** `plan` ran inside the 300s request. The host now answers at once (`planOver`) and posts `planned` or `failed` on a caller-named stream. After Stop, the source waits `ABORT_GRACE_MS` for the host's terminal event, so a silent host cannot hold the panel.
- **Idle redraw.** `GraphScene` used `frameloop="always"`, so it drew every frame at up to 2x density. It is now `demand`, with `invalidate()` in `FlyTo` and `Nodes` and `RepaintOnShow` for a hidden-then-shown canvas.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-01 — False "Continue with guidance / Stop the run" pauses (VS Code 2026.10.121 · brain-embedded 2026.10.75 · run-guards 2026.10.5)

All 78 pauses recorded in one operator's chat history were `no_progress`; none came from an undone edit or a repeated failure.

- **Cause.** `NoProgressTracker` counted only a new path, a test write or a changed check, so edits to known source files and mutating commands were idle and a working run tripped after 4 turns. `ProgressDetector.trips` never fell, so three unrelated trips in a long run ended in a pause.
- **Progress is ground or churn.** Ground is the old rule. Churn is a successful change with a fingerprint not seen before, and read-only shell earns none. `CHURN_TURNS` (12) bounds consecutive churn, and a trip does not clear it, so drift still reaches the pause.
- **Ladder.** `LADDER_RESET_TURNS` (8) ground turns with no signal clear `trips`; churn cannot. `tripsBySignal` survives the reset in snapshots.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-01 — Local-first v3 store hardening: torn-fsync detection, generation-id identity, bounded EPERM retry (local-first)

The four v3-review store-hardening items (ticket 6282) shipped in `packages/local-first`:

- **Torn / failed-fsync frame.** Writes are length-prefixed/framed so a torn tail from a failed fsync is detectable and ignored, and fsync-failure handling never corrupts a committed frame another window may have applied.
- **File identity.** The weak `(ino, birthtimeMs)` identity (unreliable on NTFS, where inode numbers are reused) is replaced by a base-generation id — an opaque per-compaction value (`mintJournalGeneration`, `crypto.randomUUID` when available) recorded in the first frame of the journal. A reader tracks the generation id rather than filesystem metadata.
- **EPERM-on-rename.** A Windows EPERM on the compaction rename no longer triggers a full rewrite retry on every commit — the retry is bounded and falls through (keeps the last-good copy, retries on the next compaction window).
- **`storeContract.ts`.** Now documents that `read`/`scan` return live, committed Maps (views of the committed state) that callers must not mutate.

Verified: `packages/local-first` `tsc --noEmit` clean; the package's vitest suite passes **559/559**. See ROADMAP for the remaining local-first items still open (damaged-journal rescans, event-loop gaps, scans with no early exit).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-01 — Unbound chat rows no longer keep a full payload copy in the pending queue (brain-embedded)

`journalWrite` in `brain-embedded/src/localChat/journal.ts` appended a journal event with the full `record.payload` for every unbound write, even though an unbound event is never sent (the coordinator refuses an unbound partition). On one machine 21,370 of these events held 39 MB and were carried through every compaction. The unbound frame now persists only a **marker** — ids, entity type, operation, a payload size, and an FNV-1a content hash of the real payload — with `payload: null`. The full payload stays owned by the record (and, once bound, by the authoritative `queueImport` / outbox send path), so after a later bind a previously-unbound row still imports and sends with its real payload, rebuilt from the record by `bindChatHistoryForSync`, never read back out of the marker. This is consistent with the G03 record-and-sync-in-one-frame contract: a bound frame still commits the record and its event together; only the never-sent unbound event drops its payload copy. On-disk format stays backward compatible — old frames that still carry a payload remain valid journal events and are read unchanged. One existing test was updated (the local-usage journal assertion now checks the record, since the journaled event is the marker), and a new test pins both halves: an unbound write leaves no full-payload copy, and a later bind still sends the row with its real payload from the record.

- **Measured on a copy of that store (20,847 records):** one commit p50 23 ms, p95 29 ms, against about 10.4 s run twice before. First import 3.3 s, later opens 1.5–3.4 s. Record, message and event counts matched through import, reopen and compaction.
- **Delta journal.** New file `local-first-v3.journal` holds `BFJF2` delta frames; `BFJF1` snapshots stay readable. The v2 file is imported under the lock and never written to, because an old window would truncate delta frames. Copy-on-write transactions, `scan`/`scanPending`, `selectRecords`/`selectPending`, `onCommit`, `applyDelta` and change hints replace whole-store clones; compaction is chunked, tail-based (8192 frames or 64 MB), and other windows read the tail.
- **Windows on the old extension lose nothing.** `local-first-v3.import.json` records the imported v2 state; on open, `localFirstLegacyMerge.ts` merges only what an old window changed since then, so deletions stay deleted and acknowledged events are not re-added.
- **Damage never truncates.** A bad frame with data after it, or a base that never closes, is copied to `local-first-v3.journal.corrupt-<timestamp>` and rebuilt from the best source (`localFirstRebuild.ts`): this window's state, the sound prefix, then the newer of the cache and v2. With none, the open rejects `local_first_store_corrupt`. A torn tail recovers as before.
- **Lock waits.** Commits wait 15 s and open waits 60 s, because compaction measured 2.7 s and import 3.3 s against the old 1.5 s limit. Short writes now fail the append or compaction.
- **Two journal stores retired.** `offlineLocalFirstStore.ts`, `createJournaledLocalFirstStore`, `JournalIo` and `JournaledLocalFirstStore` are deleted.
- **Local store rewriting every message on every commit:** closed by the delta journal. The second payload copy stays open as the unbound-rows entry in ROADMAP.md.
- **Typing.** `createComposerDraftStore` with `useDraftText`/`useDraftIsEmpty`: only the text box re-renders per key on VS Code, web and Rovr; render-count tests hold it in `packages/brain-ui`, `frontend` and `clients/chrome`.
- **First bubble.** `usePendingTurns`/`announceTurn` show the turn before the commit on VS Code, Rovr, and the web Brain and guest panels; `useBrainChats` shows `originalRequest` optimistically.
- **Model shown, wording corrected.** `servedModelLabel`, `servedBy`/`liveModel` in the timeline on the same surfaces. Hosted models called from your machine (Kimi Code) are no longer labelled as running on this device: `runsOnDevice` is separate from `isLocalModelRef`, and `hostedTip` plus "Your account" are translated in VS Code, web and Rovr.
- `packages/brain-ui/vitest.config.ts` dedupes React, which the linked `brain-embedded` otherwise loads twice.

Many entry points → ONE agent (`packages/agent-run`) → ONE kernel (`packages/agent-loop`). Nothing outside those two packages imports `runAgentLoop`, and `check:one-execution` enforces that with an empty allowlist.

Then `runLoop.ts`, `completeTurn.ts`, `finalAnswerHook.ts`, `toolCallHooks.ts`, `turnMenu.ts`, `runEngine.ts`, `runEnginePreference.ts`, `runViaAgent.ts`, `runStorePort.ts` and `vscodeAdapter.ts` were deleted, with `BRAIN_RUN_ENGINE` and `builderforce.agent.engine`.

The guard now covers the oracle by path, judges each push from the last successful Release so a cancelled run is not forgiven, fails closed in CI, and has a unit test. ### Moved from the spec

Moved word for word from [PRD 35](./docs/specs/35-prd-one-agent-one-kernel.md). Section numbers are kept, so a `PRD 35 §x` citation in the code resolves here or in the 2026-10-31 entry. The text describes the plan as written; where it says `runLoop` is the default, read it as history.

#### 4. What is left

```
WS4 chat adapters ─┬─► WS7 enforce + delete + done
WS5 channels ──────┘
```

##### WS4 — VS Code + Rovr / Web chat adapters (highest-traffic)

VS Code, web and Rovr all build a `BrainRunRequest` and call `startRun`, so one seam moves all three. The canvas already proves the shape: a host that runs its own tools sits on `runAgent` through closed `PlatformTools` and a `DeliveryLedger`.

- **The seam.** `startRun` drives the run through one engine choice: `runLoop` (today) or `runViaAgent`. `prepareRunLoop` stays and runs for both: it assembles what the canvas assembles for itself (system prompt, transcript, catalog, recall, the deterministic and memory answers). Its output becomes `RunTask.transcript`, `RunPolicy` and the ports.
- **The opt-in, until the ship gate.** The default stays `runLoop` until the gate below passes. A device opts in: the VS Code setting `builderforce.agent.engine`, and `builderforce.runEngine` in `localStorage` (or `?runEngine=agent`, which stores it) on web and Rovr. The choice is read once at the host's request site and carried on `BrainRunRequest`. It selects the engine and nothing else. The ship gate flips the default, and the same workstream deletes `runLoop` and the switch.
- **The parity oracle.** 20 test files drive `startRun`. With `BRAIN_RUN_ENGINE=agent` they run unchanged against the agent, and what fails is the list of real gaps. It starts as a baseline in the hand-off note and burns down to zero. A failure that cannot be closed goes to the planning model by name.

| What the Brain's hooks do | Where it lives on the agent |
|---|---|
| The streamed turn: live deltas, activity, the `llm.complete` step, window packing, usage, BYO banners, the local-first trace | `ModelTransport`, sharing one extracted turn recorder with `completeTurn.ts`, never a copy |
| Steers in front of a turn, saved as they are read | `SteeringSource`, over `takeRunSteering` and `persistSteer` |
| Compaction and the durable fold marker | `policy/compaction`; the note reaches the sink on `context.compacted` so `persistFoldMarker` still runs |
| Tool selection, pins, the forced menu | Closed `PlatformTools`: `schemas` withdraws `hand_off` when it closes, `selection` carries the request query and the pinned names |
| Router, alias, confirm gate, one-ticket attach, `hand_off`, ticket on first edit, auto-link, placeholder, completion and failure advisories, ledgers | `PlatformTools.execute`, by extracting those steps out of `beforeDispatch.ts` and `dispatchTool.ts` so both engines call the same code |
| Read and write dedupe with replay | `policy/tools` read coverage. `CacheServedStreak` is missing from the agent and is ported |
| A terminal `ask_user`, narration kept as its own block | `ToolExtension.terminalTurn`; narration is saved when the transport sees a turn with calls |
| Stop hook, ship gate, review gate, restated reply | `DeliveryLedger` rungs. `rungs` may become async (the stop hook awaits). A rung may enter the verify phase |
| The delegation recovery, stall nudges and failover | `policy/subagents` and `policy/stall`, with `pickFallbackModel` behind `fallbackSurface` |
| **Coder re-ask** on the first edit of an analysis turn | **Missing from the agent.** Ported into `policy/model`, switched by `RunPolicy` data, so the canvas is unchanged |
| **The run's USD cap** (warn at 80%, contained stop) | **Missing from the agent.** Ported as agent policy from `runSpendBudget.ts`, as `RunPolicy.budgets.usd` |
| Image attachments on a turn | `RunMessage.content` is text only. Gains additive `parts`, which the on-prem contract also needs |
| The settled reply, Evermind learn and reconcile, `onActivity`, a thrown error's actionable verdict, the forced final answer | The adapter, after `runAgent` returns. A failed outcome rethrows the transport's own error so `chatErrorAction` still reads it |

- **Owns.**
  - `brain-embedded/src/run/*`.
  - The `brain-embedded/src/runStore/runLoop.ts` policy (moved, then deleted after the ship gate).
  - `clients/vscode/src/run/vscodeAdapter.ts`, `rovrRunHost.ts`, `useBrainConversation.ts` and the `brainRunHost.ts` call site.
- **Accept.**
  - Conformance passes.
  - The brain-embedded, VS Code and frontend tests pass unchanged on both engines.
  - The VSIX is packaged and installed.
  - **Ship gate (operator, 2026-10-31, replaces the telemetry week):** a review of the agent engine against `runLoop`, behaviour by behaviour, finds no unexplained difference, and the unit tests prove both engines work as before. Then flip the default, delete `runLoop` and the engine switch. After that §8.1 is a live watch with no way back to `runLoop`: a regression is fixed forward.

##### WS5 — On-prem channels

- **Owns.** The `agent-runtime/src/builderforce/agent-loop/agent-loop.ts` policy (moved) and its call sites.
- **Do.** Channels and cron call `runAgent` through `agent-runtime/src/run/onPremAdapter.ts`, as tickets already do.

- Delete every source a WS2 module ported from that its adapter has not already deleted, including the `brain-embedded/src/runSteering.ts` twin.

- The planning model moves the ROADMAP entry to DONE.md.

#### 3.3 Done means

| Check | Passes when |
|---|---|
| Conformance suite | One scripted task (fake model, in-memory provider) through all four adapters gives the same `RunEvent` trace and `RunOutcome`. The cloud adapter runs it one step per tick and still matches. A board-dispatched variant with `signoff` set is included. |
| `check:one-execution` | Nothing outside `packages/agent-run` imports `runAgentLoop` or any `policy/*` module. |
| Adapter size | Each adapter < ~300 lines, only builds ports. One loop-bearing file remains: `runLoop`, deleted at the ship gate. |
| Parity | Every pre-existing behaviour test passes **unchanged** (§5.1). `check:tests-unchanged` enforces; the test count does not drop. |
| Matrix | The design's final matrix holds: one policy module per row, entry points differ only by port. |
| No lost capability | Every §7 row's old tests pass against its new home before the old home is deleted. |
| Telemetry | Every entry point writes the uniform outcome row (§8.2); VS Code stays at or better than baseline (§8.1). |
| Efficiency | The §8.4 reference scenario replays through every adapter within its budgets: first spawn by parent turn 5, ≤15 parent turns, 0 covered-read stubs for unseen lines, 0 repo-resolution errors, 0 shell reads of workspace files, and no readiness claim left unkept for more than 2 turns. A stop settles the run in ≤2 s with no child process left, and a mid-run steer reaches the next model call. |

#### 5. Rules for every agent on this program

1. **Port, then delete.** Port the missing behaviour into the agent, prove it, delete the old
   copy in the same workstream. No parallel copies, and no "duplicate remains" entries.
2. **Tests run unchanged.** Existing behaviour tests are the parity oracle. You may retarget
   an import from a deleted module to its replacement. You must not change an input or an
   expected value. A failing test means you fix the source. If a behaviour change is
   genuinely intended, stop and ask the planning model. The full procedure is §5.1.
3. **No new loop, no policy in an adapter, no `entryPoint` branching.** `RunPolicy.entryPoint`
   is a telemetry label only.
4. **No god classes.** Under ~400 lines per module, one reason to change.
5. **Model roles** are a hard rule, and CLAUDE.md states them. Never a full vitest sweep.
6. **Commits.** On `main` in the main checkout, no worktrees (operator, 2026-10-31). No Co-Authored-By line.
   Bump the version of every package you change, and never reuse a version. Wait for CI
   before pushing over a running build.
7. **Docs.** Only the planning model edits ROADMAP.md, DONE.md and this PRD. Put contract or
   scope requests in your hand-off note.
8. **Hand-off note** (end of every workstream, in the PR description):
   - what moved where (as §7 rows);
   - which tests prove it, with their pass output;
   - files deleted;
   - contract requests;
   - telemetry deltas, where relevant.

##### 5.1 Proving every capability with tests

Every capability moves under the same five steps. A workstream is not done until each §7 row it
owns has been through all five.

1. **Baseline on the old home.** Before porting, run the row's tests against the code that
   exists today and record the pass output in the hand-off note. A test that is not green on
   the old home is not an oracle. Report it to the planning model before going further.
2. **No test, write one first, against the old home.** If a capability has no test, write a
   characterization test that pins today's observable behaviour: inputs, tool calls, events,
   the outcome. It must pass on the old home, and it lands in the same branch **before** any
   porting commit. From then on it is an existing test and follows rule 2. Never write the test
   against the new home first. A test written to fit new code proves nothing about parity.
3. **Port, then run the same tests on the new home.** The same files, the same assertions.
   Rule 2 is the only allowed edit: an import moved from a deleted module to its replacement.
4. **Run them through every entry point that has the capability.** A capability that more
   than one entry point uses also gets a conformance case (§3.3). The same scripted task gives
   the same `RunEvent` trace and `RunOutcome` on each adapter, and on the cloud adapter at
   `maxSteps: 1`.
5. **Delete the old home only after steps 3 and 4 are green.** Deletion happens in the same
   workstream.

Not allowed in a test file on this program:
- changing an input, a fixture's content or an expected value;
- deleting a test or a test file, or merging tests so fewer cases run;
- adding `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo` or `it.fails`, or wrapping an assertion in a conditional;
- loosening a matcher: `toEqual` → `toMatchObject`, an exact string → `stringContaining`,
  `toHaveBeenCalledWith` → `toHaveBeenCalled`, an exact count → `toBeGreaterThan`;
- adding mocks that stub out the behaviour under test.

A test that reaches into a deleted module's internals, such as a private helper or an SDK
option object, is retargeted to the **public seam that carries the same behaviour**. It keeps
the same inputs and the same expected values. If no seam can carry them, it goes to the
planning model. It is never rewritten to fit.

Checked by reviewers and CI:
- The Opus or Fable review gets the test-file diff on its own and rejects any hunk that isn't
  an import line.
- The Sonnet verify agent reports the test count per file before and after. A drop fails the
  workstream.
- WS1 adds `check:tests-unchanged` (report mode, enforced in WS7). It diffs every test file
  touched on a `feat/agent-run-ws*` branch against main and fails on any changed line that
  isn't an `import` / `vi.mock` path, and on any new skip marker.

#### 8.1 Telemetry baseline (the live watch after WS4)

Failure rate 4.4% (20 of 452). Steps per run ≈ 43 (failed runs ≈ 62). Prompt-cache hit 23%.
After cut-over VS Code should stay at or better than these. Reproduce with
`api/scripts/telemetry-baseline.cjs` (WS6). How to attribute rows: VS Code = `tenant_api_key_id`
whose key kind is `vscode` (its `surface` is clamped to `web`); cloud = `surface='cloud'`
with `execution_id`; @-reply = `use_case='brain_agent_reply'`. Telemetry tables live on
`NEON_TRANSACTIONAL_DATABASE_URL`. Queries are read-only and never print the connection URL.

**What `steps` means.** The baseline is `AVG(steps)` on `run_model_outcomes`. On the old loop that is every completed model turn (non-error `llm.complete` rows). The kernel's `state.step` counts only turns that acted, and cloud and canvas tests pin that count, so it stays. VS Code, web and Rovr on the agent engine report the old loop's number, with one row per run (`engineRunRow.test.ts`). Compare chat entry points with the baseline only; a cloud or canvas `steps` is not comparable to it.

PRD.
