- Second copies replaced by imports: `stopIntent`, the `windowedCap` table, the 469-line `packHandoff` copy, budgets and reserve, and `isModelRole`. Dead steering exports were deleted.
- Faithful ports:
  - the on-prem reserve floor is 20,000 (from agent-settings);
  - the brought-along tests were restored to source where a seam carries them (recallQuery, inRunVerify, delegationRequest, steering, stall, compactMessages' window case, `ensureCompactReserveTokens`). The cases that cannot yet run unchanged are logged in ROADMAP (PRD 35 agent-run).
- Guards:
  - `check:one-execution` now matches real imports, reports reach-ins into `policy/*` and any second `runAgentLoop` driver inside agent-run, and has `--enforce`;
  - `check:tests-unchanged` also sees uncommitted and deleted tests, compares each brought-along test with its source, and counts cases.
- Verified (Sonnet): agent-loop 211 tests; agent-run 310 tests; brain-embedded 140 + 75 targeted tests; clients/vscode 64; agent-tools 64; run-guards 92; api 31 targeted tests. Typechecks for api, brain-embedded, clients/vscode, agent-tools, run-guards and agent-runtime are clean, and all 42 api guards pass.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-28 — VS Code chat stops sending local chat ids to the platform and re-sending refused tokens (VSIX 2026.10.112)

**Symptom.** The BuilderForce output channel filled with `GET /api/brain/chats/6/tickets → 404 — Chat not found` on every rail refresh, and with bursts of `401 — Invalid or expired token` across the rail's files, members, agents, tickets and approvals reads. The local store showed local chat 6 bound to server chat 172.

**The local view key leaked into server calls.**
- The composer's `#`-ticket typeahead read `listTickets(chatId)` with the local id. It now reads by `serverChatId`, from the rail (`clients/vscode/webview/src/chat/useTicketRail.ts` `typeaheadTickets`). The composer makes no ticket call of its own.
- Tagging a ticket called `ticketAdapter.linkTicket(localId)`, which linked it to whichever server chat happened to be #6. It now goes through the rail's one `linkTicket`, which binds the local chat first. The opened-ticket auto-link uses the same function (`useHostIntents`).
- The webview's memory hooks (`useChatMemory.ts`) passed the local id into Evermind recall, answer lookup and answer pricing. They now pass `serverChatIdOf(activeChat)`. This path was dormant while the host drives runs.
- `serverAddressedChatIds.test.ts` pins all three.

**The 401 "re-mint" did not re-mint.**
- The webview's `token.refresh` called `getTenantJwt`. That returned the cached token, which is unexpired by the client's clock and was the one the gateway had just refused.
- `token.refresh` now calls `refreshTenantJwt`, a forced exchange.
- Exchanges are single-flight per mode in `bfApi.ts`, so a burst shares one mint.
- `clearJwt` bumps an epoch, so a mint still in flight at sign-out does not write the old identity's token.
- The webview's `refreshToken` is single-flight.
- The rail adapter, `apiReq` and the memory hooks now pass the promise-returning refresher, so a read that hit a 401 is retried once instead of staying empty.

Still open: the bound chat's rail has no local copy offline (G21, Consolidated Gap Register).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-28 — The knowledge graph, deterministic prefetch and the deterministic knowledge index (builderforce-memory 2026.10.29–31 · api 2026.10.90 · frontend 2026.10.95 · brain-embedded 2026.10.69 · brain-ui 2026.10.29 · agent-runtime 2026.10.21 · Rovr 2026.10.32 · VSIX 2026.10.111)

Specs: [PRD 38 rev 3](docs/specs/38-prd-knowledge-graph.md), [deterministic-prefetch.md](docs/design/deterministic-prefetch.md) and [deterministic-knowledge-index.md](docs/design/deterministic-knowledge-index.md). The operator decided the surface name `knowledge`, a review budget of 200, fact delete for the author or an admin, and keeping unlinked folders local until they are linked.

**Knowledge is memory.** builderforce-memory gains the `/knowledge` subpath:
- `buildGraph` is bounded and byte-deterministic, and `reviewDirectory` / `planReview` run through the one `ingest` `ParserRegistry`.
- Partitions and verdicts, `traceGraph`/`toMermaid`, findings, `toCards` and `localSnapshotStore` come with it.
- The docs pack reuses the builtin parsers' new optional `extract`.
- Store judgement, compute perception: extracted output is cached by content hash and never stored. Model facts go stale when their source hash changes, and re-review works per section.

**The deterministic index.**
- One total order (`compareHits`) across every ranker, and HNSW levels drawn from the id.
- A LEANN-style knowledge index: a pruned CSR graph, int8 traversal, selective float recompute, the exact → lexical → dense cascade, `expand`, and an exact-scan mode below 20k cards so Workers pay no construction cost.
- The cloud `repoSymbolVectors` brute force is folded into `KnowledgeIndexPort`, with its tests unchanged.
- Desktop `bf-index` gets the same comparator.
- Locally, the embedder chain is Synapse → Evermind CPU → Ollama, used only when warm, with distinct fingerprints.

**The platform.**
- Migrations 1278 (`project_fact_relations`, `knowledge_scopes`, `project_facts.created_by`/`origin`) and 1279 (`previous_digest`).
- `writeKnowledge` is the single writer, with origin derived server-side.
- Routes: scopes, graph (with `at` for the Compare baseline), facts plus viewer rights, write, judge, search, extracted output and the code-analysis snapshot. All are tenancy-checked, cached on `knowledgeVersion`, and mounted under both the person and agent-host doors.
- R2 keeps one object per source path (no manifest race) and an immutable review snapshot per digest.
- Run-end facts carry anchors with content hashes.

**Packages and hosts.**
- `@builderforce/knowledge-client` is the one HTTP client. `@builderforce/knowledge-graph-view` is the 3D view: lenses, layer/path trace, findings with Fix with agent, Compare, and a list fallback. `@builderforce/knowledge-browser` holds the shared browser host: the worker review, the IndexedDB manifest, upload and File System Access sources, and the labels.
- `agent-tools/knowledge` holds the code pack (repo-map and analyzer adapters, N-layer partitions, generated dependency-cruiser rules), the shared review runner, judge, fact rights, root ids, skip list and index host.
- The web canvas `knowledge` surface, with the VFS / Cloud Drive / upload sources. The VS Code Knowledge view (now the panel default), Review with BuilderForce on folders, and `/review` / `/graph`. The on-prem host. The Rovr Knowledge tab.
- `CodeAuditVisualizer` is now an adapter over the view, with its test unchanged. `buildChangeGraph` is keyed by knowledge root id plus path.

**Prefetch.**
- `packages/prefetch` holds the gate: tier 1 exact, tier 2 lexical plus logistic, tier 3 local logprob when warm, per-action calibration and `runGate`. `answerWithoutModel` is replaced by `PrefetchPort` at every caller.
- Shared executors cover typecheck, lint, dup/cycles/dead code through the code pack, boundaries, audit, secrets, related tests, and write actions (lint fix, scaffold, codegen, codemod, format) that are always confirmed with a chip showing the plan numbers.
- The `knowledge.*` rows run on VS Code, on-prem, web and Rovr.
- Avoided calls go on the savings ledger, and the Pipeline route report has a gate column.

Also shipped: the release note (migration 1280) and the blog post "Point it at a folder and see what it knows" in five locales.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-28 — Stop before start: the last windows (brain-embedded 2026.10.68 · brain-ui 2026.10.28 · VSIX 2026.10.108)

Round-4 review of the "Stop the run" fix (below) found six gaps; all closed:
- **Stop during the change-set baseline was dropped.** The editor start captures a git baseline before the host claims the chat, and `runSteer.stop` ignores an unclaimed key. `clients/vscode/src/hostStartGate.ts` (`gateStarts`) holds a Stop (or a typed stop) asked in that window and hands it to the host as soon as `host.start` has claimed the key; `brainRunHostPorts.ts` routes its start through it. Test: `hostStartGate.test.ts`.
- **Wrong caption.** A before-start row carries `stoppedBeforeStart` metadata (`isStoppedBeforeStart`); `MessageRows` shows the new `stoppedBeforeStart` label in place of the body (labels.ts, brainChatLabels.ts, 5 l10n bundles, 5 frontend catalogs).
- **Not mirrored on the host path.** `stopBeforeStart` now `recordAppended`s the row, so `run.sync` carries it.
- **Counted as a model reply.** `isModelReply` excludes it (Retry, newest-reply actions, triage claim detectors).
- **No durable stop step.** `stopBeforeStart` persists the `agent.stopped` step row ahead of the answer row, so reopened-chat diagnostics count it.
- **Draft chat's first send.** `useBrainConversation.stop` marks the draft (`null`) and `send` moves the mark to the chat id `ensureChatId` returns.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-27 — "Stop the run" stops the run (brain-embedded 2026.10.66 · VSIX 2026.10.106)

- **Symptom.** In VS Code chat #6 the WS8p pause asked "Continue with guidance / Stop the run". The person chose Stop, and the run kept going.
- **Cause.** An `ask_user` question ends the run, and the question becomes its reply. The answer then reached an idle chat as an ordinary send, and `useBrainConversation.send` launched a run on it. The editor's `runSteer.ts` already treats a stop as the Stop button, but only while a run is live. Two other paths would have started a run on the same trailing "stop": reopening the chat (the auto-reply on load) and Retry.
- **Fix.** One rule, `brain-embedded/src/userTurnRuns.ts`:
  - `startsRun(text)` = `!stopIntent(text)`, from `@builderforce/run-guards`, the same matcher `runSteer.ts` uses.
  - `send` keeps a stop turn as the answer and launches nothing.
  - The auto-reply skips a trailing stop. It was lifted into `useAutoReplyTrailingTurn.ts`, so `useBrainConversation.ts` shrank from 691 to about 665 lines.
  - `unansweredTurnIndex` (moved here, re-exported) treats a trailing stop as answered, so Retry never relaunches it.
- **The shared turn door** (`useChatTurns`): a stop typed mid-run now stops the run on every surface that shares it, instead of waiting in the queue as the next turn. On the web it is the Stop button and is not saved as a message; in the editor the host shows it in the chat.
- **Review follow-ups (brain-embedded 2026.10.67 · VSIX 2026.10.107).**
  - A mid-run stop is the Stop and is never held, so nothing is stranded behind it (`useQueuedTurns` flushes one turn per run edge).
  - A new `isDirected` port means a stop addressed to a participant is never the Stop. The editor and the web panel pass it.
  - A stop the host routes (the editor's run) still clears the panel's queue.
  - `conv.stop` drops a launch whose send was still getting ready (`cancelledLaunchRef`), and the editor and the web panel now stop through it.
  - A stop carrying an attachment runs, so send and reload agree.
  - The Creation Canvas's `startCanvasTurn` applies `startsRun` too.
  - A Stop is honoured in every window before a run starts:
    - while a send is persisting;
    - after `prepareRun`: `launch` re-checks, and a `launchingRef` covers the auto-reply and Retry too;
    - during the host's setup: `runSteer.stopped(key)` is checked inside `runTurn`'s `try`, so its cleanup still runs;
    - during the editor's limbic fetch: `useChatSend`'s `preparing` clears only in the same commit as `conv.sending`, so the queue never flushes into the gap. A send dropped there goes back to the composer.
  - One `stopBeforeStart` (`runControl.ts`) settles a run stopped before it starts, for both the conversation and the host:
    - an `agent.stopped` step, so the run journal reads cancelled, not completed;
    - a durable "Stopped before it started." answer row, so a reopened chat does not start the work.
  - `runSteer.stop` with nothing claimed leaves no mark. That mark used to swallow the next run's waiting words. `runSteer.test.ts` is new, plus a setup-stop case in `brainRunHost.steer.test.ts`.
- **Tests.** `userTurnRuns.test.ts` is new. Cases were appended to `useBrainConversation.test.tsx` and `useChatTurns.test.tsx`, and their existing cases run unchanged.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-27 — The chat panel keeps up with typing and streaming in a long chat (VSIX 2026.10.105)

- **Symptom.** In VS Code chat #6 (1,572 messages, a 500-event live trace), typing in the composer lagged, and a streaming reply appeared slowly.
- **Every keystroke re-rendered the transcript.** `useChatSend.takeAttachments` was keyed on `conv`, which is a new object every render. The new identity cascaded through `sendOrQueue` into `answerQuestion` / `replayMessage`, which are props of the memoized `<BrainTimeline>` and its rows. So every keystroke, and every frame, re-rendered about 150 rows, each re-parsing its metadata and `<think>` text. It is now keyed on `pendingAttachments` / `removeAttachment`.
- **Every 32 ms streaming frame rebuilt the transcript.** The webview built a new trace array per `run.sync` frame even when no event had arrived, so the settled timeline was re-mapped and re-sorted per token. Each frame also re-shipped `snapshot.appended` (up to 50 replies) through `postMessage`. Its fresh identity re-fired `useChatTranscript`'s splice, which re-rendered the whole chat surface a second time.
- **A trace at its 500-event bound was resent whole on every new event.** The delta only understood growth, not a head trim.
- **One delta rule for both lists** (`clients/vscode/src/listDelta.ts`). The host ships the head trim plus the new items (`traceDrop`/`traceFrom`, `appendedDrop`/`appendedFrom`). The webview applies them and keeps the SAME array when nothing changed. A replaced list, or a new panel, is resent whole as before.
  - The host finds the last-sent TAIL in the current list; the old head is gone after a trim.
  - A panel whose copy is out of step posts `run.resync` instead of building a short list. This happens when its store evicted the cell between runs. The host then resends that run whole.
- **The relay moved out of `brainRunHost.ts`** (406 lines) into `runRelay.ts`, which owns the sinks and their delta bookkeeping. `brainRunHost.ts` is now 396 lines. The webview driver reads the host's `RunSyncMessage` type instead of a hand-copied frame, and the frame's type now says `snapshot.appended` is a delta.
- **Tests.** `listDelta.test.ts` is new. Two relay cases were appended to `brainRunHost.test.ts` and two frame cases to `webview/src/hostRunDriver.test.ts`. Their existing cases run unchanged.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-27 — A run that says it is ready now acts (PRD 35 WS8p · VSIX 2026.10.104 · run-guards 2026.10.2 · brain-embedded 2026.10.65 · agent-run 2026.10.82 · api 2026.10.89)

- **Symptom.** VS Code chat #6 said "Now I have everything I need" and read one more file, turn after turn (run #562: 105 turns, `⚠ SPUN`). Nothing tripped:
  - VS Code bound no A3 progress detector.
  - A3's `no_progress` window counts any new file as progress, so it would not have tripped even where it was bound.
  - `cacheServedStreak` sees only cache-answered repeats, switches off after the first edit, and fires at most twice a run.
- **A fifth A3 signal, `unkept_ready`** (`packages/run-guards/src/readinessClaim.ts`). `claimsReady(text)` matches the model's own readiness claim. It ignores code, quotes, questions, "make sure" and conditional claims ("when / once / if I have…"), and only the words up to the claim can negate it. A claim turn with only read-only calls is unkept; any other call clears the count. The second unkept claim trips, and new files do not reset it. `ProgressDetector.noteTurnText` feeds it, its state is plain JSON, and `progressAdvice` is split out of `progressSteerNote`. The pause question no longer claims a stronger model.
- **VS Code binds A3** (`brain-embedded/src/runStore/progressGuard.ts`). It covers every run: parent and sub-agent, before and after edits. Turn text enters at `beforeToolCalls`, every call (cache-answered too) is observed at `afterDispatch`, and the turn folds at `afterToolCalls`. The ladder:
  - **steer:** a note opens the next turn;
  - **escalate:** a forced turn (`hand_off` while planning, the change tools once coding); a question run, or a turn with no change tool, is steered instead;
  - **pause:** `ask_user` alone with "Continue with guidance" / "Stop the run"; a run that cannot ask is steered.
  - A trip that a budget's forced turn pre-empts stays due until a later turn takes it. The lever is `a3_progress_detector`, read through the new `deviceLevers.ts`, which `runPreamble`'s B1 read now shares.
  - Traces: `loop.progress_check`, `loop.progress_forced`.
- **One forced-progress turn.** `forcedProgressTurn` in `progressBudget.ts` serves both `cacheServedStreak` (migrated, behaviour unchanged) and the A3 escalation.
- **The cloud and agent-run get the signal too.**
  - `costLoop/loopGuards.ts` reads the turn text in `afterTurn`.
  - agent-run's `afterToolCalls` now drives `GuardsHook.endTurn`. Nothing called it before, so A3 and D1 never folded a turn there.
  - agent-run's `vitest.config.ts` finds the sibling builderforce-memory `working` dist by walking up. Its fixed four-level path only worked from the ws2 worktree, so 7 test files could not load from the main checkout.
- **`runAgent.ts` split** from 649 to 264 lines, with no logic change. The new modules:
  - `runContext.ts`: input, view, policy context, emit;
  - `runState.ts`: fresh, resume and transcript state;
  - `turnContext.ts`: system prompt and the volatile block;
  - `runTurn.ts`: the model turn and dispatch;
  - `runSettle.ts`: the outcome.
- **Proven by:**
  - `readinessClaim.test.ts` (48 with progressDetector);
  - `progressGuard.test.ts` (10, end to end through `startRun`): the pre-WS8p guards stay quiet; steer → forced → ask; no trip on a 30-file review; a write or spawn keeps a claim; a sub-agent follows the same rule; the due survives a pre-empting budget; the lever turns it off;
  - a new `loopGuards.test.ts` case (cloud).
  - Existing suites pass unchanged: brain-embedded (14 files, 166 tests), agent-run (23 files), api costLoop (23).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-27 — The VSIX chat panel loads again: init never waits on a cold symbol index (VSIX 2026.10.103)

- **Symptom.** After installing VSIX 2026.10.102 the chat panel stayed on "Connecting…". The extension host activated cleanly, and the webview booted and posted `ready` (headless probe of the installed bundle, 101 vs 102: identical, no page errors). The BuilderForce output channel stayed empty because the webview never received `init`, so it never made an API call.
- **Root cause.** 2026.10.102 switched the definition index to the tree-sitter extractor (`workspaceSymbols.ts` `editorExtractor`). A snapshot written by another extractor is discarded (`node-symbols.ts` `loadSnapshot`), so the first open re-parsed the whole workspace. `buildWorkspaceInit` awaited `getStableGrounding` → `symbolIndexGrounding` → `filesUnder()` → `ensureFresh()` before posting `init`. On `c:\codegentic` that took ≈4½ minutes (activation 20:26:49; the tree-sitter `symbols.json` was written at 20:31:11). The same unbounded wait sat in front of every run start (`brainRunHostPorts` grounding port) and the chat participant (`getGroundingWithHistory`).
- **Fix.** `stableGroundingWithin(root, ms, onLate?)` in `clients/vscode/src/grounding.ts` races the memoised build against a deadline with the context pack's `withinMs`. Late, it serves the rescan map alone, the build carries on, and `onLate` fires only if the build landed. Init waits 1.5 s and the surface re-pushes `init` when the index arrives (`workspaceSurface.ts` `onGroundingLate`). Runs and the participant share `RUN_GROUNDING_BUDGET_MS` (3 s). New cases in `grounding.test.ts`; the existing memo cases are unchanged.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — Cost-lever parity: spend less for the same work, and attachments the model can read (VSIX 2026.10.102 · api · brain-embedded · agent-tools · agent-runtime · builderforce-memory 2026.10.27–28)

We audited a competitor's VS Code extension (TIP Code) against ours on 13 cost levers. None was fully present in our extension, and the audit found working features that were switched off or half-wired. All of it is now built; design and contracts are in "Cost-lever parity" (archived in this file, 2026-11-18).

- **Attachments reach the model.** In VS Code, attachments and "Add context" arrived as a `blob:vscode-webview://` link no model could read. The host now inlines text under a mention budget (`@builderforce/tool-output-policy` `mentionBudget`: cloud 48K per file and 96K per turn, local sized to the model's window). Binaries upload through `POST /api/brain/upload` with the extension's login. `#file` references in the chat participant use the same path (`clients/vscode/src/{contextIngress,attachmentIngress,chatReferences}.ts`).
- **Compression works in the editor.** C8 was off twice: `localCapabilities` built the Desktop capability without the compressor, and rollout levers were always off for a null on-device tenant. On-device hosts now bucket by install id (`cost-levers` `isOnDeviceCostLeverOn`). Attached prose (.md .txt .log .rst .adoc) over 2,000 chars is compressed and code never is. A new `read_compressed` tool reads prose files compressed.
- **Images keep their format.** `imagePrep` keeps GIFs, small PNG/WebP/JPEG and transparency, and uploads the prepared file instead of the original. Settings `builderforce.images.{maxEdge,jpegQuality}`.
- **A model per stage.** `run-policy` `nextTurn` now reads the plan and code phase models as well as verify. The VSIX resolves `builderforce.models.{plan,code,review,subagent}` (then `ROLE_MODELS`) and no longer pins the code model to the whole run.
- **Quick or full pipeline.** `@builderforce/pipeline-route` scores each request with a logistic model and routes it to the full plan → code → review pipeline or a single quick pass. Settings: `builderforce.pipeline.{routing,routeThreshold,quickModel}`; writing "full pipeline" forces it. The route and score are recorded per call in the local ledger and in `llm_usage_log` (migrations `1277` / transactional `0024`, expand only). The **Pipeline route report** command summarises 30 days of runs, cost, scores, misroutes and a suggested threshold. Cloud cost metrics gained `model` and `route` groupings.
- **Per-run spend cap in the editor.** `builderforce.maxRunBudgetUsd` stops a run at the cap and warns at 80%. The rule is one shared primitive (`spend-contract` `runBudget.ts`) used by the cloud cost loop and the run store. Run outcomes (succeeded, failed, stopped, budget-contained) are recorded locally for misroute measurement. Difficulty thresholds are tunable with `DIFFICULTY_SKIP_ABOVE` / `DIFFICULTY_EXPLORE`.
- **Cheaper reading.** `local_research` hands code reading to a local model, in the VSIX and on-prem. Its answer cache is keyed by file mtime and size. Pre-search (symbol index plus ripgrep) feeds the first turn. "Where is X defined" is answered from the symbol index with no model call, in the webview and in the chat participant.
- **A real repo map.** A tree-sitter extractor (`agent-tools/node-tree-sitter.ts`; TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, PHP) falls back to regex. Its wasm ships in the VSIX and agent-runtime builds. `repo_map` is served from the local index without Desktop.
- **Code maps work.** In builderforce-memory, the 3-file minimum applies to every run and the root area is recallable. A codemap write no longer retires other areas' maps. A merged map keeps the union of anchors, and a changed file drops just its line. Recall now works from identifiers and area words as well as paths. Cloud and on-prem get area-targeted recall through `buildProjectFactsBlock`, and Claude Agent SDK (V2) runs record and write maps.
- **The prompt prefix stays stable.**
  - One `lastStableIndex` rule places the history breakpoint, tool turns included, for both OpenRouter and direct Anthropic. Before, tool loops cached almost nothing.
  - The forced-turn brief goes in the `<run-state>` tail.
  - `packHandoff` results are memoised per run (`windowFit/packMemo.ts`).
  - History windowing drops in chunks.
  - `getStableGrounding` is computed once per rescan.
  - Workforce recall rides the user turn, not the system prompt. This also fixed the recall overwriting the persona when the request had no system message.
  - Tool pins never evict a fixed tool.
  - Kept as is: thinking still turns off after turn 1 on direct Anthropic. Only the turn-2 message cache misses, and first-turn planning quality is worth it.
- **Fixes.** Stop kills ripgrep. Search is smart-case. The watcher skips noisy folders and its own `.builderforce` files. **Rescan Codebase** refreshes the index without a model route. The two new tools are classified as reads and dedup-guarded.
- **Review fixes (fresh Opus review, 36 findings).**
  - **Attachment uploads.** Every binary attach hung: the upload payload's `type` field overwrote the bridge envelope's. The envelope now always wins and the field is renamed to `mime`. A test runs through the real envelope.
  - **Transcripts.** The text the model read is persisted (`attachmentTranscript.ts`). Retries, reloads and the next run's seed send it, never a `blob:` link.
  - **Privacy and size.** Images that go inline never upload. Local-only refuses any cloud upload. Sizes are refused before encoding, at the server's limit.
  - **On-prem `local_research`.** It requires a loopback `baseUrl`, and keyless loopback servers work.
  - **Code maps from every writer.** Anchors are derived server-side for all writers, so cloud, on-prem and V2 maps go stale per file. The VSIX's own anchor port is deleted.
  - **Cache.**
    - Workforce recall is memoised behind the facts version token.
    - A fallback text breakpoint rides behind the tool-result breakpoint. A live OpenRouter probe read 9,634 of 10,664 prompt tokens from cache on turn 2.
    - The pack memo is keyed per chat.
  - **Spend.** The per-run cap covers the whole sub-agent tree, and one cost rule prices device ledger rows.
  - **Pre-search.** It aborts `rg` at its deadline and on Stop, and shares one identifier extractor and one `withinMs`.
  - Kept by decision: thinking stays first-turn-only on direct Anthropic, and the one-per-run coder re-ask brief stays an untagged directive before the tail.
- **builderforce-memory 2026.10.27–28** documents the `volatileTail` cache rule (per-turn content tagged, last, never persisted, never in the system prompt) and code maps in both READMEs, the npm description and keywords.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — A run that circles is made to act, and a follow-up never drops the original ask (brain-embedded · run-policy · agent-stall)

VS Code chat #5739's journal, split into its 11 runs, showed what the chat-wide diagnostics could not. The one-line ask ("remove the title from the top of the VSIX") was located in run 0 and never edited. Run 5 made 52 plan turns with 40 exact repeats, 20 covered re-reads, 60 cache replays, 4 folds and no write. Run 8 needed 33 plan turns before coding.

- **Fold notes are notes, not reasoning.** MiniMax and Kimi ignore the summary call's `reasoning: off` and think inline. Every run-5 fold was "<think>We need produce memory compression…", so the note's budget was spent deliberating. `streamSummaryCompletion` now keeps the answer and drops the markup. A reply that is nothing but reasoning, or a block cut off by the output ceiling, keeps the reasoning's text untagged. It usually holds the facts, and an empty note would re-run the whole summarizer call on every turn, because a failed fold is never memoized.
- **"Complete the implementation" is a work order.** `asksForChange` read it as a question, so those runs bought no analysis budget at all. That is why run 5 ran 52 plan turns with no `loop.hand_off_due`. `complete` / `finish` / `finalize` now count only as an imperative with its object (`FINISH_ORDER`, `CHAINED_FINISH`). The adjective ("a complete list", "complete with paths") stays a question.
- **A no-progress breaker the cache cannot reset.** The read guards answer repeats as successes, which cleared the kernel's failure streak every time. `runStore/cacheServedStreak.ts` counts repeats the read cache answered (stub, covered window, replay, repeated write). A narrower search served from a wider one is reuse and does not count. Any call the host runs clears the count. Six in a row, over at least two model turns, force the next turn of a change request: `hand_off` alone while planning, the change tools alone once coding. This happens at most twice a run, never once the run has changed code or handed it off, and never while verifying. Trace: `loop.no_progress`. `progressBudget.ts` owns the shared pieces: `isChangeRequest`, `budgeted`, `progressed`, `changeToolsOf`, and the `handOffBrief` / `changeBrief` builders (which name `ask_user` only when it is offered).
- **A quick pass has a quick budget.** `changeDue` takes a budget, and a run routed `quick` (`pipelineRoute.ts`) is forced to change after `QUICK_CHANGE_TURN_BUDGET = 8` coding turns, not 20.
- **A change request carries the chat's change asks.** `runStore/chatAsks.ts` reads the person's distinct change asks; questions are never carried. Turns are marked at the persisted seed, at the triggering turn, and at the person's own steer (`RunSteerMessage.fromPerson`, set by `runSteer.ts`). The loop's nudges, a child's report and an owner's direction are never marked. Only a change request (`readRequest` in the new `runStore/requestReading.ts`, which also holds the continuation directive) gets a "CHANGE ASKS IN THIS CHAT" directive. Its hand-off goal (`run.goal`) lists the earlier asks as CONTEXT ONLY, since some may be done or superseded and the latest message is authoritative.
- **The diagnostics score the run, not the chat.** `runSlices.ts` cuts the trace where the model's `step` count resets, which needs no clock. A message steered into a running run stays inside it: chat #5739's "runs" 2 and 3 were steers at steps 11 and 15. The progress picture is the latest run's. A `Runs:` line names every run, and the headline still reports an earlier run that `⚠ SPUN` (`spunEarlier`). Calls the read cache answered are counted separately and never as a mutation; a steer's skipped remainder is not one of them. A re-read after the run's own edit of that file is new ground, with `./src/a.ts`, `src\a.ts` and `src/a.ts` as one target. The revisit list and the revisit ratio are now the same measurement. The report wording moved out of `runProgress.ts` into `runProgressReport.ts`.
- **No file grew past its limit.** The turn's menu (selection, forced turn, router, trace) moved out of `completeTurn.ts` into `runStore/turnMenu.ts` (451 → 372 lines). The request reading moved out of `runPreamble.ts` (415 → 383 lines).
- Guarded in `requestIntent.test.ts`, `policy.test.ts`, `transcriptSummarizer.test.ts`, `cacheServedStreak.test.ts`, `chatAsks.test.ts` and `runSlices.test.ts`. `useBrainConversation.test.tsx` now compares the person's own words, without this turn's context block.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — One rule for every run, whatever the chat's history (VSIX 2026.10.100 · brain-embedded 2026.10.63 · run-policy 2026.10.21)

An old chat did not behave like a fresh one. Once a chat had made one edit, the run cell's `codePhaseReached` started every later run in that chat in `code`. That skipped the analysis budget, so the hand-off was never forced, and coding had no bound at all, so the run could read for its whole life (chat #5739). A fresh chat got the full chain. That chat-history state is gone.

- **Every run starts the same way.** `runPreamble` starts every run in `plan`. The one exception is a role, not history: a sub-agent starts in `code`. `codePhaseReached` is deleted from the run cell, `beforeDispatch`, `completeTurn`, the budget module and `modelPreflight`. The run-store test that asserted the old carry-over now asserts the reverse.
- **Coding is bounded like analysis.** Policy `codeTurns` + `changeDue` + the `change_forced` event apply to every coding run. One that has spent `PLAN_TURN_BUDGET` coding turns without changing code or handing it off gets one turn offering only the change tools (plus `ask_user`), with a call required: make the change, or say what blocks it. Trace: `loop.change_due`. `runStore/planBudget.ts` became `progressBudget.ts`, holding both budgets (`planBudgetTurn`, `changeBudgetTurn`).
- **Proven end to end.** `handOffExecution.e2e.test.ts` covers both: a chat that has already coded runs its next change request through the same chain as a fresh chat, and a coding sub-agent that only reads is made to edit at the budget.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — The VSIX ships the run loop that was tested (VSIX 2026.10.99)

VS Code chat #5739 ran 105 turns on MiniMax Flash on VSIX 2026.10.98 and never implemented the change. None of the turns carried a role, and the diagnostics had no "Routing by role". The cause was not the run loop: the extension never ran it. The extension bundles `@seanhogg/builderforce-brain-embedded` (and `brain-ui`) through their `main` → `dist/`. That dist was built by `prepare` on install (2026-10-25 13:52) and by nothing after, so VSIX 2026.10.97 and 2026.10.98 shipped a run loop from before the analysis budget, the `code` role, the hand-off brief and the routing record. Every test of those changes imports source, so all of them were green.

- **`scripts/ensure-linked-builds.mjs`** rebuilds every linked package whose `dist/` entry is older than its inputs. The inputs are its `src/`, manifest and tsup config, and, recursively, every package it links, since tsup bundles linked source in. Links are built before their dependents. A failed rebuild fails the script, so a stale dist is never bundled. It is wired into `clients/vscode` `vscode:prepublish`, `compile` and `build:webview` (for the frontend's links).
- **`scripts/linkedPackages.mjs`** holds the link-graph helpers (`readManifest`, `linkedTargets`), now shared by `ensure-linked-deps.mjs` and the new script.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — Delegation works like a team lead's: full briefs, reports the owner acts on, checks on the cheaper tier (VSIX 2026.10.98 · api 2026.10.87 · brain-embedded 2026.10.62 · agent-tools 2026.10.15 · agent-loop 2026.10.13 · model-router 2026.10.19)

Compared with how Claude Code delegates (a brief that carries the whole task, a report it expects back and acts on, and compile/test on a cheaper model), Builderforce's hand-off fell short in three places. Children got the slice but not the goal or its limits. They ended with free prose, and nothing obliged the owner to act on what they left. And the coder ran build and test itself, on the strongest and most expensive model.

- **The brief carries the whole task.** Each child brief (`childTaskBrief`, now taking a `BriefContext`) opens with the goal in the user's words (`HandOffPorts.request` ← `run.userRequest`). It also carries a new per-task `constraints` field from `hand_off` ("Do not: …"), along with the slice, how it is accepted, the research summary and the record of what was already read. The ticket body carries the constraints too.
- **Every child ends with a report its owner acts on.** `subagentSystemPrompt` (agent-loop) now asks every child, on both the editor and the cloud, for fixed closing lines: `Outcome`, `Changed`, `Verified`, `Open issues`. A `verify` child gets its own shape (`Outcome: pass | fail`, `Checked`, failures verbatim) and is told to check, not fix. `parseSubagentReport` reads the open issues where each host builds the report (`childRunSpawner.reportOf`, `cloudChildRuns.reportOf`). `childReportText` hands them to the owner as "yours to resolve before you finish"; a failed slice with nothing named becomes the whole slice. The same `openIssues` field rides `wait_agents`.
- **Checks run on the cheaper tier; fixes stay with the coder.** `VERIFY_DELEGATION_STEP` / `VERIFY_STEP` (agent-tools) is the ONE wording for "hand the type-check, build and tests to one `verify` sub-agent, fix what it reports, verify again". The verify role is cost-first at the gateway. The wording is used by the hand-off's inline, parallel and background next steps, by `LIVE_FANOUT_NEXT`, and by the self-review ship directive and nudge. A run that cannot spawn runs the narrowest checks itself.
- **A cheap-role child no longer copies its owner's model.** `MODEL_ROLE_OBJECTIVE` moved from model-router into agent-tools, beside the role vocabulary, so the gateway's ordering and the host read one table; model-router imports it. The new `roleLeansCheap` drives `modelForChildRun`: a `verify` / `explore` / `utility` child with no role pin is left to the gateway, instead of inheriting the parent's soft model and checking on the coder's tier. A strict user pin still wins.
- **The report parser reads realistic output.** One issue per bullet: a verify child's verbatim failure output (code fences, stack lines, indented continuations) folds into its issue, and a blank line ends the list, so closing prose is not read as work. The "this means none" match is narrow, so "None — all pass" and "No open issues." read as clean while "None of the tests ran" stays an issue. A bullet that starts with `Changed:` stays an issue; prose after `Outcome:` is ignored; `Open issues (2):` is understood. Capped at 8 issues of 600 chars. The resolve wording is one constant (`RESOLVE_OPEN_ISSUES`).
- **The hand-off is proven end to end.** `brain-embedded/src/handOffExecution.e2e.test.ts` drives the real run store with a model that reads forever (chats #6, #5739). It checks that the budget forces `hand_off`, the children get the goal and the research, every later turn asks for `code`, the coder's `edit_file` reaches the host, and "Routing by role" tells the story. It also covers a planner that ignores the forced turn, a sub-agent that starts in `code`, and a question that is never forced. `api/src/application/llm/proxySeed.codingRole.test.ts` drives the real seed and candidate chain for MiniMax + xAI + Moonshot connected. A `code` turn leads with Grok or Kimi, never MiniMax Flash: on free-first funding, and even when the tenant ranked MiniMax first. A `plan` turn keeps the tenant's order.
- **The blog says what is now true.** "One chat, a whole team working" (all five locales) said sub-agents have no shell and the lead runs every proof step. It now describes the closing report, the open issues the lead owns, and checking on a cheaper verify sub-agent.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-26 — Analysis ends, sub-agents code, and routing is no longer blind (VSIX 2026.10.97 · api 2026.10.86 · brain-embedded 2026.10.61 · run-policy 2026.10.20 · agent-stall 2026.10.2)

Even on 2026.10.94, VS Code chat #6 kept analysing and never coded. Its run journal held 778 `plan` turns and 265 `code` turns, all on MiniMax Flash. There were 198 analysis→code re-asks and zero `hand_off` calls.

- **Analysis has a budget.** `PLAN_TURN_BUDGET = 20` and `handOffDue` are in `@builderforce/run-policy`, and `planTurns` is counted per turn while the run is planning. When a change request spends the budget, `runStore/planBudget.ts` makes the next turn the hand-off: `hand_off` is the only tool offered, a tool call is required, and a brief asks for the summary and standalone tasks. If that turn still does not hand off, `plan_budget_spent` ends planning and the coding role takes over. Traces: `loop.hand_off_due`, `loop.plan_budget_spent`.
- **The research is handed to the coders.** The intended flow is: the analysis is captured, handed to sub-agents, and implemented by the strongest coders. Until now each implementation child got only a few sentences of conclusion. The `hand_off` summary is now specified as the research for the coders: everything the planner and its research sub-agents established (files, functions, what they do today, decisions, traps). Each child brief carries it, plus the planning run's own record of what it read and searched (`RunKnowledgeLog.brief`, `HandOffPorts.knowledge`). The inline coder gets the same.
- **Sub-agents start in `code`.** A child is a slice its owner already planned (`runPreamble.ts`: `req.lineage`). Before, each coding child was offered `hand_off` and went through the analysis phase again. Routing is unchanged: the host still asks for each child's own role (`brainRunHost.ts`).
- **"Review X and implement Y" is a change request again.** `asksForChange` read every request that opened with review, investigate, find and similar verbs as a question. That exempted real work orders from every "asked for a change, made none" check, the new budget included. A research-led request now counts as a change when a change verb is chained on ("… and fix it", "…, then implement …", "Review the PRD. Implement WS1."). Asking for a report ("… and write a summary") or for the reader ("… and show me the gaps") does not count.
- **Routing is recorded.** The gateway's terminal `_builderforce` frame was discarded by the client and now feeds `StreamChatResult.gateway`; the frame also carries the head of the candidate chain (`proxyFinalize.ts`). Each `llm.complete` records `failovers` (`model:status kind`), `candidates` and `traceId`. The turn log shows `[role]` and "gateway left: …". A new "Routing by role" diagnostics section (`routingByRole.ts`) shows which model served each role, counts re-asks, hand-offs and budget events, and flags code turns answered by the planning model. The gateway logs `gateway.byo_seed` (connected, demoted, ranked, learned, callerLeads) whenever demotion, learned evidence or role order moves the connected-account seed.
- Guarded in `policy.test.ts`, `requestIntent.test.ts`, `routingByRole.test.ts`, `planHandoff.test.ts` and `streamChatCompletion.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Hybrid runs get past analysis and make the change (VSIX 2026.10.94 · brain-embedded 2026.10.60 · run-policy 2026.10.19)

Under Hybrid (auto-routed), even a one-line change was analysed for hundreds of turns and never edited. In chat #172, MiniMax took 877 turns and read the PRD 65 times without making the change. Auto-routed runs start in run-policy's `plan` phase. While planning, the `hand_off` tool is always on the menu, and its description said "You are the planning model … do NOT edit files yourself". The design is the opposite: the planner's first edit re-asks the coding model automatically (`code_change_attempted` → `reask_as_coder`). The model obeyed the description and never edited.

- `HAND_OFF_TOOL_SPEC` (`brain-embedded/src/planHandoff.ts`) is now OPTIONAL and only for multi-task plans. A small change is simply made, and the first edit moves the run into coding.
- Second bug: `reduceRunPolicy` ignored `code_change_attempted` whenever a model was set (a pin, a lock or a stall failover), so the phase stayed `plan` for the whole run and the prohibition stayed on the menu. The phase now moves to `code` on any edit. The re-ask still happens only when no model is set.
- `completeTurn.ts` sets `codePhaseReached` whenever the event fires, so the chat's next run starts in coding.
- `beforeDispatch.ts` explains a `hand_off` sent in the same batch as an edit, instead of claiming a hand-off that never ran.
- Guarded in `policy.test.ts`. The pin and lock cases now expect the phase to be `code` and `hand_off` to be off the menu.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Agent commands no longer leave undeletable `nul` files (VSIX 2026.10.92 · hardened in 2026.10.93)

Kimi sometimes wrote Windows-style commands with `2>nul`. When `run_command` sent one to Git Bash, bash created a real file named `nul` (at the repo root and in `packages/brain-ui/`). Windows treats `nul` as a reserved name, so `git clean` failed with "Permission denied" and the files stayed untracked in `git status`. `spawnCommand` (`clients/vscode/src/processTree.ts`) now passes every bash command through `toBashNullDevice` (`posixShell.ts`), which turns a redirect to exactly `nul` into `/dev/null`. Commands run by `cmd.exe` are unchanged. Guarded in `posixShell.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — A refused Kimi token is rotated and retried silently (VSIX 2026.10.91 · api 2026.10.85 · Rovr 2026.10.31)

After many good turns, a Kimi call still failed "The API Key appears to be invalid or may have expired" (chat #5091, turn 69). The next turn worked. The per-request retry asked our gateway for a replacement, and the gateway handed back the same token, because by its clock the token was still live; Kimi had revoked it early. The likely cause is a second sign-in on the same Kimi account, such as the Kimi Code extension, which uses the same public client id. Unconfirmed.

- The client now tells the gateway which token Kimi refused (`POST …/local-credential { rejected }`, through `fetchLocalCredential` / `LocalCredentialStore.resolve({ rejected })`).
- `resolveKimiOAuthResolution` rotates the grant when the refused token is the one it holds. Any other value means a rotation already happened, so it returns the current token.
- The retry stays silent in the chat. The VSIX logs each refusal to the output channel (`[kimi auth] Kimi refused the token; rotated it and retried.`), so a recurring revocation is visible there.
- A transient refresh failure still answers with the held token, never with "reconnect", so a blip does not prompt for a sign-in.
- Guarded in `connectedAccounts.test.ts` and `tenantProviderKeyService.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Hybrid uses your Kimi subscription (VSIX 2026.10.90 · Rovr 2026.10.30 · brain-embedded 2026.10.58)

Hybrid used the tenant's connected accounts (MiniMax, Grok, Anthropic) through the gateway, but never Kimi. Kimi refuses our cloud, local-first only takes on-device runtimes, and the gateway skips a vendor that needs local egress. Operator decision: a connected Kimi always goes ahead of the cloud step in Hybrid.

- `localFirstPlan` (`@builderforce/local-inference`) takes `accounts` (`LocalFirstAccount`) and orders them: device attempts, then the accounts, then the cloud. The on-device filter stays, so **Local only never uses Kimi**.
- `createHostModelStream` takes an `accounts` port, read only on a Hybrid Auto call. The `run.local-success` predictor gates only the DEVICE attempt, never an account (`hybridLocalSuccess.ts`).
- The shared `createConnectedAccounts.hybridAccounts()` lists a connected account on its lead model, with the per-request token. It never prompts, and it asks the gateway at most once per session when nothing is connected. The VSIX attaches it to every Hybrid route (`modelRouting.ts`); Rovr passes it once Kimi's origin is granted. The web app passes none, because the browser cannot reach Kimi.
- A Kimi refusal (401, rate limit, outage) falls to the gateway as any failed local-first attempt does.
- Guarded in `plan.test.ts`, `hostModelStream.test.ts` and `connectedAccounts.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — A picked model survives a reload (VSIX 2026.10.89)

After reloading VS Code, Specific model still showed Kimi K3 in the `/` menu, but every turn failed `no_specific_model` (diagnostics: `Model: auto`). The mode is a setting (`builderforce.inferenceMode`) and survived; the pick (`modelState.selected`) lived only in memory and did not. The pick is now saved in the extension's global state (`builderforce.modelPick`) and restored at activation (`bindModelPickStore`), so the mode and the pick always come back together. Guarded in `modelState.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Opening the BuilderForce tab no longer opens the Visualization (VSIX 2026.10.88)

`chatView.ts` opened the Visualization panel whenever the chat view loaded or you signed in (`openVisualizationOnce`). Both triggers are gone. The panel now opens only from the header's Visualize button or the `builderforce.openVisualization` command, which is what the agent runs. Guarded in `authPanelSync.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — A Kimi turn no longer dies after its first step (VSIX 2026.10.87 · api 2026.10.84 · brain-embedded 2026.10.57 · Rovr 2026.10.29)

The first Kimi call in a turn worked; the next failed "The API Key appears to be invalid or may have expired". Two causes:

- **Server handed out a token about to die.** `resolveKimiOAuthResolution` returned the held access token until its REAL expiry (Kimi's stored `expires` has no margin), so a client got a token with seconds left. It now rotates inside `OAUTH_SAFETY_MARGIN_MS` (5 min), so every issued token outlives the client's 2-minute refresh margin. Guarded in `tenantProviderKeyService.test.ts`.
- **Client captured one token for the whole run.** The route (and its bearer) is resolved once per run. `LocalEndpoint.credential` (`@builderforce/local-inference`) is now asked for the current token before EVERY request by the one helper `fetchLocal`, which also retries a 401 once with a replacement. The shared `localTransport` / `completeLocal` and the VSIX panel proxy all go through it. The token source comes from the shared `createConnectedAccounts.credentialFor` (VSIX and Rovr) or the Kimi Code CLI login. Guarded in `fetchLocal.test.ts` and `connectedAccounts.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Kimi uses its US hosts, spelled once; a failed Kimi sign-in is logged and never silent (VSIX 2026.10.84 · api 2026.10.83 · Rovr 2026.10.27)

**Reported:** on VSIX 2026.10.83 the Kimi turn went back to the server (`local_egress_required`) with nothing logged.

- **Cause.** The Kimi Code CLI login on this machine had died. Kimi answered its refresh with `invalid_grant`. The install's config names `oauth_host = https://auth.kimi.ai`, but the VSIX refreshed against the hard-coded `https://auth.kimi.com`. Kimi's regions refuse each other's grants. The Kimi Code VS Code extension also refreshes the same `~/.kimi-code` credential. When authorization failed, `resolveChoiceRoute` returned the bare pick (`if (!authorized.ok) return choice;`), which sent the turn to the server without any log.
- **One owner for Kimi's hosts.** `KIMI_DOMAIN = 'kimi.ai'` in `@builderforce/kimi-oauth` is the only spelling. `KIMI_OAUTH_DEFAULT_HOST`, `KIMI_CODE_API_HOST` and `KIMI_CODE_API_BASE_URL` derive from it.
  - The server's vendor spec, local-credential route and provider-key copy import it.
  - Rovr's host permission and `kimiOriginDenied` copy (`$1`, all five locales) import it.
  - The server copy of `KIMI_CODE_API_BASE_URL` is gone.
- **Refresh at the issuing host.** `parseKimiCodeConfig` reads `oauth_host`, and the authorizer refreshes there. An explicit `KIMI_CODE_OAUTH_HOST` still wins.
- **Logged, never silent.**
  - `authorizeLocalEndpoint` writes each step to the BuilderForce output channel (`[kimi auth]`): CLI login used or why not, and workspace connection used or why not.
  - A failure is filed through `reportExtensionError` (`kimi.authorize`).
  - `resolveChoiceRoute` logs every route decision (`[route]`).
  - Under Specific, a pick for a provider only this machine can reach (registry `gatewayVendor`) that cannot be authorized now fails the turn with the reason and the remedy. Hybrid still answers with Auto, but logged.
- **The workspace Kimi sign-in was never wired; now ONE shared implementation (VSIX 2026.10.86 · Rovr 2026.10.28).** The editor's credential store was an activation step (`initLocalProviderCredentials`) that nothing called. So every turn without a CLI login failed "Kimi credentials are not initialized" and never offered Connect Kimi, while Rovr ran its own copy (`connectedAccount.ts`). Both now run `createConnectedAccounts` (`@builderforce/provider-connect/accounts`).
  - It creates each provider's store on first use, hydrated before its first resolve, so there is no init step to forget.
  - It resolves a pick (`clientPinOf`) or a runtime to its endpoint through the runtime registry's new `accountProvider`.
  - The hosts keep only their own UX: the editor's Connect notification, and Rovr's origin permission and Connect card.
  - Tests: `clients/vscode/src/connectedAccounts.test.ts`, plus a guard in `modelRouting.test.ts`.
  - Kimi's `auth.kimi.ai` device authorization was verified live.
  - **Regression in 2026.10.85, fixed in .86: picking a Kimi model would not stick.** The store's change listener refreshed the panels. A refresh resolved the route, the authorizer re-asked the store, and an unchanged "not connected" was persisted and notified again, which looped the panel and reset its model pick. The fix has two parts.
    - The shared store neither writes nor notifies when the credential is unchanged.
    - The authorizer offers the sign-in and files a failure only for a turn (`interactive: request.turn`). A panel refresh resolves quietly.
- **Known consequence.** A workspace Kimi connection granted on `auth.kimi.com` before this change will ask to be reconnected once, which re-grants it on `kimi.ai`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — A connected Kimi pick runs from this machine, with sign-in (VSIX 2026.10.83 · brain-embedded 2026.10.56 · api 2026.10.82)

**Reported:** chat #5091 pinned `direct/kimi-code/k3` in the VSIX and every turn failed `Strict-pin: model 'direct/kimi-code/k3' is unavailable (local_egress_required)`. The Kimi login was never offered. After the routing half shipped (VSIX 2026.10.82), the turn reached Kimi and failed `Invalid request Error`: 2026.10.82 was verified only by unit tests, never against the live API.

- **Kimi rejected our body (verified against the live Kimi Code API with the CLI login).** The shared streamer sent gateway-only fields to every local runtime, on the assumption runtimes ignore them. Kimi 400s `metadata` with numeric values ("Invalid request Error", on every model). K3 also 400s any `temperature` other than 1, and the streamer always sent 0.3. `strict`, `role`, `arcStage`, `routingMode`, `reasoning`, tools and `prompt_cache_key` were accepted.
  - `BrainTransport.wire: 'openai'`, set by `localTransport`, drops the gateway-only fields. This is the same set the gateway strips (`STANDARD_BODY_FIELDS`).
  - `BrainTransport.providerSampling` drops `temperature`. It is set from the registry's `providerSampling` (Kimi Code), so Kimi applies each model's own default.
  - The gateway's Kimi adapter (connected-runtime path) also sent 0.3. It now honours `providerSampling` (spec → `createOpenAICompatibleVendor` → `buildOpenAIChatBody`, which drops `temperature`/`top_p`).
- **Under Hybrid the pick still went to the gateway.** `createLocalStream` treated a call naming the pin in the gateway spelling (`direct/kimi-code/k3` against the pin `local/kimi-code/k3`) as a different model and sent it to the cloud. That is how turn 1 was answered by MiniMax. It now resolves the call through `clientPinOf` and stays on the pin.
- **Live end-to-end check:** `kimi-e2e.ts` (scratchpad) drives the built `createLocalStream` with the VSIX's own `ensureFreshKimiToken`, replaying chat #5091's call for `k3` and `kimi-for-coding`.

- **Cause.** The picker lists a connected Kimi account's models in the gateway spelling (`direct/kimi-code/…`). `modelRouting.resolveChoiceRoute` and Rovr's `connectedAccount.pinFor` recognised only `local/kimi-code/…` (`parseLocalModelRef`). The pick went to the Worker, which cannot reach Kimi's edge. Once the previous fix made picks strict, the Worker had nothing to fail over to and answered `local_egress_required`.
- **Fix.** The runtime registry now carries `gatewayVendor` (`kimi-code` → `kimi-code`). `clientPinOf` in `@builderforce/local-inference` resolves both `local/<runtime>/<model>` and `direct/<gatewayVendor>/<model>` to the client runtime. The VSIX route and Rovr's account pin both use it, so either spelling reaches the authorizer: the Kimi Code CLI login first, then the workspace connection, with the device-code connect offered on the spot.
- Tests: `packages/local-inference/src/ref.test.ts` (`clientPinOf`) and a source guard in `clients/vscode/src/modelRouting.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — The model you pick is the model that runs (brain-embedded 2026.10.55 · brain-ui 2026.10.26 · VSIX 2026.10.81)

**Reported:** picking a BYO model (`direct/kimi-code/k3`) left the mode control on Hybrid, and the turn was answered by `direct/minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`.

- **Cause.** Under Hybrid, `createHostModelStream` only tries a pick: it sends `modelStrict: false` (`pickThenAuto`), so the gateway could fail the pick over to another model. Local only sets aside any pick that leaves the device. Picking a model never changed the mode.
- **The rule, in one place.** `inferenceModeForModelPick` (`brain-embedded/src/inferenceModeForModelPick.ts`) is pure and has vitest tests.
  - A model or the BYO pool selects Specific.
  - Auto while on Specific returns to Hybrid.
  - An on-device pick under Local only keeps Local only. On-device is `runsOnDevice`, moved into `@builderforce/local-inference` beside `localRuntime` and shared with `createHostModelStream`, so a Kimi Code pick counts as off-device.
  - An undecided Local only is never lifted by a pick, so the first-run opt-in still asks.
  - An undecided Hybrid does move to Specific, which also answers the first-run question.
- **Applied once per pick, where the pick is made.**
  - Menu picks on every host go through brain-ui `ModelPane`, which applies the mode before the model. The hosts' menu setters (VS Code `model.set`, Rovr `choose`, the web's selection state) set only the model, so there is never a second, possibly stale, mode write.
  - Picks outside the menu: in VS Code, `clients/vscode/src/modelPick.ts` `applyModelPick` covers the QuickPick, the signed-out on-device list and Kimi connect. In Rovr, `usePinnedModel`'s `pick` covers Settings → Model and Kimi connect.
  - A pin a host clears on its own never moves the mode. This covers the VS Code entitlement clear (Specific then reports `no_specific_model`) and Rovr's removed-model clear.
- **Rovr no longer offers "your connected accounts".** It pins one model string, so a pool pick ran as Auto. The new `ChatModelOptions.byoPool: false`, set through `composerModel({ byoPool: false })`, drops that row.
- **Stale init.** `WorkspaceSurface.sendInit` posts only the newest build. A superseded call waits on the newest, so `ready` still posts the init before the intent.
- A rejected mode write is caught in `ModelPane`, `applyModelPick` and Rovr's `pick`, leaving the mode as it was.
- **Known, by design:**
  - A pin saved earlier under Hybrid stays a soft pin until it is picked again, and the mode control honestly shows Hybrid.
  - If someone picks a cloud model while Local only is still undecided and then answers Hybrid at the first-run question, they get Hybrid's try-then-fall-back. Hybrid is their explicit answer there.
  - On the web, an anonymous visitor who chose Local only and then picks a cloud model moves to Specific, and the guest allowance is minted. That explicit cloud pick is the opt-in.
