## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Long chats stay responsive, show context use and compaction; the context logic moves into builderforce-memory (builderforce-memory 2026.10.25 + 2026.10.26 · VSIX 2026.10.79)

**Reported:** the VS Code panel froze ("window unresponsive") on long chats, and nothing showed how full the context was or when a run compacted it.

- **Freeze.** `BrainTimeline` rendered every node: one chat had 529 messages and 4,535 run steps, all redrawn on every streamed token. It now renders a key-anchored window (`packages/brain-ui/src/timeline/useRenderWindow.ts`, 150 nodes) with Show earlier / Show newer / Jump to latest. The window stays bounded: expanding pins both ends, a reveal applies once per nonce, and switching chats opens the newest page. Rows are memoized, message and trace nodes are derived once per object (WeakMap caches in `timelineNodes.ts`), and `hasSubagents` reads messages instead of nodes.
- **Context meter.** `ContextMeter` in every composer (VS Code, web, Rovr, canvas, guest) shows the last turn's `usage.prompt` against the serving model's window, which the run now stamps on `llm.complete` (`contextUsageOf`). It is localized in all catalogs and themed by tokens.
- **Compaction is visible.** A fold renders as one expandable row with its note: from the durable auto marker, else from the run's `context.compacted` step when no marker was saved.
- **Defect 1, the fold was not durable.** Every new run re-summarized the whole history. A fold is now persisted as an auto consolidation marker carrying `keepFromId`, the first persisted message it did not cover. The run records which persisted message each transcript entry is (`runStore/runFoldMarker.ts`). It matches history persisted between runs and clamps `keepFromId` to any message the cell never saw (an @agent reply, another surface's turn). An unplaceable marker is ignored, never read as covering everything.
- **Defect 2, Consolidate and Fork were dead in VS Code.** The local-first `summarizeChat` now summarizes through the gateway (`clients/vscode/src/chatSummarizer.ts`). Over-long input is summarized in 48k-token chunks.
- **Markers are not replies.** `isModelReply` (`brain-embedded/src/modelReply.ts`) is used by retry, newest-reply actions, triage claim detectors and child reports. The api's `learnFromPersistedTurns` skips markers.
- **Architecture (operator: "split by layer").** The pure logic now lives in `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory/working`: `buildWorkingTranscript`, `summarizeTranscript`, consolidation markers, `scopeToConsolidation` and `foldKeepFromId`, each with jest tests. The old vitest tests were ported with unchanged assertions. `brain-embedded` keeps the bindings: `transcriptSummarizer.ts` (the stream adapter), the run store and the hooks (`useChatTranscript` was split out of `useBrainConversation`). `windowFit/` stays in brain-embedded as a binding: its pure core is `/handoff`'s `packHandoff`, and the rest depends on run-policy, cost-levers, local-inference and the model catalog. Recorded in PRD 35 §3.1.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — VS Code Visualization panel draws the board and shows real before/after diffs (VSIX 2026.10.78)

**Why.** Every open of the Visualization panel showed "The board could not be drawn." twice and nothing else.
- **Root cause (webview).** `VisualizationScreen` mounted `CreationCanvas` outside every provider it reads: intl, the Brain runtime, toasts, confirms, the canvas host install and the theme. The first `useTranslations` threw.
- **Root cause (host).** The panel posted a narrow frame of its own and answered only `ready`, so the canvas's persistence, capture, run and error calls were never answered.

**What shipped:**
- **The panel is a third host of the ONE `WorkspaceSurface`**, beside the editor tab and the sidebar chat. Its frame is `buildWorkspaceInit`'s, run through the pure `asVisualizationFrame`: `view` is the literal "visualization", and `surface`, `boardBeside` and an undefined `pendingChanges` are dropped. It inherits the run mirror, the live working tree, theme re-push and sign-in refresh. `buildVisualizationInitFrame` is deleted.
- **`webview/src/canvas/CanvasScreenProviders.tsx` is the one provider stack** for every board screen. `WorkspaceScreen` and `VisualizationScreen` both mount it. The wiring test moved with it.
- **The error boundary now wraps only the canvas**, so a board that fails to draw leaves the Changes toggle and tree working, and the notice prints once.
- **The change tree renders hunks.** Before this, every file read "No diff to show".
  - `detectPendingDiff` (`gitChanges.ts`) is served as `changes.diff`, and `usePendingDiff` re-asks on every `pendingChanges` push.
  - The pure `pendingDiffModel.ts` (tested) picks the commands: `diff HEAD`, or `--cached` plus worktree when a repository has no commit yet. It pins the `a/` and `b/` prefixes against `diff.mnemonicPrefix`, and bounds the result by file, so one huge first file no longer blanks every row.
  - Reads are untrimmed (`runGitRaw`), so the last context row survives. Concurrent asks share one read, and a generation counter stops a read that crossed an invalidation from being cached.
- **The panel offers no page engines** (`offersPageEngines: false`). The host prefers the newest webview, so the panel would otherwise have loaded the chat's WebGPU models and ended a turn when it closed.
- **`WorkspaceSurface` stays host-agnostic:** the host supplies its `frame` transform.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Connected accounts in every chat: see each provider account's health, Test it and Reconnect it from the composer's `/` menu (web, canvas, VS Code, Rovr)

**Why.** A Grok 403 left no way to check or reconnect the account from the chat surface. Status lived only in Settings ▸ API Keys and the VS Code command palette's QuickPick, and that QuickPick ignored the dispatch-observed alert.

**What shipped:**
- **`@builderforce/provider-connect` `connections.ts`.** `listProviderConnections` (`GET /llm/provider-keys`; 403 → `null`), `testProviderConnection`, `completePasteConnect`, `connectionHealth` and `createProviderConnectionsClient` (one port: list, test, start, completePaste, awaitDevice). Brand names come from `@builderforce/model-catalog`. `ProviderConnectError` now carries `detail`.
- **brain-ui `connections/`.** `ConnectionsPanel` sits under the Status tab of the ONE `BrainComposer` (`account.connections`). Each row shows its health (working, usage limit, not entitled, sign-in expired, unreadable), a Test button that repaints the row from the probe's verdict, and an in-place Reconnect (paste code or device approval) for subscription rows. THE connect state machine is `reconnectFlow.ts`: one flow per (client, provider) that lives OUTSIDE React, read through `useProviderReconnect`. It does this so that closing the menu mid-connect neither aborts a device approval (which the server redeems only when a poll sees it) nor loses a paste step. Every await is fenced by a generation number. A gateway 403 on the list shows a "not available from here" line rather than hiding the section. A probe that persisted no verdict leaves the row's health alone. Copy goes through `connectionsLabelsFrom` (`connections.<key>`). All colours are theme tokens, and the actions wrap.
- **Hosts.**
  - Web: `lib/providerConnections.ts` (`webConnections`), `providerConnections.*` in all 5 catalogs.
  - VS Code: `editorConnections` over the new `authedGateway`, which shares `authedFetch`'s token-refresh send. The host's new `open.external` opens only a provider sign-in URL (`isSubscriptionSignInUrl`, from the per-provider `signInDomains` in `@builderforce/model-catalog`). `conn.*` keys are in `connectionsLabels.ts` and all l10n bundles.
  - Rovr: `PanelServices.gateway` (one status-preserving call, which the Kimi account now takes too) and `PanelServices.connections`, with `conn*` messages in all 5 locales. `useKimiConnect` now runs on the same flow, so a Kimi connect started from Settings or from the Status tab shows in both.
- **Duplicates removed.**
  - The web settings card's own start/paste/device-poll state now runs on `useProviderReconnect`. Remove and Save stay disabled while a connect is in flight. The web lookup passes `{code}` through literally.
  - Deleted: `providerKeysApi.oauthStart` and `oauthComplete`, `isDeadConnectCode`, the unused `providerKeys.errStartConnect`, and the VSIX `bfApi.completeByoOAuth` and `ByoOAuthCompleteResult` (now `completePasteConnect`).
  - The VSIX `byoConnections.ts` provider list is derived from `LLM_PROVIDER_INFO`.

**Tests:** new `provider-connect/src/connections.test.ts`, `brain-ui/src/connections/ConnectionsPanel.test.tsx` (including survives-menu-close and late-device-approval cases) and the `isSubscriptionSignInUrl` cases in `model-catalog/src/providers.test.ts`. Existing tests unchanged.

**Still open:** whether only owners/managers may reconnect is an operator decision, logged in ROADMAP (OTHER).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — PRD 35 WS8i–o: the overnight run that did nothing — children stop delegating, routing finds the coder, dead and nearly-spent accounts stop leading (api 2026.10.81 · brain-embedded 2026.10.53 · agent-stall 2026.10.1 · agent-tools 2026.10.14 · model-router 2026.10.18 · tool-output-policy 2026.10.2)

**Why.** VS Code chat #6 ("implement the PRD using subagents") ran ~6.5 hours overnight: 857 turns, 11 children, 5 files written, all on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`. Diagnosed from the chat's local journal and the ops DB (`llm_failover_log`, `llm_usage_log`).

**What shipped:**
- **8i: a mention of sub-agents is not a request for them.** Every PRD 35 brief names the sub-agent policy, and the delegation gate read any mention as an ask, so the WS1 coder was told "STOP READING AND DELEGATE" at step 2 and spent 90 minutes spawning and waiting on researchers. `asksForSubagents` now needs an ask ("use / with / via / delegate to / run … sub-agents", "spawn agents", "fan out the …"). A sub-agent runs the same gate as its owner, on its own brief: no child-only branch. One `runLeftDelegationUndone(run)` serves the early nudge, the prose-end backstop and the `ask_user` redirect.
- **8j: child reports reach the owner whole.** One `SUBAGENT_REPORT_CHARS` (8K) and `clipChildOutput` in agent-tools, used by the VS Code and cloud report builders; `wait_agents` budgeted at 34K, so four clipped reports and their headers fit (`subagentReportBudget.test` holds the two numbers together). Before: 4K per report, then 6K for the whole wait.
- **8k: evidence cannot seal out a stronger coder.** `liftUntriedStronger` (model-router): on quality-first roles an untried model stronger than every measured one keeps its lead until it is measured. Connected-account and plan-pool paths both.
- **8l: empty-handed runs count.** An IDE change request that ran ≥20 turns and changed and delegated nothing reports `failed` (score 0) for the model that served most of its turns. Every run, top-level or sub-agent, is graded by that one rule on its own request; an owner's wake turn on its children's reports is not a request. A research brief ("Research / investigate / find / trace / audit …") reads as a question for every caller of `asksForChange` (agent-stall 2026.10.1).
- **8m: a refused OpenRouter connection stops leading.** Live failovers now raise connection alerts (keyed connections), and the credential resolver demotes alerted connections behind every healthy account (`demoteAlertedConnections`). ~1,770 401 attempts that night came from one connection. Resolves the auth-failover half of the roadmap's "Autonomous trigger errors and auth failovers" entry.
- **8n: routing reads how much of an account is left.** `providerHeadroom.ts` parses each attempt's rate-limit headers (Anthropic unified/API key, OpenAI-style `x-ratelimit-*`, Codex `x-codex-*`) via a per-attempt `observeHeaders` hook; an owner account ≥90% used is demoted until its window resets. Each header family is read in its own unit (Codex percent, Anthropic fraction). Per-minute TPM/RPM buckets are not quota: a remaining/limit window counts only when it resets ≥5 minutes out. The record is written past the response (`deferPastResponse`), once per window per isolate.
- **8o: one refresh verdict.** `isRevokedRefresh` (400/401/403) for the Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI and Kimi subscription resolvers. A dead Claude refresh token now reads "revoked — reconnect", not "expired — retry".
- Also: xAI's "out of credits or need a Grok subscription" 403 is classified as capacity (another session's change, same release); the repo scanners skip `.builderforce/` worktrees.

**Tests:** new `untriedStronger.test`, `runOutcomeReport.noDeliverable.test`, `earlyDelegation.child.test`, `providerHeadroom.test`, `openRouterConnectionDemotion.test`, `subscriptionRefreshVerdict.test`; existing router, role, delegation, outcome, resolver and capacity tests unchanged.

**Left for the operator (accounts, not code):** reconnect Claude (refresh token dead), top up or resubscribe Grok, check the Codex entitlement (403), and re-enter the OpenRouter connection key (401).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — PRD 35 WS8: VS Code runs read once, delegate early, stop when told

**Why.** A VS Code run took 79 turns to update PRD 35, dispatched nothing and never edited the PRD. "STOP" and "write the update now" were both ignored (PRD 35 §2.1, E1–E10).

**What shipped** (VSIX 2026.10.76; agent-tools 2026.10.13, agent-loop 2026.10.12, run-guards 2026.10.1, tool-output-policy 2026.10.1, model-catalog 2026.10.19, brain-embedded 2026.10.51, brain-ui 2026.10.24, agent-runtime 2026.10.19, api 2026.10.80 with regenerated container files):

- **8a: read coverage records what was served.**
  - Coverage covers the trimmed window the model saw, not the untrimmed file.
  - A covered replay serves the requested window, not line 1.
  - `cat`/`head`/`tail`/`sed -n` prints of a file count as reads, resolved against the shell's effective directory.
- **8b: one default repo.** `resolveDefaultRepo` resolves from an explicit `repo`, then a path in the request, then the chat's project repository, then a single checkout.
  - Git tools and `run_command` use it, and `run_command` accepts `cwd`.
  - The scope helpers moved to `git-repo-scope.ts`, which caches the "root is not a repo" answer.
  - `ticketBranchTool` uses the shared helpers.
- **8c: delegation nudged early.** When sub-agents were asked for and none has spawned by the 6th read, the read result carries the brief-shaped nudge. The end-of-run check stays as the backstop.
- **8d: memory.** Code-area fact writes carry `chatId` and `fileAnchors`. When Memory is off, the run trace says no facts were written.
- **8e: stop and steer.**
  - The abort signal reaches every tool. Stop or a timeout kills the shell's whole process tree.
  - The kernel races each dispatch against cancel. Every call in a stopped turn gets a "stopped" tool row, so the transcript stays valid.
  - A message typed while a run is going steers it. It interrupts a foreground command, or a wait on a background job, and is logged as `steer.applied`.
  - A steer arriving at setup, during unwind or after the run is never lost; it becomes the next turn.
  - "STOP executing" or `/stop` works like the button. On-prem's bare abort words are now in the same `run-guards` module.
  - A visible "Queue" control (⌥/Alt+Enter) holds a message until the run finishes. It is translated in all five bundles.
- **8f: context pack before turn 1.** It is built with no model call and attached as the volatile turn context:
  - the focus files (inlined, or their outline);
  - the chat's tickets and runs, through one shared reader with the web;
  - git state for each checkout;
  - matching `codemap:` facts.
  
  Inlined files count as already read. Recall searches with the request plus the focus-file hint.
- **8g: reads and shell.**
  - The per-result output limit is sized to the model's window (`windowedCap`); `read_file` gets 16–64k characters.
  - `read_file` takes `paths[]`, and a large markdown file returns its outline.
  - `run_command` takes `background` and `yieldMs`. `command_status` and `command_stop` work on jobs scoped to the run, and a run's jobs die when it settles or the extension deactivates.
- **8h: model preflight.** Before turn 1 the run checks BYO account health (this also triggers a token refresh) and announces an expired or unresolved provider and its fallback. A pinned model below the agentic tier gets a warning. `llm.model_downgrade` also fires for auto-routed turns.
- **Structure.** `brainRunHost.ts` was split into `brainRunHostContract`, `runSetup` and `runSteer` (591 → 395 lines). `run-guards` has its own vitest config.
- **Proof.** Every new test is in a new file or appended to an existing one; no existing assertion changed. Results, all targeted runs:

  | Package | Tests |
  |---|---|
  | brain-embedded | 236 |
  | clients/vscode | 157 |
  | agent-tools | 315 |
  | agent-loop | 200 |
  | run-guards | 64 |
  | tool-output-policy | 35 |
  | model-catalog | 31 |
  | brain-ui | 18 |
  | agent-runtime abort | 14 |

  These checks are green: silent-catches, source-package-graph, tenant-scope, i18n-keys and the container generator checks.
- **Left over:** the native chat participant, the web composer, the container shell and a stop during setup. They are in ROADMAP › Cloud and IDE agent runs.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-25 — Core holds no run telemetry: writers fixed, steps moved to ops

- **Core cleanup (prod).** Eight run-telemetry tables copied to ops (`db:copy-run-telemetry`, `run_context_state` verified on its natural key), checked, and truncated on core. 142,605 superadmin step rows and the remaining 253 other-user step rows deleted from `brain_chat_messages` (core now holds none), and 94 `activity_log` `task.created` rows moved to ops. `VACUUM FULL` took core from 621 MB to 319 MB.
- **Writers that still reached core, fixed.**
  - The retention sweep listed `primary` beside `transactional`, and its rollups INSERT rows, so sweeping core wrote telemetry back into core. Every swept table is now `OPERATIONAL` only (`sweptTablesBounded.ts`).
  - `siblingDatabase` returned core when the caller passed no env. It now falls back to the env the handle was built with.
  - `PlatformBroadcastService` and `StakeholderMapService` wrote `activity_log` directly. Both go through `activityDatabase`, and the broadcast console reads its engagement there.
- **Run steps on ops.** New `brain_chat_steps` table (ops `0023`, core mirror `1276`; ids start at 1e12 so they can never equal a message id). `appendRaw` and the VS Code sync importer (`SyncStepStore` port) send `isStepRow` rows there. The transcript tail read merges them back by time, so released clients are unchanged. Chat consolidation copies steps, and tenant delete cascades them. Retention is 30 days (14-day floor).
- **Diagnostics.** The shared copy-diagnostics report shows `History (loaded): N message(s) · M run step(s) · full dialogue: <location>`. N counts conversation rows only, and both counts are what the view has loaded. On VS Code the location is the local journal path plus the chat ids. On web it is the chat URL (origin and path only, because a query string can carry a share token) plus its messages API path.
- **Opus review fixes, same pass.**
  - **Steps keep their place on the web.** A merged step now carries the seq of the conversation row it precedes, or of the last row when nothing follows it (`anchorStepSeqs`). Before, it had seq 0, and the client's seq sort (`mergeTranscript`) jumped every step to the top after each turn, which broke `ratedTurnTool` and the prior-research readers.
  - **One clock per write.** `appendRaw` stamps both halves of a batch from one app clock, rising with the batch index. The two databases' separate `now()` no longer decide whether a step renders before or after its reply.
  - **Consolidation.** Copied messages keep their `createdAt`. Before, every copied step sorted ahead of the conversation and fell outside a truncated tail. Message inserts are chunked, and `copySteps` is one `INSERT … SELECT`, so a long chat no longer passes Postgres's bind-parameter limit.
  - **Sync retry.** A synced step without an event key is keyed `sync:<clientEntityId>`. It commits outside the sync transaction, and the key keeps a rollback retry from duplicating it.
  - **Segment erasure (DSR)** also erases the run steps of the segment's chats (`SegmentTelemetryKeys.chatIds`).
  - **`activity_log` readers left on core.** The visitor-journey flow and the journey reads now go through `activityDatabase`. The registry projection's `<domain>.events` facts used a cross-database JOIN. They are now an ops aggregate per object, a core domain lookup and an in-memory fold.
  - **`= ANY(${array})`** is a row value under Drizzle and Postgres rejects it. It is now `IN ${array}` in the broadcast console, the suspect-accounts read and the revoke route.
  - **Removed** the core `brain_chat_messages.step_payloads` column retention. Core has no steps, and the ops row sweep replaces it.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — VSIX memory growth while a chat streams, from PRD 36 and the run host (VSIX 2026.10.73 · local-first 2026.10.26 · brain-embedded 2026.10.49)

- **What was wrong.**
  - **Per-token full-store copies (PRD 36 regression).** PRD 36 made the run host translate running LOCAL chats to their SERVER ids for the Sessions tree. It did that on every run-store event (`clients/vscode/src/brainRunHostPorts.ts` `onRunsChanged`). The run store emits on every streamed text delta, and each lookup (`identity.serverIdFor`) is a `store.read`. The in-memory local-first store `structuredClone`d its whole state on every read and every transaction (`packages/local-first/src/store.ts`). On a 14 MB store that is about 14 MB of copying per token for each running chat, and the async reads piled up faster than they finished.
  - **Run cells never evicted (older than PRD 36, found in review).** The host subscribed to every run key it ever ran and never unsubscribed (`brainRunHost.ts` `watch`). The run store never evicts a cell that has a listener, so every chat's and sub-agent's cell stayed for the editor's whole session, each with up to 500 trace events and 50 appended messages. The panel replay set (`known`), each panel's delta bookkeeping, the stored run specs (with the turn's seed and research) and empty note recorders also only grew.
  - **Per-token repaints and resends.** The forced closing turn repainted on every delta instead of once per frame (`brain-embedded/src/runStore/runLoop.ts`). Every 32 ms frame relayed the WHOLE streamed reply to each panel, so a long reply cost O(n²) bytes in the host (`brainRunHostProtocol.ts` `syncMessageFor`).
- **Fix.**
  - The run host looks the bound ids up only when the run set changes (a key of the sorted running and awaiting ids), or when a store commit may have bound a live chat.
  - The memory store indexes committed rows into fresh maps without cloning the whole state first. Its getters already return clones and its writes already store clones, so a draft never touches a committed row.
  - `clients/vscode/src/runWatches.ts` subscribes to a run only while it is live and releases it when the run settles, so the store can evict its cell. The replay set is capped at the store's 50-cell bound, and a dropped key's per-panel bookkeeping goes with it. A settled run's cleared error is relayed directly.
  - Stored specs drop the turn's seed, research and message, which no child or wake reuses. Empty note recorders are deleted.
  - The closing turn coalesces its deltas like every other turn.
  - The streamed text is relayed as a delta from what each panel was last sent (`textFrom` / `text`). `webview/src/hostRunDriver.ts` splices it back.
- **Still open (Gap Register).** The unbound journal keeps a second full copy of every message. *Blocker: operator decision.*

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — PRD 36: a VS Code chat's local number never leaves the machine; chats bind on sign-in, spend is priced on the device, history syncs on enable (api 2026.10.78 · VSIX 2026.10.71 · brain-embedded 2026.10.48 · brain-ui 2026.10.23 · local-first 2026.10.25 · Rovr 2026.10.25 · frontend 2026.10.92)

- **What was wrong.** VS Code numbers its chats 1, 2, 3… on the device. It sent that number to the server as the chat id: in gateway metadata, in the model's prompt, in the ticket backstops, in run context and Evermind scope, and in the ticket rail. So local chat N read, edited and was billed to server chat N. The spend pill never showed in VS Code. Rovr sent its negative device ids the same way. The native session restore and the cloud audit path read the server by local id.
- **36.1, the leak.** A chat reaches the server only through a binding (`BrainRunRequest.serverChatId`, `serverChatIdOf`). An unbound chat sends no chat id at all. The gateway also drops a `chatId` that the caller's tenant does not own (`resolveCallerAttribution`). Acceptance test: `brain-embedded/src/runStore/serverChat.test.ts`.
- **36.2, bind on sign-in.** `createLocalChatIdentity` binds a chat on its first signed-in run. It sends only the title and project; `POST /api/brain/chats` is now a connected feature. The rail, participants and diagnostics use the bound chat. The Sessions tree translates between the server ids it lists and local ids (`clients/vscode/src/sessionChats.ts`). It continues only the caller's own chats; a colleague's chat opens on the web.
- **36.3, spend on the device.** The fold and the cost rule moved into `@builderforce/spend-contract`, and the api re-exports them. A bundled price snapshot in `@builderforce/model-catalog` is regenerated on every VSIX release. A per-call usage ledger records the cache split and the run-end memory call. The pill shows spend offline, with ≈ on estimates. A new `local_model` saving prices local calls against the chat's paid route. All 5 locales on VS Code, Rovr and the web.
- **36.4, sync on enable.** The server gains chat, message and usage importers. They write only into the caller's OWN chat (`resolveOwnChatId`). A synced usage row is written once: partial unique index migrations `1275` / transactional `0022`, and the `sync-usage:` key prefix is reserved for the importer, so a gateway caller cannot use it to skip billing. A failed write is retried, never marked applied. Offline history goes up as one import per row. After sync, a bound chat's pill does not count imported rows twice.
- **Review.** Two Opus reviews ran: a peer session's review of the first commit, then a review of the fix diff. Both found real defects, and every one is fixed; the details are in the PRD's §7 "As built".
- **Test decisions that change behaviour, not retargets.** `syncImporterFor('chat')` is now `importSyncedChat`. `POST /api/brain/chats` is now `connected-feature`. The `unlinkedRunId` test was removed with the function, which has no caller.
- **Verified (Sonnet, targeted).**
  - Builds: brain-embedded and brain-ui `dist`, including `.d.ts`.
  - Typechecks: api, brain-embedded, brain-ui, VS Code host/webview/canvas/harness, Rovr and spend-contract.
  - Guards: source-package graph, plus api conflict-targets, tenant-scope, layering, application-layering, domain-boundary, usage-counts, signature-duplication, migrations and schema.
  - Tests:
    - api: 14 sync / llm files
    - brain-embedded: 5 files, 115 tests
    - local-first: 534 tests
    - brain-ui: 42 tests
    - VS Code: 15 files, 179 tests
    - Rovr: 6 tests
- **Not proven here.** Not run against a live Postgres: the migrations and the `ON CONFLICT` predicate, which `check:conflict-targets` checks lexically. Not exercised end to end: sync with a real account.
- **Still open (Gap Register).** Cross-device chat history: chats synced from another device are hidden, and a web-only chat opens without its earlier transcript. *Blocker: operator decision.*

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — One cloud runtime: every run is the one engine, and the container is only its sandbox (api 2026.10.76 · agent-runtime 2026.10.18 · frontend 2026.10.91 · VSIX 2026.10.68)

- **What was wrong.** The paid "container" surface ran its OWN agent loop inside `api/container/server.mjs` (`runImageLoop`, a compiled copy of the kernel, a relayed tool table, an `llm` op, `finalize`/`fail` ops). The GitHub Actions runner inlined a third copy. So a run behaved differently by plan, and every engine improvement had to be made twice. The run record, the code map, the per-turn brief and the IDE-workspace writes reached some surfaces and not others.
- **The design.** Every cloud run, on every plan, runs the ONE engine (`cloudAgentEngine.ts`) on the durable runner (CloudRunnerDO). The plan decides only what a run is charged (the monthly cloud-run allowance). The container is a SANDBOX the engine calls for what a Worker cannot do. `api/container/sandboxCore.mjs` is the one implementation of its primitives: list/read/write/delete in the clone, run a command, and drain the post-edit checks. It has two transports. The Cloudflare Container serves it over HTTP (`server.mjs`, proxied by AgentContainerDO). The GitHub Actions runner inlines it (`githubActionsRunner.ts`, from the generated `sandboxCoreSource.ts`, drift-checked by `check:sandbox-core`) and long-polls the run's CloudRunnerDO for the engine's requests (`sandbox/sandboxMailbox.ts`), because nothing can call into a runner.
- **Engine side.** `sandbox/runSandboxHost.ts` decides the run's sandbox on the prep tick (Actions runner, else the container when bound and the repo is clonable) and opens it so the clone and the preview warm early. It hands each tick a `RunSandbox` and closes it at run end. A paused Actions run releases its runner, and `/resume` queues a fresh one. `sandbox/sandboxProvider.ts` puts the sandbox behind the SHARED tool definitions: `shell` (`run_command`, the `git_*` tools, `analyze_codebase`), with a heartbeat during long commands and the run's cancel killing them; reads from the working tree; and writes that commit through the provider's existing path (lease, outbound inspection, file-change ledger) and are then absorbed into the clone. A run's capability set is the cloud set plus `shell` when sandboxed (`runSurfaceCaps.ts`), so it also keeps `search_code`, `run_checks` and `web`, which the old container set lacked. The run's sandbox is stamped on its payload (`withRunSandbox`), so run history (`chatRunHistory.ts` `sandbox`), the `chats.runs` tool and chat diagnostics say whether a run could build.
- **Behaviour ported from the old container loop, not dropped.** (1) Post-edit checks: the sandbox's verdict now feeds the engine's own D1 cascade and D7 steer (`loopGuards.ts`), not a container-only cascade. (2) Committed writes are absorbed by fast-forwarding the clone to the ticket branch (`absorbCommit`), so `git_undo`/`git_redo`/`git_sync_latest` act on real history, which the old per-command fetch preamble approximated. (3) Run-end verify runs the project's declared checks in the sandbox with honest exit codes (`sandbox/sandboxVerify.ts`). (4) `analyze_codebase` saves its full snapshot for the visualizer and returns a bounded summary (`cloudAgent/auditAnalysis.ts`). (5) Repo-less (zero-setup) projects read and write their IDE workspace through the engine (`cloudAgent/ideWorkspaceProvider.ts`); before this only the container's `write` op could, so a durable run told the model to paste its deliverable into the summary. (6) Live preview starts when the sandbox opens.
- **Deleted.** The image loop (`agentImageLoop.mjs`, the kernel bundle `agentLoop.mjs` and its generator), the relayed tool table (`agentRelay.mjs`), the in-image analyzer bundle, the op table (`containerOps.ts`: `llm`, `write`, `verify`, `finalize`, `fail`, `heartbeat`, `ask_human`, the relayed ops), `imageRunTurn`, `imageToolHandshake.ts`, `imageCascade.ts`, `containerRunModelStore.ts`, `skillOp.ts`, `containerRunLauncher.ts` and `CONTAINER_MAX_STEPS`. Also `CONTAINER_SURFACE_CAPS`, the container branch of resume, the container executor and its health-probe fallback, and the `containerRuntime` plan feature and its picker gate. From the image went bf-context, `repoIndex.mjs`, `stringEdit.mjs`, `fileWindow.mjs`, `semanticTools.mjs` and `readOnlyTools.mjs`. The container run context is now the run identity only (`loadSandboxRunContext`), so its plan/routing cache and the card-validation cache bust that existed for it are gone. A container crash no longer self-heals by re-dispatching (that would start a second engine). The next sandbox call reopens a fresh clone. The picker offers Automatic, Builderforce Cloud and GitHub Actions in all five locales, and a stored `container` reads as the cloud runtime.
- **On-prem keeps ONE run record.** `agent-runtime/src/infra/run-knowledge-registry.ts` owns each run's recorder. The agent loop's brief and the knowledge loop's note and code map read the same one, and the knowledge loop no longer re-records calls the loop recorded.
- **Not proven here:** a live container deploy and a live Actions run. The sandbox is exercised by its unit tests and the typecheck, and the image needs `wrangler deploy` (see the Gap Register).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — Short-term vs long-term memory is a builderforce-memory concept; the per-turn brief rides the cacheable volatile tail (builderforce-memory 2026.10.24 · VSIX 2026.10.68)

- **Why it moved.** The per-run record (what this run read, searched and changed) and its consolidation into a `codemap:<area>` fact are memory, not tool plumbing. They lived in `packages/agent-tools/src/run-knowledge.ts`. They now live in `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory/working`: `WorkingMemory` is short-term memory (`observe`, `brief` restated before every turn); `consolidate` / `mergeConsolidated` turn it into long-term memory. `agent-tools` keeps only the tool vocabulary: `RunKnowledgeRecorder` maps every runtime's tool names (`fileToolKind`, the search tools) onto observations, and exposes `brief()` and `consolidate()`. `runLedgerBrief`, `buildCodeMapFact`, `codeMapFromActivity`, `mergeCodeMapFact` and `CodeMapFact` are deleted.
- **Prompt-cache defect fixed.** The 2026.10.67 ledger rode the request as an UNTAGGED trailing user message. The gateway's history breakpoint therefore landed on a block that changes every turn, so every turn re-billed the whole transcript. The small-window packer also took it for the user's latest request and could summarise the real request away. The volatile-tail convention (`<run-state>`) now lives in `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory/handoff` (`volatileTail`, `isVolatileTail`, `VOLATILE_TAIL_TAG`). The packer (`packHandoff`) keeps a tail last, never treats it as the directive, and budgets the history around it. Every runtime sends the brief inside that one tail: the Brain loop (`completeTurn.ts`), on-prem (`agent-loop.ts`) and the cloud engine (`costLoopSession.turnMessages` sections, beside the budget line and task state). The gateway (`promptCaching.ts`) and `costLoop/volatileTail.ts` use the shared tag instead of their own copies. The local-first transport's `coreMessages` skips the tail.
- **Readers that took the tail for the request.** The local-success learner (`localSuccess/verifiedLocalLabel.ts`, `turnFeatures.ts`) and the gateway's workforce-model recall query (`gatewayChatSupport.ts`) read "the last user message", which a long run now ends with. Both skip the tail, so a successful local turn is no longer labelled a retry and recall still searches on the request.
- **Retired maps stay retired.** `upsertProjectFact` merges a new code map only into a LIVE prior row: not expired, not superseded. A map the decay sweep retired is no longer folded back in.
- **Merge rules.** A file a run deleted is removed from the area's map and never stored as a line. An earlier run's edits read as `changed earlier`, so a new run is not credited with them.
- **Editor fixes.** The run-end step (`editorRunEnd.ts`) takes the run record, so the code map includes searches. Memory goes to the project the run STARTED in when the run carries one: the native participant always does, and the panel does whenever its run names a project (`RunNoteOptions.projectId`). A panel run with no project falls back to the project selected at commit time. Only the editor's own tools feed the panel's record (`recordingOnly`), so a remote platform call never lands in the workspace's note or map. The panel swaps in the workspace's current SHAPE per run (`ports.grounding` → `getStableGrounding`: scan map, repo map, symbols, never notes). A panel opened mid-index therefore reaches the finished map, and the prompt bytes change only on a rescan. The participant's run end runs in a `finally`, so a turn that threw or was stopped still leaves its note. A recorder lent by the host is named for the request when it has no prompt yet (`runPreamble.ts` `recorderFor`).
- **On-prem.** `knowledge-loop.ts` records each call with its own arguments, so searches reach the brief and the map, and clears pending arguments on every result instead of only on checks.
- Tests: builderforce-memory `working/working.test.ts` and `handoff/handoff.test.ts`; `packages/agent-tools/src/run-knowledge.test.ts`, rewritten for the adapter; `clients/vscode/src/memoryCommit.test.ts` and `brainRunHost.test.ts`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — Every run starts from what the last one found: one run-knowledge record for every runtime (VSIX 2026.10.67)

> Superseded in part by the entry above. The ledger described below rode the request UNTAGGED and did break prompt caching. The memory concepts it names (`runLedgerBrief`, `codeMapFromActivity`, `mergeCodeMapFact`) moved to `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory/working` and were deleted here.

- **Symptom (VS Code chat #162).** "Move the visualization canvas to a side panel" took 92 turns and 25 minutes. 17% of calls revisited ground already covered and 24 were exact duplicates. Project-fact writes: 0. The next run on the same area would have had to search the same way again.
- **Root cause 1: the panel froze its knowledge at open.** The webview built the system prompt, including the workspace map and recent run notes, once from `init.grounding`. Every later run in that panel started from the notes of runs from before the panel opened, never from the run that just finished.
- **Root cause 2: what a run FOUND was never kept.** The accumulators recorded only created and edited files. The learned-facts step ran only for runs that changed files, and its prompt says not to list files. So "where X lives" left with the transcript.
- **Root cause 3: three copies of the run lifecycle.** The loop kernel and the engine were already one. The record around them was not: VSIX `SessionNotes`, on-prem `RunAccumulator` and the cloud `writtenPaths` set used three different tool-name lists. On-prem also counted a write that failed.
- **Root cause 5: inside one run, the model re-derived the codebase every turn.** Its `<think>` reasoning is stripped from the next turn's transcript (deliberately: models copy the markup). Old tool results compact out of the 64k working window. So late turns could see neither what was read nor what was concluded. Completion tokens climbed to 8–10k a turn for two tool calls each, re-analysing the same files.
- **Root cause 4: the Memory switch was ignored at run end.** With Memory off, the run host still committed learned facts.
- **Fix.** `packages/agent-tools/src/run-knowledge.ts` is the one record. `RunKnowledgeRecorder` (contract `RunKnowledgeLog`) was extracted from the VSIX `SessionNotes`. It now also records reads, searches and deletes through ONE classifier, `fileToolKind`, which `agentReplyLoop.ts` now uses instead of its own list. Paths come from the shared `toolCallPaths`. `buildCodeMapFact` / `codeMapFromActivity` turn a run into a deterministic `codemap:<area>` fact with no model call. Changed files rank first, then reads by count (`rankByCount`, shared with the note format). Absolute paths resolve against the workspace root. Build output, dependencies, lockfiles and `.builderforce/` are dropped. The area is the deepest directory holding a majority of the files, so a root DONE.md edit never decides the key. `mergeCodeMapFact` runs inside `upsertProjectFact`, the one place every runtime's write lands, so a small run ADDS to an area's map instead of overwriting it. Wired in four places. (1) Both editor surfaces through ONE run-end step, `editorRunEnd.ts` `recordEditorRunEnd`: the note is awaited because the next run reads it. The facts write is not awaited, so the chat is no longer held claimed. It is gated on Memory by `memoryCommit.ts` `commitRunKnowledgeIfAllowed`. The native chat participant now has a run end at all. (2) On-prem `knowledge-loop.ts` records once per call on its result, success only. Verify still sees failed checks (`invokedTools`), and the map is pushed via `pushProjectFact` with the workspace root. (3) The cloud `cloudAgentEngine.ts` `afterDispatch` → `commitRunMemory({ codeMap })`, written at PROJECT scope; the default ticket scope hid it from every other run. The shared note format gains `**Read**` and `**Deleted**` lines. Fresh run notes reach each editor run through the per-run context seam (`recentActivitySection` joined to `augmentSystemPrompt`). The panel's system prompt holds only the stable workspace shape (`getStableGrounding`), so it stays a cacheable prefix. The VSIX `SessionNotes` class is deleted.
- **In-run fix.** `runLedgerBrief(recorder)` restates the run's own record ("What this run has already established": changed files, reads with counts, searches) in front of EVERY tool turn. It rides that request only, never the transcript, so it does not grow history or break prompt caching. It is wired into the Brain loop (`brain-embedded` `completeTurn.ts`; the run context holds ONE `knowledge` recorder, recorded in `afterDispatch` on success, and the VSIX host passes its own via `BrainRunRequest.knowledge`, so the ledger and the note/code map are one record). The same ledger goes to the cloud engine (`cloudAgentEngine.ts` per-turn messages) and the on-prem loop (`agent-runtime/src/builderforce/agent-loop/agent-loop.ts` `streamAssistantResponse`).
- Tests: `packages/agent-tools/src/run-knowledge.test.ts`, `clients/vscode/src/memoryCommit.test.ts` (commitRunKnowledge, commitRunKnowledgeIfAllowed: Memory off never resolves the facts port; absolute paths), `brainRunHost.test.ts`, `brain-embedded/src/brainRunStore.test.ts` (the bare-"Fix" test now reads the whole request; the B1 stable-prefix lever moved that directive into the turn context), `agent-runtime/src/infra/knowledge-loop.test.ts`, `api/.../runEndMemory.codeMap.test.ts`.
- Residual: container runs and the brain-reply loop. See the Gap Register (`[runtime] Container and brain-reply runs do not commit a code map yet`).

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — VS Code canvas no longer calls the gateway without a token (VSIX, ships with the next build ≥ 2026.10.66)

- **Symptom.** The BuilderForce output channel showed `[webview api] POST /api/creation-sessions/<id>/presence → 401 — Missing or malformed Authorization header`, and the same for `GET /api/agile/ceremonies/sessions`. The request carried no token at all.
- **Root cause 1: a pinned on-device model freed the board, not just the chat.** `WorkspaceScreen` mounted the board on `tokenReady || init.localRoute`, and the root skipped the tenant-token mint on a local route. A durable (server-persisted) board then polled presence and loaded ceremonies through the web app's API client with no `setEmbedAuth` token.
- **Root cause 2: the visualization split never handed the token over.** `VisualizationScreen` mounted the same server-persisted `CreationCanvas` without ever calling `setEmbedAuth`, so every canvas read in that panel went out without a token.
- **Fix.** `webview/src/canvas/useBoardAuth.ts` is the one gate both screens read. It bridges the token into `setEmbedAuth`, mounts a local board (`durable === false`) at once, and makes a server board wait for the token, minting it itself when a local route skips the root gate. `canvas/BoardAuthNotice.tsx` says why a board isn't drawn yet (Connecting… / Couldn't reach · Retry / Sign in), above the chat, which stays usable. It reuses the existing `app.*` labels.
- Tests: `src/authPanelSync.test.ts` ("never mounts a server-persisted board without the tenant token").

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-24 — Hybrid runs local turns on OUR engine inside the editor; Ollama/FreeToken rank last with their real windows and executable tool calls (local-inference 2026.10.20 · brain-embedded 2026.10.45 · VSIX 2026.10.66 · Rovr 2026.10.23 · builderforce-inference `bfi-engine` / `bfi-node`)

- **Symptom (chat #9, VSIX 2026.10.65, Hybrid).** A 67-tool "fix the merge conflicts, commit and push" turn ran on `local/ollama/hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B…` (CPU). It received 2,050 prompt tokens, made 0 tool calls, wrote fenced `bash` blocks about an unrelated task and took 7m49s.
- **Root cause 1: the ranking.** With our engines unable to take the turn, a third-party server won it. Operator decision: Ollama and FreeToken stay in the automatic tier but rank LAST, behind our engines. `automaticRank` in `packages/local-inference/src/runtimes.ts` is now webllm 10 · bfi 20 · synapse 30 · browser 40 · ollama 50 · freetoken 60. Nothing is excluded. Settings copy (`config.localModels.localFirst.desc`) is updated in all five locales.
- **Root cause 2: Ollama reported its trained window.** `/api/show` said 262,144; Ollama served `num_ctx` 4,096 and truncated silently. `probe.ts` now reports the window our option-less requests get: the Modelfile `num_ctx` when set, else the loaded `/api/ps` `context_length`, else Ollama's 4,096 default, capped by the trained length.
- **Root cause 3: the tool calls were never lifted.** Qwen3-Coder's native `<tool_call><function=x><parameter=k>` (passed through as text by an Ollama import without the `qwen3-coder` parser) is now parsed by `brain-embedded/src/xmlToolCalls.ts`. Values are kept verbatim (one newline trimmed at each end). The new `xmlToolArgTypes.ts` types each argument against the advertised schema, as Qwen's own parser does: a `string` property gets the text as written (`1.10` stays `1.10`, a JSON file's content stays text), and an `array` / `object` / `number` / `boolean` property is parsed.
- **Synapse's engine runs INSIDE the VSIX.** builderforce-inference:
  - `crates/bfi-engine` is extracted from `bfi-web` (state machine, load, chat, `contextFor`, `HostProfile`). `bfi-web` becomes its wasm face.
  - `crates/bfi-node` is the napi face: one engine thread per engine, a panic becomes a `RuntimeError` trap, and `pushChunk` is acknowledged chunk by chunk. A busy load never touches its stream, and every chunk promise settles. `dispose()` and the finalizer (a worker torn down mid-turn) close the chunk stream and abort, so the engine thread never outlives its engine.
  - Native GPU: bfi-core opens ONE process-wide wgpu device on the API CubeCL uses (Vulkan; Metal on macOS), with device-lost tracking. CubeCL runs server calls on its own thread, where thread-local error scopes cannot see them, so the device's uncaptured-error handler records errors instead of wgpu's default panic. `Gpu::checked` and `drain` report them as `Allocation` errors, and the KV probe (`kv_fits`, on the engine thread) still halves on out-of-memory. `support()` reports that same device.
  - CPU: rayon, with a KV budget of RAM/2/4 clamped to 512 MiB–2 GiB.
- **VSIX wiring.** `packages/bfi-node` is vendored by `scripts/vendor-bfi-node.mjs` (`--check` is in the api guard suite), sharing `scripts/lib/vendoredBuild.mjs` with `vendor-bfi-web`. Per-platform addons come from the inference repo's `bfi-node` workflow (`--from`). `esbuild.mjs` copies this platform's addon into `out/`.
  - The host worker (`hostBfi/worker.ts`) runs the addon, falling back to the wasm on the CPU.
  - The addon loads on first need (a cached Bonsai, a picker support read, a local turn), so a session with nothing cached and no local turn never maps it. Its `support()` probes off the JS thread and reads the GPU live: a device that failed to open or was lost reads unsupported, so the next turn runs on the CPU (`bfiEngine.ts` drops the dead GPU engine and re-probes).
  - Its bridge port is PREFERRED over the webview's (`pageEngineBridge.ts`).
  - A trapped native engine is disposed (`BfiEngineInstance.dispose`).
- **Bonsai auto-provisioning (operator decision 2026-10-24).** The first unpinned local-first TURN (never a panel opening or a scan: `resolveModelRoute(…, { turn: true })`) with no Bonsai cached downloads the largest recommended row the device fits, up to 4B (`hostBfi/provision.ts`). It shows a cancellable progress notification (localized ×5) and runs once per session.
  - Downloads write unique part files (`hostBfi/modelFiles.ts`). Two downloads in one host share one transfer, each hearing progress, and one caller cancelling leaves the other's transfer running. Two windows never corrupt each other's copy.
- **Measured (win32-x64, this dev machine).** Bonsai-1.7B on native WebGPU: f16 KV, 18,688-token window, 96 tokens in 37.7 s. On the CPU: 9,216-token window, 96 tokens in 297.7 s.
- **Tests:** `plan.test.ts`, `runtimes.test.ts`, `localFirstTransport.test.ts`, `hostModelStream.test.ts`, `xmlToolCalls.test.ts`, `xmlToolArgTypes.test.ts`, `bfiEngine.test.ts`, `pageEngineBridge.test.ts`, `hostBfi/{runtime,provision,modelFiles}.test.ts`, `modelRouting.test.ts`, Chrome `route.test.ts`, `cargo test -p bfi-engine`, and `crates/bfi-node/smoke.mjs` (support, workers, busy, load, chat, abort).
- Also carried by VSIX 2026.10.66: the canvas board-auth fix from 7dacfda40.
- Still open (Gap Register): prose-only answers to a local tool turn are accepted, and the chat diagnostic calls "0 mutating calls" healthy.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-23 — Every consumer on builderforce-memory 2026.10.23 (api 2026.10.74 · frontend 2026.10.89 · agent-runtime 2026.10.17 · brain-embedded 2026.10.44 · VSIX 2026.10.65)

Every `@seanhogg/builderforce-memory*` range is now `^2026.10.23`, and the lockfiles are reinstalled.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-23 — Route consolidation: the four data-migration duplicates folded into one store each (api 2026.10.71 · frontend 2026.10.86)

Operator decisions (2026-10-23): templates go into `catalog_items`, canvas relations go onto the kernel, `agent_assignments` is canonical, and releases carry plan vs actual dates. Each move ships expand/contract. Migrations 1263–1266 only add and backfill, so the old Worker keeps running through the deploy window. The contract followed in two more releases, each safe against the Worker still live during its deploy window. The second release (api 2026.10.73 · frontend 2026.10.88) re-ran each fold and dropped the legacy template tables (1267) and `project_agents` (1269), and 1270 carried the canvas window writes, including removals, into kernel memberships. The third (api 2026.10.75 · frontend 2026.10.90) dropped `release_date` and added the plan-vs-actual CHECK (1272), dropped the legacy member columns so `creation_session_members` carries presence only (1273), and dropped `skill_assignments` after checking every grant had been carried into `artifact_assignments` (1274). The second release had made `skill_assignments` a restricted entity, because the Worker before it still counted that table.

- **Templates → `catalog_items` (1263):** kanban and canvas templates are catalog rows, read and written by one `catalogTemplateStore` (split into `templateKinds` / `templateCache`).
  - The generic entity surface is read-only for the catalog and hides private canvas templates.
  - Marketplace listing lookups filter to listing kinds.
  - The copy is recorded in a fold ledger, so window edits are refreshed (newest write wins) and window deletes are removed by 1267.
- **Canvas members → kernel `memberships` (1264):** board access is a kernel membership on the board's object, cached per grant and bumped on every write.
  - Fixed: board share links could be minted and revoked by non-members; the gate now sits in `ObjectRegistry`. Accepting an invitation can no longer demote the last owner. Three board creators now seat an owner. The roster listing is gated.
  - `creation_session_members` keeps only presence (viewport, cursor, replay cursor). Its legacy name stays, because renaming it would break the Worker live during a deploy. 1273 dropped its access columns.
- **`project_agents` → `agent_assignments` (1265):** one assignment store with integer handles.
  - Removal must name its target scope, so a chat member can't delete other assignments.
  - The MCP tools moved out of `builtinMcpService` and are MANAGER-gated through the same policy as REST.
  - The bridge and hire return both `agentHandle` and `projectAgentId`.
- **Release dates, plan vs actual (1266):** `target_date` / `released_at` replace `release_date`.
  - Legacy statuses are mapped and unknown ones abort. A date the new pair can't carry is kept in notes.
  - The legacy alias still returns `releaseDate`.
  - Release writes now invalidate the delivery-insights cache through a version token.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-23 — Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io) on every surface, one engine (api 2026.10.72 · frontend 2026.10.87 · agent-runtime 2026.10.16 · brain-embedded 2026.10.43 · VSIX 2026.10.64 · Rovr 2026.10.22 · @builderforce/agent-skills 2026.10.1)

The question was "what is the standard for skills, and do we support it?" The answer was: partly. The on-prem runtime loaded `SKILL.md` folders, but nothing else did, and nothing enforced the spec. Closed in one pass:

- **ONE implementation: `packages/agent-skills`** (zero-dep; Worker, browser, Node, VS Code host). It holds the spec rules (`name` kebab-case ≤ 64 and equal to its folder; `description` ≤ 1024; `compatibility` ≤ 500; `metadata` string map; `allowed-tools`), a YAML-subset frontmatter parser (a host may inject a full YAML parser), skill-folder read/write with path-escape and size limits, `SKILL.md` serialisation, and the `<available_skills>` catalog formatter. It is wired into all 8 tsconfigs.
- **agent-runtime:** `native-loader` validates through the package and reports problems as diagnostics. Before this, a missing description was dropped silently and naming rules were never checked. **Bug fixed:** `disable-model-invocation: true` was never honoured, because the string-coerced frontmatter was compared `=== true`. The catalog now comes from the shared formatter. `.claude/skills` (personal and project) now loads and is watched alongside `.agents/skills`. **`artifacts.sync` writes assigned skills to disk** as real folders (`agents/skills/assigned-sync.ts`, via `GET /llm/v1/skills/:name/package`). Before this it recorded slugs and assumed the files "were already present". A user's same-named folder is never overwritten.
- **Data:** migration 1259 adds `manifest` JSONB to `tenant_skills` and `marketplace_skills`, plus a `skill_files` table with exactly one owner (CHECK) that cascades with its skill. `skillFileStore` is the single reader/writer, and `toSkillFolder` is the single exporter.
- **ONE loader for every platform surface:** `application/skills/skillLibrary.ts` provides the catalog plus `readLibrarySkill` (instructions → bundled file), resolving workspace (approved) → marketplace (published or assigned) → builtin. It is exposed as the platform tool **`skills.read` → `builtin_skills_read`** (`llm/skillLibraryToolCatalog.ts`). The gateway rewrites the tool's description with each tenant's catalog and drops the tool when the library is empty. Through the one gateway catalog it reaches the Brain on web, VSIX and Rovr (pinned in `runPreamble` via `skillLibraryTools.ts`), the canvas and Studio, external MCP clients, and cloud and container runs (`CLOUD_AGENT_PLATFORM_TOOLS` and the `builtin_*` relay, so no image redeploy is needed). The @-addressed chat reply receives it through the platform set (it needs no chat, so it is not in `CHAT_SCOPED_AGENT_TOOLS`), and it is on the `delivery` surface.
- **Cloud runs: progressive disclosure.** The workspace-skills block is now a catalog (lever E1 still ranks it) instead of full inlined bodies. An assigned skill's readme cut at 4 KB now names the tool that returns the rest.
- **Portability:** `POST /api/workspace-skills/import` (MANAGER; the importer signs the skill off → approved; re-import replaces the whole folder) and `GET /api/workspace-skills/:id/export`. Marketplace `POST`/`PUT /marketplace/skills` accept `files` and derive slug, description and readme from the `SKILL.md`. New `GET /marketplace/skills/:slug/export` serves the folder. Gateway `GET /llm/v1/skills` and `/llm/v1/skills/:name/package`. `proposeSkill` holds an agent's slug to the spec name.
- **Web UI:** `SkillFolderPicker` validates in the browser with the same package. Also added: `SkillFolderImport` (SlideOutPanel), `SkillFolderExportButton` (.zip via fflate; on review cards and the public marketplace page), `WorkspaceSkillAuthor`, and `PublishWorkspaceSkillButton`. **Fake flow retired:** "My skills" and "Share to marketplace" lived only in localStorage (no body, never reached an agent, "shared" listings visible only in that browser). "New skill" now writes a real `SKILL.md` through the import path; the localStorage readers in `SkillsClient` and `MarketplacePageClient` are deleted. The publish form was extracted from `MarketplacePageClient` (1315 → ~1200 lines) into `PublishSkillForm`, with folder support. **Bug fixed:** the publish client sent `repoUrl`/`iconUrl` and no pricing, while the route reads snake_case `repo_url`/`icon_url`/`price`/`pricing_model`/`price_unit`; it is now mapped in one place (`skillDraftBody`). The token bridge is one hook (`useMarketplacePublisherToken`). 40 new `skillFolder.*` keys in 5 locales; unused `skillsPage.*` and `common.deleteSkillConfirm` keys removed.
- **Docs and marketing:** docs-site `tools/skills.md` and `creating-skills.md` (en and zh-cn) rewritten against the spec. The old `hello_world` example broke the name rule and claimed "single-line frontmatter only". New post `bring-your-skills-with-you` (+ zh/es/fr/de); an update note on `skills-assignment-and-the-marketplace` (5 locales); release note migration 1260.
- **ONE skill-assignment store (was two):** grants in `skill_assignments` (the host panel, `/api/skill-assignments`) never reached a run, because runs, the catalog and the on-prem sync read `artifact_assignments`. Migration 1261 copies every grant across (a union, `INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS`, through the re-runnable `backfill_skill_assignments()`). `skillAssignmentPort` now reads and writes `artifact_assignments` (scope `tenant`/`host`) and nothing touches the old table; the held contract 1271 re-runs the copy and drops it. `/api/skill-assignments` stays as a route because installed VSIX bundles still call it, and it now writes the store runs read.
- **Binary skill assets kept, not skipped:** migration 1262 adds `skill_files.encoding` (`utf8`/`base64`) and `r2_key` (CHECK: text inline, binary in R2, never both). Files travel as `{ path, content, encoding? }` on import, marketplace create/PUT, export and package; one shared request schema (`skillFolderSchema.ts`) caps base64 at the package's `SKILL_BINARY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`. `saveSkillFolder` uploads under a fresh write id, commits the row and file rows in ONE transaction, then deletes the replaced objects (or the new ones on failure). `skills.read` answers a binary path with a one-line description instead of bytes. With no UPLOADS bucket bound, a folder with binaries is refused up front (`binary_storage_unavailable`).
- **Host-exact on-prem sync:** `GET /llm/v1/skills/host` (agent-host keys) returns `{ skills: [{ name, updatedAt }] }`, which is every skill resolvable for a run on that host (`resolveArtifactsForHost`: tenant + host grants, plus the grants of projects bound to the host and agents registered on it). It is cached under the tenant's assignment version (`skillAssignmentCache`, bumped by every assignment writer) and the timestamps are read live, so the runtime prunes exactly instead of on a 7-day staleness window.
- **Review fixes:** paid marketplace skills are visible only when assigned, and the public export 404s for them. Saving a skill and its folder is atomic. The tenant-assigned slugs are cached. Re-import invalidates the old project's cache too. "New skill" refuses a name in use (409 `skill_name_taken`, `mode: 'create'`). Marketplace descriptions are capped at 1024 characters. `skills.read` respects the run's project scope. Non-uuid skill ids return 404. `skill_files` has tenant-column and shape-lint verdicts.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-23 — LLM cost optimization, wave 3: operator decisions applied, builderforce-memory 2026.10.22 published, lossless compaction in VS Code (api 2026.10.68 · brain-embedded 2026.10.42 · cost-levers 2026.10.1 · VSIX 2026.10.62 · builderforce-memory 2026.10.22)

Operator decisions (2026-10-23): pick the best approach for durable dense search, always take the cheaper option, keep free embeddings always on.

- **builderforce-memory 2026.10.22 published** (tag `v2026.10.22`, release run green). The api and VSIX now depend on `^2026.10.22`; the api's local `ensurePinned` stopgap is deleted because `packHandoff` honours `pinned` itself.
- **Claude Code memory hook reinstalled** from the published 2026.10.22 installer (operator-approved). The installer wrote the Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI and Codex CLI configs; it also added the `Stop` capture hook, and stubs are now injected with their `contentLost` label.
- **The 100 already-stubbed local memory facts are accepted as lost** (operator, 2026-10-23: no Evermind coordinator export). They stay flagged `contentLost` and are injected labelled at half weight; `memory_restore` remains available if a copy ever turns up.
- **VS Code lossless compaction landed** (the held patch): memorySnapshot / markdownMemory / memoryImport / evermindView. A fact is stubbed only after an Evermind recall probe passes.
- **The recall probe no longer records a saving per question.** `/api/projects/:id/answer?probe=1` answers as usual but skips `recordMemoryAnswerSavings`. The option is the shared `MemoryAnswerOptions.probe` in brain-embedded.
- **E3 free embeddings always on** (`e3_free_embeddings` rollout 100). This is safe before the backfill finishes, because recall dual-reads the 1536 column for rows without a 1024 vector. The paid 1536 backfill now runs only while some tenant is in the lever's off arm. Before this, it would have paid to re-embed every new write for a column no recall reads.
- **The semantic chat cache embeds with free bge-m3.** The paid 1536 model is used only when Workers AI can't answer. The space id is folded into the namespace, so the two models never share a bucket. Before this, every B2 lookup paid for an OpenRouter embed.
- **The semantic cache index stays on KV LSH; no Vectorize** (cost decision). A lookup is four KV reads, about $2 per million. A Vectorize query is billed per queried dimension, about $10 per million at 1024-d. KV also already provides the TTL and purge. What we give up is about 10% recall at the 0.92 bar.
- **C8 compression starts its A/B at 10%** like every lever that changes what the model sees (it was the one lever at 0%). It runs only where the local engine already reports a loaded compressor.
- **Batch calls write `llm_traces` rows** (`surface: 'batch'`, the job id and the provider batch id in the metadata), so a served batch job is traceable like a synchronous call.
- **Durable `semantic_search` is hybrid** (`repos/repoSymbolVectors.ts`):
  - definition vectors come from free bge-m3, embedded lazily on the first search and not on each commit;
  - vectors are keyed by definition text and stored per repository in R2 as int8, so a new commit re-embeds only the definitions it changed;
  - coverage is capped at the 6,000 definitions with the highest PageRank;
  - each embedding pass gets an 8 s budget (`indexing: true` while partial);
  - the dense ranking is fused with the keyword ranking by RRF. Without a Workers AI credential, search is keyword-only, as before.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-23 — LLM cost optimization, wave 2: verifier cascade, progress guards, cloud repo map, batch API, retrieval, specialists, cost dashboard (api 2026.10.67 · frontend 2026.10.83 · brain-embedded 2026.10.41 · agent-runtime 2026.10.15 · VSIX 2026.10.61 · Rovr 2026.10.21)

All behind `@builderforce/cost-levers`; lever off = previous behaviour.

- **A3 progress guards:** new `@builderforce/run-guards` (read coverage, failure tally, write ledger, edit-revert, no-progress) shared by the Brain and the cloud loop; trip 1 steers, trip 2 escalates a tier, trip 3 pauses for `ask_human`.
- **D1 weak-first verifier cascade** (`run-policy/cascade.ts`): soft-seeded runs start on the weakest tier; a failed post-edit check or finish gate escalates one tier (max 2 per unit) with the verifier's reason and a reasoning boost; container runs escalate on in-image check verdicts. Finish gates moved out of `cloudAgentEngine.ts` (2,660 → 2,478 lines across both waves).
- **D2 difficulty router** (`@builderforce/difficulty-router`, `cascade_outcomes`, migration 1254): daily-trained per-tenant/global heads skip a weak attempt predicted to fail.
- **D6 batch APIs:** deferred job queue (migrations 1255 / transactional 0020) over Anthropic Message Batches and OpenAI Batch at half price; memory consolidation, session summaries, ticket classification fallback and distillation teacher text defer; BYO calls batch only on the tenant's own key.
- **D7 deterministic paths:** arithmetic, unit and date answers without a model (not metered, counted as served-without-model); durable runs check written files immediately; container runs typecheck/lint/cargo/py_compile after edits and report failures only.
- **D8 concurrent read-only tool calls** in the kernel and the container loop.
- **C4 / C6 / E3 retrieval:** adaptive K (`chooseK`), Workers AI `bge-reranker-base`, `bge-m3` 1024-d columns with dual-read and an hourly catch-up backfill (migration 1256).
- **C5 cloud repo map:** `@builderforce/repo-map` (TS port of bf-index's PageRank) built from one tarball and cached per commit in R2 for durable runs; bf-context in the container image; `repo_map` / `semantic_search` advertised behind the lever.
- **C8 compression call sites:** shell and web-fetch outputs on Desktop/VSIX/on-prem surfaces.
- **B4 agent answer replay** on `memory_recall`; **E1** auto-drafted skills (never auto-approved); **E2** specialist admission (frontier-parity gate extracted from the Evermind coding gate, migration 1257); **E5** local success = served AND passed (retry, malformed-call or thumbs verdicts).
- **A4 cost dashboard:** Cost efficiency lens + hub card (KPIs incl. served-without-model, daily trend, lever on/off comparison) and per-run cost breakdown with budget vs cap; five locales.
- **Fixed along the way:** deterministic answers were metered as zero-token usage; `classifyTask.ts` string literals broken by an escape; arithmetic guard rejected `10 - 4 - 3` as a phone number; pre-existing failures in `packForModel.test.ts`, `useBrainConversation.test.tsx` (stale tool count) and Rovr `ChatView.test.tsx` (mock missing `pageEngines`); flaky lock-test cleanup.
- **Decided:** the cloud loop keeps the 5-minute prompt-cache TTL — durable ticks are seconds apart and the history breakpoint advances every turn, so 1-hour writes (2× vs 1.25×) would cost more; vendors still honour `cacheTtl: '1h'` when a caller passes it.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-22 — LLM cost optimization, wave 1: the audit's defects plus measurement, caching, context and routing levers (api 2026.10.66 · brain-embedded 2026.10.40 · agent-runtime 2026.10.14 · builderforce-memory 2026.10.22 · builderforce-inference 2026.10.11)

Every lever is gated by `isCostLeverOn` in the new `@builderforce/cost-levers` (env `COST_LEVER_<ID>=on|off|<pct>`, tenant-hash rollout, `COST_LEVERS_ALL=off` kill switch); lever off = the previous behaviour.

- **Defects closed (from the 2026-10-22 audit):**
  - Cloud turns now record cache read/creation tokens, so cloud spend is priced with the cache multipliers (`cloudLlmTurn.ts`).
  - Direct-Anthropic usage counted prompt tokens without cache tokens (underpriced, cache-hit rate could exceed 1); `anthropicPromptTokens()` fixes the JSON, stream and BYO `/v1/messages` meters, and the stream path now reports cache counts at all.
  - The limbic affect block, budget line and task state ride one trailing `<run-state>` block after the history, so the cached prefix holds on the direct-Anthropic and OpenRouter paths; the direct vendor honours `cacheTtl: '1h'` (`costLoop/volatileTail.ts`, `promptCaching.ts`).
  - Brain per-turn recall and limbic text moved out of the system prompt into a trailing `<turn_context>` block (`runStore/turnContext.ts`).
  - Work-mode prompt prefers `edit_file`; the container surface has `edit_file` (`repo.edit`) with edit_file semantics; container tool output returns head + tail, not the head.
  - Compaction pins the task brief; at most 5 relevance-ranked skills per run instead of 50 unranked.
  - Memory-answer cache keys are principal-scoped (`qa:v3`, one `cacheScope.ts` builder for every cache) and Brain answers send file anchors; semantic-cache KV writes expire after 7 days.
  - Per-run token cap alongside the $25 USD cap, so BYO runs (priced $0) are capped.
  - builderforce-memory: compaction is lossless (archive sidecar, stub only after an Evermind recall probe), `memory_restore`, `.bak` rotation, one store-path resolver; recall applies importance + recency.
- **Measurement (A1, A4, A5):** reasoning tokens, `turn_index`, `tool_schema_tokens` (migrations 1253 / transactional 0019), estimated context categories and lever arms on every usage row; `GET /api/cost/metrics` and `/api/cost/runs/:executionId`; spend-spike, run-outlier, containment-stop and run-anomaly alerts; cost per merged PR is per-run attributed everywhere.
- **Caching (B1–B3):** semantic cache on tool-free chat (tenant + project + principal + model tier scope, facts-revision and file-anchor staleness); per-isolate single-flight.
- **Context (C1–C3, C7, C9):** role core tool sets (≤20) + `tool_search`; observation masking every 6 turns; `update_task_state`; one `@builderforce/tool-output-policy` (caps table, line-boundary cuts, failure-focused shell/test summaries, JSON projection) used by the Brain, agent-runtime, the durable codec and the container; container `read_file` honours offset/limit; compaction respects long-context price tiers.
- **Routing and output (D3, D4, D5, D8):** Thompson exploration (≤5% cold share) with a 30-day half-life, never for pins/BYO-strict/premium; role reasoning effort (OpenRouter `reasoning` too); per-role `max_tokens`; prompt asks for batched independent tool calls.
- **Local engine (C5 ranking, C8, E4):** bf-index PageRank repo map + C#/Ruby/PHP/Kotlin/Swift; LLMLingua-2 compression in bf-context (feature `compress`); prompt-lookup speculative decoding and a byte-bounded LRU prefix cache in bfi.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-22 — One turn path on every surface: VSIX `s[i.method]` and `platform_send_disabled`, Studio/canvas no-model flow (frontend 2026.10.82 · VSIX 2026.10.60 · Rovr 2026.10.20 · brain-embedded 2026.10.39 · brain-ui 2026.10.20 · local-first 2026.10.23)

- **VSIX `s[i.method] is not a function`:**

  - The host now uses the shared `createLocalBrainPersistence`. The copy is deleted.

  - The VSIX and Rovr also refused ordinary writes the web allowed.

  - Every turn entry point now goes through the one `useInferenceModeGate`: the landing prompt, object Ask, inspector, queue and the signed-in panel seed. It keeps every held send in order.

  - `rovrBrainPersistence` is the device record with live `subscribeMessages`.
  - Its parallel send/run plumbing is deleted, and a jsdom ChatView mount test was added.
- **Also:**
  - The WebGPU adapter probe is bounded at 5 s (`settleWithin`).
  - `upgradeAction` gates on its PATHS table.
  - The dead webview `localPersistence.ts` / `persistence.ts` are removed.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-22 — BuilderForce in the VS Code agent chat area (VSIX 2026.10.59)

- **Where it shows:** a `viewsContainers.secondarySidebar` container (`builderforce-chat`) holds the webview view `builderforce.chatView`, so BuilderForce gets its own tab in the secondary sidebar next to Chat, Claude Code and Codex.
- **Older editors:** VS Code before 1.106 has no secondary-sidebar contribution point. There, `builderforce.doesNotSupportSecondarySidebar` is set and the same view appears in the BuilderForce activity-bar container as `builderforce.chatViewSidebar`. The version gate is the one Claude Code and Codex use.
- **One surface, two hosts:** the webview logic moved out of the 1,148-line `builderforcePanel.ts` into the host-agnostic `WorkspaceSurface`, which holds the bridge, run attach, page engines, model files and editor/pending-changes pushes.
  - It is backed by `workspaceInit.ts` (the `init` frame), `localFetchProxy.ts` (the fenced on-device fetch), `contextPicker.ts` and `brainChatLabels.ts`.
  - The editor tab (`BuilderForcePanel`, now about 170 lines) and the sidebar view (`chatView.ts`) each compose that surface. They differ only in their chrome: tab registry and status, or view description.
- **Callers:** `refreshWorkspaceSurfaces`, `notifyChatDeleted` and `configureWorkspaceSurfaces` replaced the panel-only statics, so sign-in, model, project, policy and permission changes now reach the sidebar view too. ## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-20 — Review of the 17–19 Oct commits: every finding fixed (api 2026.10.62 · frontend 2026.10.79 · VSIX 2026.10.54 · Rovr 2026.10.17 · agent-runtime 2026.10.13 · brain-embedded 2026.10.36 · local-first 2026.10.20)

- **Local-first durability.** A crashed lease holder no longer bricks the store: VSIX lock records pid + host start and is reclaimed only when that holder is provably dead; IndexedDB uses Web Locks (heartbeat fallback). `leaseBusy` still never steals from a live holder. Sync work carries a fence (signal + `holds()`); a timed-out or lost lease commits nothing. VSIX journal compacts (one policy with `journalStore`), tracks its prefix in memory, opens read-write (the append-mode handle failed `ftruncate` on Windows), and moves a corrupt snapshot cache aside on every open. Run recovery journals finished/cancelled/failed from the host's terminal events (`cancelled` is a real `ExecutionStatus`), so past runs are no longer mirrored as interrupted. One `bootDeniedHost` for web, VSIX and Rovr; `PlatformPolicyBoot` no longer writes a ticket. Webview bridge prunes disposed panels and posts policy only on change; change-set baselines fingerprint with bounded concurrency. `localFirstStore.ts` split into lock / journal IO / snapshot file / durable store / chat persistence.
- **Server sync wired end to end.** `/api/sync/v1/{push,pull}` mounted with auth; ONE Drizzle `SyncRepository` behind `SyncStores`; importers write inside the receipt transaction (savepoint) and refuse non-member assignees; replay looked up before validation with payload-hash check; pull carries the tip in the cursor (no idle-destination resnapshot loop, no lost changes while paging; MAX(seq) + index, migration 1251). Clients mint UUID event ids; the composite is `idempotencyKey`. Destination tenant comes from auth only; first bind = developer+ on the project (PRD question closed). 30 twin modules (second cursor codec, occurredAt gate, apply, pull readers, batch handler) deleted.
- **api correctness/security.** Approval decide claims the row (`status='pending'` in the UPDATE, 409 otherwise). Chat-turn saves stay exempt but agent dispatch + mention notifies spend a `:dispatch` bucket. Built-in agent refs no longer 500 a canvas save. Advisor: invite works across the advisor/founder tenants (declared `acrossTenants`) with a localized client action; continuation re-checks active service/host and provisions; provisioning idempotent (migration 1249); admission cached. Evermind transfer requires `approved`; learning runs swept at 90 days (migration 1250). Counter buffer honours `CACHE_L2_KV`. Workspace list invalidated on plan/billing/rename. Reaper ceiling in SQL; impersonation ignores expired sessions; run-activity cache keyed by day; likes require the artifact; board cache bump inline. 1099 export no longer relabels a DB failure as "invalid year".
- **LLM/Brain.** Tool retry only on structured 429/Retry-After, only for tools declared idempotent, wall-time bounded — exec/write never re-run. Compaction counts tool-schema tokens with one estimator and restores the elision fallback. "Saved" figures: compaction counts only what could have been sent; savings origin derived server-side from `llm_usage_log` (client value dropped), chat access + `memory_enabled` enforced on `/answer`. Stream header deadline per attempt; abort listener removed. Canvas memory switch off until the chat's setting loads. Guest allowance meters model round-trips. QA telemetry uses keepalive fetch with auth (no silent anonymous drop). `prompt_cache_key` reaches the provider (it was dropped since 67859cc2c).
- **God files split.** `ChatTicketService` (14 modules + thin facade), `projectFacts`, `advisoryReservation`, `localFirstStore`, `runChangeSets`, `mountSyncBatch`.

## ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-18 — A steer in one chat restarted another running chat (brain-embedded 2026.10.35 · VSIX 2026.10.49)

- **Reported.** "Only do analysis", steered into chat #149's live run, stopped chat #148, which was running four sub-agents in parallel. The text was saved correctly to #149 (row 88935, `midTurn`). 20 s later #148's top-level run started fresh, at step 0, on those exact words. No user row was written to #148.
- **Root cause.** `useBrainConversation` held `messages` as a bare list. When the panel walked from #149 to #148, the first render had `chatId = 148` while the list (and `loadingMessages = false`) were still #149's. The auto-reply effect saw an idle #148, whose owner was parked while its sub-agents worked, with a trailing un-directed user row: #149's steer. It called `startRun(148, …, last.content)`. #148's cell already had a transcript, so the seed was ignored and only the stolen text was appended. The same stale render also fed `markChatRead(148, <#149's seq>)`, the ratings and `send`'s seed.
- **Fix.** The list is held as `{ chatId, list }` and read only for its own chat. Every write names its chat and is dropped otherwise, which replaces `stillOpen()` for the list. The auto-reply also never replays a mid-turn user row: a steer was already delivered to a live run. `useRunSnapshot` now reads through `useSyncExternalStore`, so it is correct on the render a key switch lands in; the state-plus-effect version returned the previous key's snapshot for one render. The hook's inline copy and the webview's duplicate `useRunSnapshotOf` (`chatChildren.ts`) now use it.
- Tests: `useBrainConversation.test.tsx` adds "switching chats never answers the PREVIOUS chat's trailing user turn" and "no auto-reply to a trailing MID-TURN user row".
